# Phase 2 Pull Request 5: Tuning Evidence and OCR Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task by task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** A job's file phase runs spec 6.4's steps 10 and 10a, so spec 8.7's text rule and spec 8.6's audio rules decide with the OCR (optical character recognition) text and the compact audio proxy instead of holding on S32 or S33; the evidence lands in the two tuning trees that `retune` reads beside the phase 0 clone; and `lazymkvctl licenses` and `export-models`, the relayed `retune --jobs` and layer 2 of the tests arrive with it (design part 12.6 item 5 as the notes' B1 (scope) amends it). A UHD (Ultra HD Blu-ray) movie job with one English subtitle stream and a job with several run steps 10 and 10a and decide without holding on S32 or S33, the trial's verdict is recorded in `docs/phase2/ocr-trial.md`, and the pull request's test count and mini PC runs go into `docs/phase2/engine.md` as pull request 4's did.

**Architecture:**
- `core` gains the pure bitmap pipeline `core::subtitle::bitmap`: a small EBML (Extensible Binary Meta Language) reader of `evidence.mks` with the zlib inflater (`miniz_oxide`), the PGS (Presentation Graphic Stream) and VobSub decoders, the preparation and its distinct crop, the row line finder and its four triggers, the OCR evidence files with design 10.3's cross-check, and the fixed time cap. It also gains `core::audio::pass`, the port of `scripts/phase0/audio-levels.ps1`, and the note `subtitle_text_unread` with `SubtitleFacts`' unread streams. Nothing in `core` reads a file (RP19).
- Two new packages hold OCR. `lazymkv-ocr-models` embeds the two pinned ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange) models through a build script that reads `LAZYMKV_OCRS_MODELS` or, on CI (continuous integration) only, downloads them from their two pinned Amazon S3 (Simple Storage Service) URLs (uniform resource locators); it links no rten, so `lazymkvctl` can carry the models (E3). `lazymkv-ocr` (ocrs and rten) is the worker binary `lazymkv-ocr.exe`, the only program that links rten (A2, K1).
- `tools` gains the worker's driver `tools::ocr` (one function the engine and the trial both use, K2), `Spawn`'s working folder, and the extraction, packet-listing and `ffmpeg` drivers. `lazymkv-dev ocr-trial`, behind the cargo feature `ocr-trial`, runs design 10.9's trial through the same driver and the platform's native guard; the trial is a stop point before any engine OCR task.
- The engine runs steps 10, 10a and 11 as one unit: the worker reads each English or no-language bitmap stream in a local work folder under the data folder (B1 (the worker's folder)), step 10a decodes the audio in another, and every file crosses between the data folder, staging and `tuning_root` only through one size-checked copy (T5-R55). A complete staged tuning folder is skipped on a re-run (C3). After Decide, the dataset copy and the recordings refresh run outside the reducer, the copy's state lives in `state.json`, and only a pending copy holds a filed job's staging data (C2).
- `dev`'s `retune` reads several evidence folders (D1, D2); the relay carries `retune --jobs` and decide's `--text <tuning_root>\dataset`, fetching stale TMDb (The Movie Database) copies first (G2, G3); `lazymkvctl` makes retune's path flags absolute (V10), prints the licences and exports the models (E1 to E3). Layer 2 runs real `mkvmerge`, `ffprobe` and `ffmpeg` on the three CI runners (G1).

**Tech Stack:** Rust 1.99.0 (`rust-toolchain.toml`), edition 2021.
- New crates (A1; the binding list, each crate with its exact version, manifest licence and checksum, is the one Task 0 reads from crates.io for the owner's plan-time yes and Task 1 prints with the hand-written `Cargo.lock` delta for the second yes): `ocrs = "=0.13.1"` (default features off, only the features Task 0 reads from its feature table for the ONNX models, T5-R63), `rten = "=0.26.0"` (default features off) and rten's transitive crates (design part 4.7 names `rayon`, `rayon-core`, `rten-tensor`, `rten-imageproc`, `rten-base`, `rten-gemm`, `rten-parallel`, `rten-shape-inference`, `rten-simd`, `rten-vecmath`, `num_cpus`, `rustc-hash`, `smallvec`, `typeid`, and with the ONNX feature `rten-onnx` and `flatbuffers`), `rten-imageproc` as a direct dependency of `lazymkv-ocr` at the delta's exact version only if Task 0 finds that ocrs does not re-export the line rectangle types (T5-R63), `png` (with its deflate encoder), `sha2` (a normal and a build-dependency of `lazymkv-ocr-models`, a dev-dependency of `lazymkv-ctl`), and `miniz_oxide` resolved to the 0.8 line `png` pulls in, each caret. The models' build script reuses the workspace's one `ureq` 3.5.0 entry as a build-dependency. The notes' A1 estimates about 15 to 25 transitive crates; phase 0's `experiments/ocrs-trial/Cargo.lock` suggests about 40 to 45 (Task 0 Step 4 and Task 1 Step 7 tell the owner the real count).
- Tools used only on CI (P33; pinned at Task 0, T5-R28): `cargo-about`, MKVToolNix on the three runners, a static FFmpeg 7.x on ubuntu; GitHub's `actions/cache` and `actions/upload-artifact`.
- Nothing else new: no Matroska crate (design part 10.3), no image crate beyond `png`, no Tesseract build (B3).
- The build and test host: the mini PC, an Intel J4125 with 4 cores, 7.8 GB (gigabytes) of memory and a 119 GB SSD (solid-state drive), is the only Windows build host; every cargo command runs there through `scripts/box.sh`, and the Mac has no toolchain.

**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-phase-2-pr5-design-notes.md` (the notes: decisions A1 to G3, the planner's calls 1 to 26, sections 4 and 6), `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-21-phase-2-engine-design.md` (the design: parts 2.5, 3.5, 4.1, 4.5, 4.7, 5.2, 5.3, 5.7, 5.9, 5.10, 6.6, 7.1 to 7.7, 9.5, 9.6, 10.1 to 10.13, 11.1 to 11.5, 12.1 to 12.6; P3, P17 to P22, P26, P29, P31, P33, P34; K1, K2, K11, K14; R-A5, R-A6), `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-04-lazymkv-design.md` (the spec: 4.4, 6.4 steps 10, 10a and 11, 7, 8.7, 14, 15, 17 row 14), `docs/phase2/engine.md` (W24, W25, V10, S32, S33, S74, S80, T4-R7, T4-R9, owner item 22, "Left for later pull requests"), and `.superpowers/pr5/decisions.txt` (the owner's dated lines of 2026-11-06, which bind this plan). The notes use the id B1 twice; this plan cites them as B1 (scope), the split of section 2, and B1 (the worker's folder), the decision of section 3 (T5-R61). Requirement ids refer to `.superpowers/pr5/plan/req-R1-evidence.md` (R1-evidence-n), `req-R2-decoders.md` (R2-decoders-n), `req-R3-worker.md` (R3-worker-n), `req-R4-commands.md` (R4-commands-n), `req-R5-code.md` (R5-code-n) and `req-R6-phase0.md` (R6-phase0-n), whose lines cite the notes, the design and the code. The tasks were drafted from the git-ignored skeleton `.superpowers/pr5/plan/skeleton.md`, which fixed their order, interfaces, rulings, tests and requirement map; the planner notes at the end say where a task departs from it.

## Global Constraints

- **Toolchain and commands.** Rust 1.99.0 from `rust-toolchain.toml`; Dependabot pull request 8's 1.99.1 waits for its own yes. Every cargo command runs on the mini PC through `scripts/box.sh`, one at a time, with `--locked`, never while a real disc rips, a desktop-session job runs or a timed trial run runs (each call replaces `C:\lazymkv\src`). A second session that only watches the mini PC (call 4's memory sampler, the A3 hash checks) uses plain `ssh`, never `scripts/box.sh`; the sampler runs beside a build only with the owner's `watcher` yes (owner item 33, Task 0 Step 1), and without it no sampler starts. The Mac has no toolchain.
- **The workspace run.** A task's Run is its targeted command; before its commit it runs `scripts/box.sh cargo test --workspace --locked` once (expected `0 failed` in every `test result:` line). Tasks 2, 10, 14, 15, 16, 17, 18, 21 and 22 run the junction form instead, since the goldens and the RP21 guard run only there and each of them changes a reader the goldens use or a folder under `corpus/scenarios/`: `scripts/box.sh "(if not exist corpus mkdir corpus)&& mklink /J corpus\owner C:\lazymkv\evidence\owner&& set LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE=C:\lazymkv\evidence\owner&& cargo test --workspace --locked"`. A golden that changes stops the task and goes to the owner (K5).
- **Line numbers** are as of `07ccc48`; a task that runs after another that edits the same file finds the named item where it then is. A filter matches test paths (module path and function name); `--test <stem>` names an integration-test file of the crate given with `-p`.
- **Models (A3, calls 2 and 3).** `text-detection.onnx`, 2,499,479 bytes, SHA-1 (Secure Hash Algorithm 1) `709176816006063da8155f549aa0e44735ed0e9c`, from `https://ocrs-models.s3-accelerate.amazonaws.com/text-detection.onnx`; `text-recognition.onnx`, 9,713,177 bytes, SHA-1 `b16f361df884a9afaa067e4d6932567f6f652a81`, from `https://ocrs-models.s3-accelerate.amazonaws.com/text-recognition.onnx`; 12,212,656 bytes together; licence CC-BY-SA-4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0). The two SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm 256) pins are Task 1's `A3 pins` lines in `.superpowers/pr5/decisions.txt`. The build script reads `LAZYMKV_OCRS_MODELS` first; `scripts/box.sh` sets it to `C:\lazymkv\phase0\models`; CI passes its cache folder; the build script downloads only when the variable is unset, which happens only in CI's `models` job on a cache miss (T5-R41). No run-time code fetches a model.
- **Dependencies.** Task 1 makes every `Cargo.toml` dependency change of this plan (pins, the two packages, every path edge, dev's feature, the dev- and build-dependencies) and fetches only after the owner's second yes; no later task edits a dependency list. Before that yes the plan writer checks the code and test imports of Tasks 7 to 24 against Task 1's lists (a temporary folder in `lazymkv-ocr-models`' tests is `std::env::temp_dir()` with a per-test name, never another crate's helper), and any missing edge is added in Task 1. No `scripts/box.sh` call runs between the hand edit of `Cargo.lock` and the second yes; the hand-written lock is checked on the Mac only. After the first fetch, `Cargo.lock` equals the approved hand-written delta (`cmp` against `.superpowers/pr5/Cargo.lock.approved`).
- **rten out of every program (A2, E3, K1, call 23).** Only `lazymkv-ocr` links rten and ocrs; `lazymkvctl` links `lazymkv-ocr-models` only; `lazymkv-dev` links `lazymkv-ocr` only with `--features ocr-trial`; the engine reaches OCR only by starting `lazymkv-ocr.exe`. CI's ubuntu job checks it with `cargo tree -p <package> -e normal -i rten --locked` for `lazymkv-ctl`, `lazymkv-engine` and `lazymkv-dev`, each printing no line that starts with `rten`.
- **The CI matrix (call 23).** A `models` job on ubuntu fills the model cache once per cache miss (T5-R41); the three matrix jobs `needs: models`. ubuntu-latest builds and tests the whole workspace and runs the worker, the run's one rten build (T5-R52); macos-latest and windows-latest run `cargo build --workspace --exclude lazymkv-ocr --locked` and `cargo test --workspace --exclude lazymkv-ocr --locked`; all three restore the model cache (they build `lazymkv-ocr-models` through `lazymkv-ctl`).
- **No network beyond the notes.** No non-ignored test contacts any host but `127.0.0.1`. CI's only new network is the `models` job's download on a cache miss from the two pinned URLs (uniform resource locators) and Task 0's pinned installs (MKVToolNix, the static FFmpeg 7.x, `cargo-about`); Task 7's push checks that CodeQL's default setup does not run the models' build script.
- **No I/O in core (RP19).** `core::subtitle::bitmap` and `core::audio::pass` are pure functions of bytes and text; `core::testsupport::mks` builds bytes only.
- **RP21 and the trial's tracks.** No file under `crates/`, `corpus/scenarios/` or `scripts/` holds a byte copy of, or a value read only from, `corpus/owner` or the tuning dataset. Test bitmaps are made-up block shapes, with no glyph and no font; tests of several evidence folders build them from made-up values; clone-reading tests skip without `LAZYMKV_EVIDENCE`. The goldens and the trial read the share only in the desktop session and name the six tracks only through design 10.9's table and the git-ignored `C:\lazymkv\phase0\trial-tracks.txt` (T5-R45). Nobody reads or writes `corpus/owner` except the junction runs' read-only goldens, the live-record replay and the owner (the notes' section 4); on the mini PC the evidence mirror `C:\lazymkv\evidence\owner` is read only by the junction runs, by Task 25's replay stand-in (Step 9) and by its `retune --jobs --evidence` run (Step 14).
- **The trial's build (T5-R54; design 10.6, 10.9 "One trial", K2).** The trial runs once, on Task 11's pushed and green commit, checked clean before Task 12 builds it and recorded in `docs/phase2/ocr-trial.md` and the evidence line. From that commit on, no task edits `crates/core/src/subtitle/bitmap/`, `crates/ocr/`, `crates/ocr-models/`, `crates/tools/src/ocr.rs`, `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`; a change there goes to the owner, and design 10.6 makes it a new trial. Task 25 checks it with `git diff --exit-code`.
- **Fixtures and `.gitignore`.** `.gitignore` ignores `*.ocr.jsonl`, so no fixture is named so: a stand-in worker's records are `records-s<n>.txt` in its scenario, which the stand-in creates as `sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl`; made-up record lines hold only sentinel words such as `text-sentinel-3e8f`.
- **Where text lives (design 10.12).** OCR text and crops are written only to `<data>\work\ocr-<job id>-<title key>\` while a worker runs, to `<staging>\<job id>\tuning\<title key>\subs-ocr\` and to `<tuning_root>\dataset\<job id>\<title key>\subs-ocr\`; the worker's capture (its standard error can hold text, T5-R57) is written only to the work folder and deleted with it; neither is ever written to `%ProgramData%\lazymkv\jobs\`, a `decide.json`, `state.json`, `job.log`, `engine.log`, a note's detail, a notification, the IPC (inter-process communication) snapshot, `<tuning_root>\recordings\`, a test's printed output or the repository.
- **Unchanged output.** The goldens stay byte-identical (K5); `decide`'s output for every recording without an unread stream is unchanged; `retune`'s single-folder output is unchanged for every existing test; `state.json` without a tuning copy reads and writes byte-identical.
- **Persisted files.** Engine-written job-folder files go through `lazymkv_platform::write_atomic` (it creates no folder; each step makes its folders first); `state.json` keeps `lazymkv job v1`; lookup answers stay `serde_json::to_vec_pretty` plus a final `\n`; every copy between the data folder, staging and `tuning_root` goes through `staged::copy_checked` (`<name>.partial` flushed with `sync_all`, a size check against the source, a rename), a move is that copy and then the source deleted (T5-R55), and a copy into the job folder is `staged::copy_into_job` (the bytes read, their count checked against the source's size, then `write_atomic`); level series files are UTF-8 (the Unicode byte encoding) without a BOM (byte order mark) with CRLF (carriage return and line feed) line ends on every system (T5-R19).
- **Fixed values (spec 14, never settings).** The time cap `max(60, 2.03 x events)` seconds; `RTEN_NUM_THREADS=3`; the worker's command line `lazymkv-ocr <evidence.mks> --stream N --clear-max BYTES --out DIR`, exit 0 read, 2 argument error, 3 the stream refused with the reason on standard error; ink level 127, a gap of 2 rows, 16-pixel padding, factor 1.6, 3 lines, the video frame's middle row; grey `255 - round(Y * alpha / 255)` composited onto white; the proxy FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec) 8000 Hz, 24 bits, mono, compression level 5, `gain_db` -18 then -30 (dB, decibels), a clip at or above -0.1 dBFS (decibels relative to full scale); `sub_clear_max_bytes` from the job's own settings (default 64, "larger than" is an event), the same value for the worker, the cross-check and the text rule (T5-R59).
- **Names.** The note `subtitle_text_unread` with the detail `stream {n} was not read: {reason}`, the reason `time cap of {s} s reached after {k} of {m} events` or the error; `tuning_evidence_pending`; the paths `<staging>\<job id>\evidence\<title key>.mks`, `<staging>\<job id>\tuning\<title key>\`, `<data>\work\`, `<data>\work\ocr-<job id>-<title key>\s<n>.capture.txt`, `<tuning_root>\recordings\<job id>\`, `<tuning_root>\dataset\<job id>\<title key>\`.
- **Secrets and names.** No secret, webhook ID (identifier), title of the owner's disc, job ID, host, Windows user name, account SID (security identifier) or drive serial in the repository, a test, a commit message or a mini PC evidence line; the placeholders are `<job id>`, `<film folder>`, `<title>`, `<share>`, `<tuning dataset>`, `<slug>`, `<label>`; mini PC lines name the trial's tracks by row number only.
- **Docs and prose.** Every `pub` item has a `///` doc naming its spec section, design part, notes decision or ruling and ending "Def: T5-<n>. Use: T5-<m>."; prose is plain sentences, no em-dashes or en-dashes, acronyms expanded at first use; the notes' two B1 decisions are cited as "B1 (scope)" and "B1 (the worker's folder)" (T5-R61); expected multi-line texts in tests are arrays joined with `"\n"`. From Task 2 on, every commit step runs the Def/Use check `perl .superpowers/pr5/pub-docs.pl 07ccc48` (Task 0 Step 10) after its `git add` and before its `git commit`: it must print `<k> new pub items, 0 without a Def/Use doc` and exit 0; a `<file>:<line>: <kind> <name>` line it prints is fixed, staged and checked again before the commit, so no missing doc reaches T5-R54's frozen paths (Task 11 Step 14 is the last commit before they freeze).
- **Tests.** Tests go in the file's `mod tests` or a sibling `tests.rs`, named as snake_case sentences; tests that run `fake-tool` live in `crates/fake-tools/tests/` (S12); waits that only wait scale by `ci_factor()` (4 with `CI` set, else 1), and a bound that proves a kill or a give-up does not; a test whose input is missing prints `skipped: <reason>` and passes, and the notes count it as not run; layer 2 finds tools through `LAZYMKV_TEST_MKVMERGE`, `LAZYMKV_TEST_FFPROBE` and `LAZYMKV_TEST_FFMPEG`, else `PATH`, and skips below FFmpeg 7.0 (K11); Task 13's ffprobe cross-check skips only without ffprobe.
- **CodeQL.** The draft's CodeQL result shows 0 alerts after each push; an alert is a red run.
- **The mini PC and the Mac.** Nothing is installed on either. No scheduled task is registered or re-registered except by `scripts/engine-task.ps1 -AcceptWritableBuild` after a release build, with the owner's yes (Task 25). The engine task `lazymkv-engine` is stopped with `lazymkvctl stop` for the trial and the heavy run. Every mini PC evidence line goes first to the git-ignored `.superpowers/pr5/pr5-mini-pc-runs.txt` in engine.md's form. A build that runs the mini PC short of memory is retried with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2` and its peak recorded (call 4).
- **TDD (test-driven development) cycle per task.** Write the listed tests; Run and see the named failure (a compile error or FAIL); implement; Run for PASS; the workspace run once; commit; push.
- **Commits.** One signed commit per task, no attribution line, author and committer `krcm0209 <17315774+krcm0209@users.noreply.github.com>`; `git log -1 --format='%G? %an <%ae> %cn <%ce>%n%B'` shows `G` and that identity. From Task 1's push on, each commit is pushed to the draft pull request; CI green on ubuntu, macos and windows and CodeQL at 0 before the next task starts. A red run or an alert after a task's push is fixed by a new signed commit on the branch, subject `<area>: <what> (fix)`, never by an amend or a force push; Tasks 0 and 25 commit nothing, and Task 26 carries their evidence.
- **Stop points.** A model hash difference (Task 1, A3), a `Cargo.lock` that the first build after the yes finds wrong (Task 1: a renewed A1 yes before the corrected build), CodeQL's extraction running the models' build script (Task 7), any golden fail, unpaired count or size mismatch (Task 11, call 24), any trial fail (Task 12, B3, whose verdict file is still committed), a runner's ffprobe that lists sizes other than the reader's (Task 13, call 24) and any byte difference of the level series (Task 25, call 9) stop the pull request and go to the owner with the numbers; no check is weakened to pass (the size check never falls back to count and order alone).
- **The notes' section 4** (the constraints the plan inherits) binds as written in the notes; the lines above apply it task by task.

## Review Focus

The five input classes or failure modes the notes and design imply that the tasks' main tests do not reach, most likely to bite the owner. Each line names the task whose tests now pin it; every test named is written out in that task's text.

1. **`tuning_root` drops or fills while files land** (the share goes away mid-copy, a full share, a `.partial` left by a lost connection, a restart with a copy pending). Task 19: `a_partial_left_by_a_lost_share_is_replaced_and_the_copy_lands_at_the_next_reach` (a `.partial` of another size waits in the dataset; the next reach replaces it; `tuning_copy` goes from `pending` to `done`; one `tuning evidence copied to tuning_root` line, every earlier line a `tuning copy` line), `a_copy_whose_size_differs_after_the_write_stays_pending_and_keeps_the_staging_data` (a fault seam shortens the written file; no rename; `retention_due` is false), `a_full_tuning_root_leaves_the_copy_pending_with_the_note_and_the_decision_unchanged` and, for the restart with a copy pending, `a_pending_copy_is_retried_at_engine_start_and_only_copies`.
2. **The worker misbehaves** (a panic with text on standard error, a kill in the middle of a record, more records than events). Task 15: `a_worker_that_panics_leaves_the_stream_unread_with_its_exit_code_and_no_stderr_text` (the stand-in writes `text-sentinel-3e8f` to standard error and exits 101; the detail is `stream <s> was not read: lazymkv-ocr exited with code 101`; the sentinel is in no file under `jobs\`, nor in `engine.log` or the IPC snapshot, and no capture file is under `jobs\`), `a_killed_worker_with_a_torn_last_record_counts_only_whole_records` (3 whole records and a torn fourth over 10 events, the harness's cap override `c`: `time cap of <c> s reached after 3 of 10 events`, T5-R58) and `a_worker_that_writes_more_records_than_events_is_unread_by_the_cross_check`.
3. **The unit is interrupted** (a stop or crash during a worker run, during the move into the staged folder, or during step 10a's copies). Task 18: `a_restart_after_a_torn_move_deletes_the_staged_folder_and_reads_again` (the staged folder holds `sub-0.ocr.jsonl` and no `summary.json`; after the restart the worker ran again and the folder is complete) and `an_incomplete_staged_folder_is_deleted_and_both_steps_run_again` (the staged level folder without its own `audio-proxy.json`, as a stop during step 10a's copies leaves it); Task 15: `engine_start_removes_a_leftover_work_folder` and `a_stop_during_a_worker_run_kills_it_and_leaves_no_work_folder`.
4. **mkvmerge-written Matroska beyond the minimal shape** (EBML Void and CRC-32 (cyclic redundancy check) elements, clusters of unknown size, Cues, Tags and Attachments around the clusters, block groups with a duration, a negative relative block time). Task 3: `the_reader_skips_void_and_crc_elements_and_reads_unknown_size_clusters`, `cues_tags_and_attachments_around_the_clusters_are_skipped` (with `ATTACHMENT_TRAP`'s fake block bytes inside an attachment), `a_block_group_with_a_duration_reads_as_its_block` and `a_negative_relative_timestamp_is_the_cluster_time_minus_it` (through `MksBlock.cluster_ms`).
5. **Level-series formatting at its edges** (`-inf`, `nan`, values below -100, halves, values that round to zero, 15-digit inputs, a raw file with CRLF line ends and a blank last line), which decides the byte-for-byte check of call 9. Task 16: `net_fixed1_matches_dotnet_framework_on_the_edge_values` (the expected strings read once from Windows PowerShell 5.1 on the mini PC, Task 16 Step 1) and `a_raw_file_with_crlf_and_a_trailing_blank_line_gives_the_same_series`.

## Rulings this plan makes

The notes leave these open or two sources disagree; the plan settles each as below, and Task 0 Step 1 asks the owner whether any is overturned (an overturn reopens the named task before it starts). Each ruling goes into engine.md at Task 26. T5-R64 was added when the plan was assembled, to settle what Tasks 13 and 24 do on CI, and T5-R65 at the plan's review, to settle where the self-test's minimum versions go.

- **T5-R1** (R2-decoders-4, R3-worker-3, R4-commands-15, R4-commands-68). The `ocr` crate is call 23's two packages; the models' build script belongs to `lazymkv-ocr-models`; engine.md's crates table records the split, and Task 26 amends design 4.1, 4.7 and 10.11 for it (T5-R50).
- **T5-R2** (R3-worker-4, R4-commands-11). `lazymkvctl` links `lazymkv-ocr-models` only (E3 binds over spec 4.4's "compiled into `lazymkvctl.exe`" and design 11.1's ocrs row); Task 12 rewords spec 4.4's ocrs row and Task 26 design 11.1's.
- **T5-R3** (R2-decoders-45, R6-phase0-10, R6-phase0-29). `--stream N` is ffprobe's subtitle-relative index, counted from 0 over the evidence file's subtitle tracks in track order, the `n` of `subs\sub-<n>.packets.json`; the worker maps it to the n-th track of type subtitle (17).
- **T5-R4** (R2-decoders-50, R3-worker-17 to 19, R5-code-41). `--out` names the local folder `<data>\work\ocr-<job id>-<title key>\s<n>\`, outside `jobs\` (B1 (the worker's folder) amends design 10.2 step 3). The engine copies `<staging>\<job id>\evidence\<title key>.mks` to `<data>\work\ocr-<job id>-<title key>\evidence.mks` before the title's first run, moves each stream's output into the staged `subs-ocr\` after its run (both through T5-R55's checked copy), deletes a killed run's `s<n>\` and the whole title folder after the last stream, and deletes `<data>\work\` at engine start.
- **T5-R5** (R2-decoders-26). A VobSub alpha of 0 to 15 maps to `alpha * 17` (0 to 255); Task 11's VobSub golden checks it.
- **T5-R6** (R2-decoders-31). The prepared event is composited onto a white canvas of the video frame (the PGS composition's size, the VobSub idx frame size), and the crop's 16-pixel growth is clamped to that canvas, as phase 0's crop trial clamped to the rendered frame; Task 11's goldens check the result.
- **T5-R7** (design 10.6's triggers 1 and 2). A run is a maximal block of contiguous inked rows; a line is a maximal group of runs joined across a single empty row (2 or more empty rows separate lines); trigger 1 holds when a run is taller than 1.6 times the median, trigger 2 when a line is; the median is over the line heights of the stream's events with one or two lines, and without such an event neither trigger holds.
- **T5-R8** (R3-worker-5). Worker exit 3 leaves the stream unread with the first line of its standard error as the reason; exit 2 fails the step (`DecisionFailed { Unknown }`, `lazymkv-ocr refused its arguments: <line>`), an engine bug; any other code (101 is a panic) leaves the stream unread with `lazymkv-ocr exited with code <c>` and quotes no standard error; a run that ends with no exit code leaves it unread with `lazymkv-ocr ended without an exit code`; a worker that is not beside the engine fails the step with `OCR_MISSING` (`lazymkv-ocr is not beside the engine, so step 10 cannot read subtitles`).
- **T5-R9** (R3-worker-24). `{s}` is the cap in seconds with one decimal (`1800.6` for 887 events, `60.0` at the floor); `{k}` counts the whole lines of the killed run's `sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl` (a torn last line does not count), read before its folder is deleted; `{n}` is the scan stream number, as `Noted.stream`.
- **T5-R10** (R3-worker-60). The cap stays fixed: the engine and `lazymkv-dev ocr-trial read` always compute it with `time_cap_s(events)`; the seams tests set short are `tools::ocr::run_worker`'s `cap` parameter and `read_streams`' `cap` function (T5-R58), and neither is a setting.
- **T5-R11** (R2-decoders-47, R3-worker-15, R6-phase0-14). A text subtitle stream (`text::is_text_codec`) is never given to the worker and gets no note (set aside, spec 8.7); every English or no-language stream (`eng`, `en`, `und` or none) of any other codec goes to the worker, which refuses a codec other than `S_HDMV/PGS` and `S_VOBSUB` with exit 3 naming it.
- **T5-R12** (R1-evidence-30). `subs-ocr\summary.json` is written into the job folder's `<title key>\subs-ocr\` through `write_atomic` and copied into the staged `subs-ocr\` through `copy_checked`, the staged one last, after every stream's output has moved; C3 reads the staged one.
- **T5-R13** (R1-evidence-26, R1-evidence-31, R6-phase0-61). In the staged folder step 10a writes, in order, the level folder's files, `audio-proxy.mka` when kept, the `audio-proxy.json` beside it, and last the level folder's own `audio-proxy.json`, which is C3's marker; the job folder's level folder gets its `audio-proxy.json` only when the dataset copy lands (design 7.5).
- **T5-R14** (R1-evidence-32, R1-evidence-33, R1-evidence-53, R4-commands-43). `JobRecord` gains `tuning_copy: Option<TuningCopy>` (`pending`, `done`; absent when no copy is owed). It becomes `pending` when the unit's Decide feeds `DecisionDone` for a job whose own settings keep tuning evidence, `done` when every file has landed, and absent again when an attempt finds that none of the job's titles has a staged tuning folder while the staging share answers (C2: nothing is owed, `CopyEnd::Nothing`). `TuningEvidencePending` is added only when a copy attempt finds `tuning_root` unreachable or short of space (spec 7's words) and stays after the copy lands. The cleanup and the relay read `tuning_copy`, never the note; "the job's dataset copy exists" means `tuning_copy == Some(TuningCopy::Done)`.
- **T5-R15** (R1-evidence-41). The recordings refresh never writes or deletes `notes.md`, `audio-labels.json` or `subtitle-labels.json` (design 7.1's three owner files).
- **T5-R16** (call 11). The refresh keeps `.lazymkv-refresh.json` in `<tuning_root>\recordings\<job id>\`, naming each file it wrote with its size and modification time; those are "its own earlier copies"; it deletes only a TMDb (The Movie Database) copy listed there that the job folder no longer holds. An orphan's copy fetched by a relayed `retune` (T5-R60) is never listed there.
- **T5-R17** (R1-evidence-54, R6-phase0-75). An `audio-proxy.json` that kept no proxy has `"proxy": null`, `"gains_tried": [-18, -30]` and `encoding.gain_db` -30; `retune` leaves a title out of the dataset only when a level folder's `audio-proxy.json` parses and holds `"proxy": null` (`AudioProxy::kept_no_proxy`); a file without the key, as phase 0's and the existing tests' files are, counts as before (Task 16); design 7.5's sentence is amended (Task 26).
- **T5-R18** (R6-phase0-74). The byte-for-byte check compares each series file whole, header included; the replay keeps phase 0's rip file name, so `file=` matches; a difference of name or value goes to the owner.
- **T5-R19** (R6-phase0-56). Series files are UTF-8 without a BOM with CRLF line ends on every system; `net_fixed1` reproduces the .NET Framework `0.0` format (the parsed double to 15 significant digits, then half away from zero), with a value that rounds to zero printed as Windows PowerShell 5.1 prints it; Task 16 reads the edge values' strings once on the mini PC.
- **T5-R20** (R6-phase0-73). `sub-<n>.frames.json`'s `markers` keep phase 0's five keys `bracket`, `note`, `hash`, `speaker`, `upper` with `Count-Markers`' expressions ported (`scripts/phase0/ocr-subs.ps1` lines 58 to 74); `summary.json` gives their per-stream sums; design 10.12's "the text rule's markers" is read so.
- **T5-R21** (R6-phase0-76). A crop is `s<n>\f-<pts in milliseconds, zero-padded to 9 digits>.png`, so name order is `pts` (presentation timestamp) order.
- **T5-R22** (R2-decoders-57). The goldens pair events and frames as `text::pair_text` does; an unpaired event or frame is counted and reported, not failed, and any unpaired count goes to the owner with the numbers before the trial.
- **T5-R23** (R2-decoders-60). A golden difference above 2 grey levels is a finding for the owner; the tolerance stays 2 (call 7).
- **T5-R24** (R3-worker-45, R6-phase0-18, R6-phase0-20, R6-phase0-71, R6-phase0-78). B2 amends design 10.9 step 1 for its four inputs. A track missing its frame set takes an existing `ocrs-s<n>.jsonl` as arm F when one exists (row 2) and reports R' as not run; with neither frames nor an F reading, parity cannot be judged on it and the trial stops and goes to the owner. The proof of concept's readings may lack `pts` and `lines`: `FrameEntry.t` and `FrameEntry.pts` are both `Option<f64>`, `f-records` writes `t` alone for a frame without `pts` (the text rule then pairs by the proof of concept's rule of R6-phase0-18), and a frame with neither stops the trial at B2; `inventory` finds `evidence.mks` in the dataset copy, else at the staging path `summary.json` names under `evidence`, else at `$Staging\<slug>\<label>\evidence.mks` (R6-phase0-20).

K11's skip below FFmpeg 7.0 stays as the rule for a machine without a new enough copy; CI's ubuntu runner gets the static 7.x and does not skip; windows installs MKVToolNix with its installer (call 20 over design 12.1's package managers).
- **T5-R50** (A2, B1 (scope), B1 (the worker's folder), C1, E1, E3, calls 20, 22 and 23). Task 26 amends the design in place, each change marked with the notes' id: part 4.1's sentence on `dev` and `ocr` (A2) and its one-package `ocr` row (call 23); part 4.7's "`ocr`'s build script" (call 23) and its notices generated on the release runner (E1); part 10.11's "The `ocr` crate's `build.rs`" (call 23); part 11.1's ocrs row, "compiled into `lazymkv-ocr.exe` and `lazymkvctl.exe`, with both models embedded" (E3); part 11.4's "the release job generates the crate notices" (E1); parts 3.5 and 6.6's lists of the data folder, which gain `<data>\work\` (B1 (the worker's folder)); part 7.5's sentence on `audio-proxy.json` (call 22) and its sentence on where step 10a's pass and the OCR write (B1 (the worker's folder)); part 10.2 step 3 and part 10.7's output folder (B1 (the worker's folder)); part 12.1's ubuntu sentence (call 20); part 12.6's numbering (B1 (scope)).
- **T5-R51** (R2-decoders-63, design 10.8, spec 8.7). `text::subs_run` gains `unread: &[(i64, String)]` (the `n` and `why` of `summary.json`'s unread streams); when it is not empty, before its two checks for missing text, it writes one line `stream s{n} {tag}: not read by the engine: {why}` per unread stream and returns refused, so a title with an unread stream gets that Skipped subtitles section and its text adds no review; with `unread` empty its output is unchanged, and phase 0's hint "read it with ocr-subs.ps1" stays for a stream without text that no `summary.json` marks unread (the golden `a_subs_run_with_an_english_stream_without_text_gives_no_subs_golden` unchanged). `retune --subtitles`' row 14 harness reads a labelled unread stream as it reads any labelled stream without text today ("Labels that cannot be judged:", the folder's code 3), and a several-folder run's code is then D1's worst.
- **T5-R52** (R4-commands-23, F1). F1's "one rten build" is one per CI run, in the ubuntu job, with no build cache; "cached by the models' SHA-256 values" qualifies the model download. The `ocr-trial` build of Task 10 reuses that job's rten.
- **T5-R53** (G2, call 12). The TEXTDIR half of `--evidence DIR=TEXTDIR` is read only with `--subtitles` and ignored otherwise, so the relay's `--evidence <tuning_root>\recordings=<tuning_root>\dataset` serves the audio harness unchanged; `--evidence DIR=TEXTDIR` given with `--text` exits 2 with `argument --text: not with --evidence DIR=TEXTDIR, which names the text already`, so a relayed `retune --jobs --subtitles --text X` exits 2 and the owner gives `--evidence DIR=TEXTDIR` instead.
- **T5-R54** (R3-worker-54, R6-phase0-37, design 10.6 and 10.9 "One trial", K2, B3). The trial's build is Task 11's pushed commit with CI green and CodeQL at 0, checked clean before Task 12's build and recorded in `docs/phase2/ocr-trial.md` and the evidence line. From it on no task edits `crates/core/src/subtitle/bitmap/`, `crates/ocr/`, `crates/ocr-models/`, `crates/tools/src/ocr.rs`, `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`; a change there goes to the owner and reopens the trial. Task 9 writes `run_worker`'s `Spawn` with `..Spawn::default()` so Task 13's new field leaves `crates/tools/src/ocr.rs` untouched. On a FAIL, Task 12 still commits `ocr-trial.md` with its numbers and pushes it, and the pull request stops (B3).
- **T5-R55** (B1 (the worker's folder), design 7.5's EVID-4 discipline). The data folder, staging and `tuning_root` are different volumes, so a rename between them fails: every copy between them is `staged::copy_checked` (copy to `<to>.partial`, flushed with `sync_all`, its size against the source's, rename to `<to>`), and the "moves" of B1 (the worker's folder) are `staged::move_checked` (that copy, then the source deleted); a copy whose target is in the job folder is `staged::copy_into_job` (the source's bytes, their count checked, then `write_atomic`), so every engine-written job-folder file goes through `write_atomic` (R5-code-30). A unit test reads the unit's sources and finds no other `fs::rename` or `fs::copy`.
- **T5-R56** (design 5.6 step 6, review round 1 of pull request 3, V5). Steps 10 and 10a return `staged::UnitError`: `Failed(String)` (a tool, decode or argument failure) feeds `DecisionFailed { Unknown }` with its sentence; `Staging(String)` (a write error on the staging share) is classed by `staging_write_failure(self.staging_health())`, so the job waits as AwaitingShare or AwaitingSpace, never Unknown.
- **T5-R57** (design 5.3 "Recording", 7.1, 10.12 item 3; R3-worker-40, R1-evidence-22). The worker's run is recorded capture-style at `<data>\work\ocr-<job id>-<title key>\s<n>.capture.txt` with its `.stderr`, `.timing.jsonl` and `.exit.json`; exit 3's reason is the first line of the `.stderr` file, read before the folder is deleted; no capture file reaches the job folder (design 7.1 has no row for it, and a panic's standard error can hold text); the run's exit code and wall time are kept in `summary.json` and its `job.log` line. Step 10a's setting-on pass keeps phase 0's `ffmpeg.txt` in its level folder; the setting-off streamhash pass runs in `<data>\work\levels-<job id>-<title key>\` too, and its capture is copied into the job folder's `<title key>\` as `streamhash-ffmpeg.txt` with its three siblings, beside `streamhash.txt`.
- **T5-R58** (R3-worker-21, R3-worker-60, design 10.8). `step10::read_streams` takes `cap: &dyn Fn(usize) -> Duration`; `RealSteps` fills it with `time_cap_s` unless `EngineConfig.ocr_cap_override` is set, which only the testkit harness sets, as it sets `limits_override`; it has no settings key and the native main passes None. The engine's kill tests set it to 2 s times `ci_factor()` (a wait for the stand-in to write its records, so it scales) and pin the detail with that value.
- **T5-R59** (R3-worker-6, R2-decoders-12). `dev::cmd::decide::subtitle_section` takes `clear_max: i64`; `lazymkv-dev decide` passes `TextRule::default().CLEAR_MAX_BYTES` and the engine the job's `sub_clear_max_bytes`, the value the worker and `check_events` take, so the text rule's events and the worker's records agree for any value.
- **T5-R60** (call 25). An orphan's copy fetched by a relayed `retune` is written into `<tuning_root>\recordings\<job id>\` as `serde_json::to_vec_pretty` plus a final `\n`, through `<name>.partial`, a size check against the bytes and a rename; it is that copy's only home.
- **T5-R61** (the notes' two B1s). They are cited as "B1 (scope)" and "B1 (the worker's folder)" in the code's docs, engine.md's rulings and the design's amendment marks.
- **T5-R62** (K2, R3-worker-47, R6-phase0-28). Arm R starts the worker through `ocr_trial::read_with`, which the binary calls with `lazymkv_platform::native_guard()` (`JobProcessGuard` on the mini PC), so it runs below normal with the engine's cleared environment plus `RTEN_NUM_THREADS=3`, exactly as the engine starts it; arm R' runs in-process with `RTEN_NUM_THREADS=3` set by the script; the evidence line records both.
- **T5-R63** (call 1, R2-decoders-41, R3-worker-8). Task 0 reads ocrs 0.13.1's feature table and public re-exports (metadata and published documentation only, Ruling T3-1-a): the features that load the `.onnx` models (call 1's "only the feature ocrs needs", which phase 0 built as `onnx` and `rten`) and whether the rectangle and point types `OcrEngine::recognize_text` takes are re-exported. If they are not, `lazymkv-ocr` takes `rten-imageproc` as a direct dependency pinned to the delta's exact version, so the lock keeps one entry; Task 1's manifest and both owner sentences name it.
- **T5-R64** (R2-decoders-17, R4-commands-27, R4-commands-29; call 20, T5-R49). With `CI` set, as GitHub Actions sets it, a layer 2 test whose tool is missing or whose FFmpeg or ffprobe is below 7.0 fails with `layer 2 must run on CI (call 20, T5-R49): <reason>` (Task 24), and Task 13's ffprobe cross-check fails with `CI has no ffprobe, so call 24's cross-check cannot run on this runner`, instead of printing `skipped:`, since cargo hides a passing test's output and a skip on CI would hide that the check never ran; every runner installs the tools. Off CI, design 12.1's skip and K11's rule below FFmpeg 7.0 stand (the mini PC, a developer's machine). This narrows design 12.1's "a test whose tool is missing prints skipped and passes" for CI only; Task 26 records it in engine.md. Tasks 13, 24.
- **T5-R65** (engine.md's S80, design part 12.1, G1; Task 26). The self-test's judging of spec 13's minimum versions of MKVToolNix and FFmpeg moves to pull request 6, with the release's FFmpeg build; layer 2 checks FFmpeg 7.0 in its tests only (Task 24, K11, T5-R64), and the self-test keeps printing each tool's version and path as at `07ccc48`. Task 26 amends S80's sentence in engine.md, which put those minimums with layer 2 in pull request 5, and lists the check under pull request 6 in "Left for later pull requests".

## Interface sheet

The names and signatures each task produces for later tasks, by task, used exactly as written (the task's own Interfaces block gives each item's doc, its `Def`/`Use` line and the texts it pins; the `///` doc lines are left out here). Every item compiles and is tested on all three systems unless its task says otherwise (`lazymkv-ocr` builds and runs on ubuntu and the mini PC only, call 23). Where a task's draft and the skeleton differed, the producing task's form is the one used throughout the plan: `MksBlock::new` and `MksBlock.cluster_ms` (Task 3); `Detected` and `open_stream` (Task 8); `run_recorded_in` re-exported at `lazymkv_tools`' root (Task 9); `read_with`'s `err` and `read`'s `--packets` (Task 10); `extract_args` over `&[i64]` (Task 13); `parse_layouts` and `proxy_check` returning `Result` (Task 16); `CopyEnd`, `Msg::TuningCopied { job, retry, end }` and `Harness::tuning(&self) -> &Path` (Task 19).

The script `scripts/phase0/engine-ocr-trial.ps1 -Step inventory|read|rows|compare|f3 [-Row <k>] [-Slug <slug>] [-Label <label>] [-Stream <n>] [-Evidence <dir>]`, started through `scripts/phase0/job.sh`: `-Row` (1 to 6) is required for every step but `f3`; the row's slug, label and stream are read from `trial-tracks.txt`, and a `-Slug`, `-Label` or `-Stream` given (Task 12 gives them) must equal that line's, else the run stops; the log names rows, never a slug or a label; `compare -Row <k>` compares every row of row k's title and is refused for a row that is not its title's first (rows 4 and 5 run as `-Row 4`); `f3` is Task 12 Step 10's report. Its last line is `RESULT ok` or `RESULT FAILED: <reason>`.

---

## Tasks

Each task gives its model tier and risk, the requirement ids it covers, its files, its interfaces, and numbered checkbox steps: the failing tests as code, their Run and expected failure, the implementation with its signatures and pinned values, the Run and pass line, the workspace run, the commit and the push. Every commit is checked with `git log -1 --format='%G? %an <%ae> %cn <%ce>%n%B'` (`G`, the noreply identity, no attribution line), and from Task 1's push on CI is green on ubuntu, macos and windows and CodeQL at 0 before the next task starts.

The order is call 21's, with three placements it implies: Task 2 lands the note in `core` before any decoder, as call 17 asks; Task 9's worker driver comes before the trial because arm R starts the worker through the engine's own driver (K2: the trial measures what ships); and Task 13's extraction, packet and ffmpeg drivers, which only steps 10 and 10a use, come after the trial and before step 10 (T5-R26). Tasks 0, 12 and 25 are the controller's with the owner; Task 11's pushed commit is the trial's build, frozen from then on (T5-R54).

### Task 0: The plan-time answers, the crate and tool pins, and the baseline (A1, T5-R28, T5-R63; owner and controller, manual)

**Tier and risk:** the controller (opus); risk medium: a wrong pin costs a second owner round, and a no stops the plan before the branch.
**Covers:** R4-commands-5, 6, 7, 25, 26, 54 (the reads), R4-commands-58 (the `cargo-about` pin); R6-phase0-1, 2.

Nothing here changes a tracked file; every record goes to the git-ignored `.superpowers/pr5/` folder, and nothing is committed. `BOX '<cmd>'` is `ssh -o BatchMode=yes "$LAZYMKV_BOX" '<cmd>'`, with `LAZYMKV_BOX` from `scripts/phase0/box.env` (Task 25 uses the same form). Every read of crates.io, of a release page or of a model card is metadata only (Ruling T3-1-a): no crate, installer or archive is downloaded; the one file fetched is the CC-BY-SA-4.0 (Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0) legal code, a text file. The cutoff of A1's 14-day rule is `2026-10-23` (the notes' date, 2026-11-06, less 14 days) for the crates and for the continuous integration (CI) tools alike, so Task 1's second read uses the same date.

**Files:** Create (git-ignored, never committed): `.superpowers/pr5/lock_delta.py` (copied from `.superpowers/pr4/lock_delta.py`, then edited), `.superpowers/pr5/pr5-lock-delta-plan.txt`, `.superpowers/pr5/lock-blocks-plan.txt`, `.superpowers/pr5/CC-BY-SA-4.0.txt`, `.superpowers/pr5/baseline-list.txt`, `.superpowers/pr5/baseline-per-crate.txt`, `.superpowers/pr5/baseline-junction-run.txt`, `.superpowers/pr5/pr5-mini-pc-runs.txt`, `.superpowers/pr5/pub-docs.pl` (Step 10). Modify (git-ignored): `.superpowers/pr5/decisions.txt` (append only; its header line `<item>, <date>, <answer>` stays).

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: the notes `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-06-phase-2-pr5-design-notes.md` (A1, calls 1, 20, 26), this plan's "Rulings this plan makes" (T5-R1 to T5-R65), `main` at `07ccc48` with `Cargo.lock` at 79 packages, `experiments/ocrs-trial/Cargo.toml:20` (phase 0's `ocrs` features `["onnx", "rten"]`), `docs/phase0/ocr-engine-research.md:68` (the model card's URL).
- Produces, in `.superpowers/pr5/decisions.txt`, one line each, exactly in these forms (later tasks find a line by its words before the first comma):

  - `watcher, <yyyy-MM-dd>, <answer>` (owner item 33: whether call 4's memory sampler runs beside a build; Tasks 1, 8, 11, 12 and 25 read it).
  - `A1 plan time, <yyyy-MM-dd>, <answer>`.
  - `ocrs features <comma-separated list>, <yyyy-MM-dd>, read from the index record of ocrs 0.13.1` (Task 1's `ocrs` line).
  - `ocrs line types re-exported, <yyyy-MM-dd>, <the re-exported paths>` or `ocrs line types rten-imageproc <version>, <yyyy-MM-dd>, <the type paths recognize_text takes>` (Task 1's `rten-imageproc` line and Task 8's imports).
  - `ubuntu-latest <release> <codename>, <yyyy-MM-dd>, read from <url>` (Task 24's apt source).
  - `MKVToolNix ubuntu <apt version string>, <yyyy-MM-dd>, read from <url>` (Task 24).

- [ ] **Step 1: Owner. The rulings and the memory watcher.** The controller sends the owner one message: "Pull request 5's plan makes rulings T5-R1 to T5-R65 (the plan's section 'Rulings this plan makes', where each gives the plan's call and the requirement it settles). Is any of them overturned? An overturn reopens the task the ruling names before that task starts. Eight of them amend the spec, the design or engine.md and are named here: T5-R1 (the `ocr` crate as two packages; design 4.1, 4.7, 10.11), T5-R2 (`lazymkvctl` links the model bytes only; spec 4.4's and design 11.1's ocrs rows), T5-R17 (an `audio-proxy.json` with `"proxy": null`; design 7.5), T5-R43 (the crate notices committed and checked on ubuntu, not made by the release job; design 4.7 and 11.4), T5-R49 (CI's ubuntu runner gets a static FFmpeg 7.x and the Windows runner the MKVToolNix installer; design 12.1), T5-R50 (the design's in-place amendments at Task 26), T5-R64 (with `CI` set, a missing tool or an FFmpeg below 7.0 fails layer 2 and Task 13's cross-check instead of skipping; design 12.1), T5-R65 (the self-test's judging of spec 13's minimum versions of MKVToolNix and FFmpeg moves to pull request 6; engine.md's S80)." In the same message it asks owner item 33: "Call 4's memory sampler is typeperf in a second plain SSH session beside a scripts/box.sh build (Tasks 1, 8, 11, 12 and 25); it runs no cargo and touches no C:\lazymkv\src. May it run beside the build, although the mini PC otherwise runs one command at a time?" It waits for an explicit answer to both in chat and appends `rulings T5-R1 to T5-R65, <yyyy-MM-dd>, none overturned`, or one `T5-R<n>, <yyyy-MM-dd>, overturned: <the owner's words>` line per overturn, and `watcher, <yyyy-MM-dd>, <answer>`. An overturn of T5-R1, T5-R2 or T5-R63 changes Task 1's lists, so Step 2 waits for it.

- [ ] **Step 2: The crates' feature table and re-exports (T5-R63, call 1; metadata only).** The controller reads, on the Mac:
  1. ocrs 0.13.1's index record at `https://index.crates.io/oc/rs/ocrs` (its `features` and `features2` tables and its `deps`). The features to name are the smallest set, under `default-features = false`, that turns on rten's loading of `.onnx` files. Expected: `onnx` alone (phase 0 built `["onnx", "rten"]`, `experiments/ocrs-trial/Cargo.toml:20`, where `rten` only adds `.rten` files, which this plan does not load). A table without an `onnx` feature, or one whose `onnx` does not reach an rten feature, is marked `DIFFERS FROM THE PLAN` and goes to Step 5's message by name.
  2. ocrs 0.13.1's published documentation, `https://docs.rs/ocrs/0.13.1/ocrs/` (the crate root's re-exports) and `https://docs.rs/ocrs/0.13.1/ocrs/struct.OcrEngine.html` (`recognize_text`'s signature). The answer is whether every rectangle and point type in `recognize_text`'s parameters is reachable as `ocrs::<name>`. When one is not, the answer names the `rten_imageproc` paths, and `rten-imageproc` becomes a direct root at the version rten 0.26.0 pulls in.
  The controller appends the two lines of the Interfaces (`ocrs features ...`, `ocrs line types ...`).

- [ ] **Step 3: The resolver for pull request 5's roots.** `cp .superpowers/pr4/lock_delta.py .superpowers/pr5/lock_delta.py`, then edit only these parts of the copy:
  - The docstring names pull request 5, Task 0 Step 3 and Task 1, and the roots below.
  - `ROOT`, `ROOT_FEATURES` and the single-root block of `resolve` become `ROOTS`, a list of `(name, requirement, default_features, features, member)` resolved in this order, each through `pick` and `add` as `ureq` was: `("ocrs", "=0.13.1", False, <Step 2's features>, "lazymkv-ocr")`, `("rten", "=0.26.0", False, set(), "lazymkv-ocr")`, `("png", "*", True, set(), "lazymkv-ocr")`, `("sha2", "*", True, set(), "lazymkv-ocr-models")`, and, when Step 2 found the line types not re-exported, `("rten-imageproc", "^0.26", True, set(), "lazymkv-ocr")`. - [ ] **Step 10: The Def/Use check (R4-commands-69).** Write `.superpowers/pr5/pub-docs.pl` exactly, so every task from Task 2 on runs it before its commit (Global Constraints, Docs and prose) and a missing doc is found before T5-R54 freezes `crates/core/src/subtitle/bitmap/`, `crates/ocr/`, `crates/ocr-models/` and `crates/tools/src/ocr.rs` at Task 11:

```perl
#!/usr/bin/perl
# usage: perl .superpowers/pr5/pub-docs.pl <base>
# Prints each pub item added since <base> under crates/ whose /// doc lacks "Def: T5-<n>. Use: T5-<m>." and exits 1
# when there is one. An item is added when its line is in the working tree's diff against <base> (run after git add,
# so a new file is tracked) and its name is not in the base file. The doc is read joined, so the sentence may wrap
# onto a second /// line.
use strict; use warnings;
my $base = shift or die "usage: pub-docs.pl <base>\n";
my @files = grep { /\.rs$/ } split /\n/, `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=AM $base -- crates`;
my ($seen, $bad) = (0, 0);
my $item = qr/^\s*pub\s+(?:const\s+|unsafe\s+)*(fn|struct|enum|const|static|type|trait)\s+(\w+)/;
for my $f (@files) {
  my %added;
  for (split /\n/, `git diff -U0 $base -- '$f'`) {
    next unless /^@@ -\S+ \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@/;
    my ($s, $n) = ($1, defined $2 ? $2 : 1);
    $added{$_} = 1 for $s .. $s + $n - 1;
  }
  my $old = `git show $base:'$f' 2>/dev/null`;
  open my $fh, '<', $f or die "$f: $!\n";
  my ($doc, $ln) = ('', 0);
  while (my $l = <$fh>) {
    $ln++;
    if ($l =~ m{^\s*///}) { $doc .= $l; next }
    next if $l =~ m{^\s*#\[};
    if (my ($kind, $name) = $l =~ $item) {
      if ($added{$ln} && $old !~ /\b\Q$kind\E\s+\Q$name\E\b/) {
        $seen++;
        (my $d = $doc) =~ s{^\s*///\s?}{}mg;
        $d =~ s/\s+/ /g;
        unless ($d =~ /Def: T5-\d+\. Use: T5-\d+(?:, T5-\d+)*\./) { print "$f:$ln: $kind $name\n"; $bad++ }
      }
    }
    $doc = '';
  }
}
print "$seen new pub items, $bad without a Def/Use doc\n";
exit($bad ? 1 : 0);
```

  Check, on the branch at `07ccc48` with nothing changed: `perl -c .superpowers/pr5/pub-docs.pl` prints `.superpowers/pr5/pub-docs.pl syntax OK`, and `perl .superpowers/pr5/pub-docs.pl 07ccc48` prints `0 new pub items, 0 without a Def/Use doc` and exits 0.

```rust
    /// The versions Cargo.lock holds for one package name, in the file's order.
    fn locked_versions(wanted: &str) -> Vec<String> {
        locked_packages().into_iter().filter(|(name, _)| name == wanted).map(|(_, version)| version).collect()
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_lock_pins_ocrs_0_13_1_and_holds_one_rten_at_0_26_0() {
        for (wanted, pin) in [("ocrs", "0.13.1"), ("rten", "0.26.0")] {
            let versions = locked_versions(wanted);
            assert!(!versions.is_empty(), "Cargo.lock lacks {wanted}");
            assert_eq!(versions, [pin], "Cargo.lock holds {wanted} {versions:?}, not {pin} alone (notes call 1)");
        }
        let rten_crates: Vec<String> =
            locked_packages().into_iter().map(|(name, _)| name).filter(|name| name.starts_with("rten-")).collect();
        assert!(rten_crates.iter().any(|name| name == "rten-imageproc"), "Cargo.lock lacks rten-imageproc");
        let mut distinct = rten_crates.clone();
        distinct.sort();
        distinct.dedup();
        assert_eq!(distinct.len(), rten_crates.len(), "Cargo.lock holds a second version of an rten crate {rten_crates:?} (design part 4.5)");
    }

    #[test]

        assert_eq!(on_0_8.len(), 1, "Cargo.lock holds miniz_oxide {on_0_8:?}; core's inflater shares png's one 0.8 (design part 4.7)");
    }
```

### Task 2: The note subtitle_text_unread and the unread streams

**Tier and risk:** opus (judgment: four crates share one rule, and the goldens must not move); risk medium: `decide`'s goldens and the engine's decide.json files must stay byte-identical for every recording without an unread stream (K5, the notes' section 4 and call 17), and a reader that took a phase 0 `summary.json` entry for an unread stream would change them.
**Covers:** R2-decoders-63 (`subs_run`'s unread input, T5-R51), 64 (the detail's form); R3-worker-28 to 33; R5-code-47, 48. Design part 10.8; the notes' call 17.

Precondition: Task 1 is committed, pushed and green. This task edits no `Cargo.toml` and no `Cargo.lock`. Nothing here reads a file in `core` (RP19): `core` gets the note, the facts and the line, and `lazymkv-dev decide` reads `<label>/subs-ocr/summary.json`. Task 6 writes that file's `"read"` and `"why"` keys for this reader, and Task 15 makes the engine fill the same facts; until then the engine passes no unread stream.

The rule this task adds, in design part 10.8's words: a stream step 10 did not read gives the job the note `subtitle_text_unread`, whose detail is `stream {n} was not read: {reason}` with no subtitle text; the note raises no review and never holds the job; and while a title has an unread stream its text adds no review (`decide_subtitles` leaves `facts.text` out, and `subs_run` refuses the title with one line per unread stream, T5-R51). With no unread stream every output is unchanged.

```rust
// crates/core/src/review.rs (spec 8.7 "Text", design part 10.8, P19)
pub enum Note { /* ..., */ SubtitleTextDisagrees, SubtitleTextUnread, /* CompatTagOmitted, ... */ }
// serde and as_str: "subtitle_text_unread"
impl Note { pub const ALL: [Note; 14]; } // SubtitleTextUnread right after SubtitleTextDisagrees

// crates/core/src/tracks/subtitle.rs
pub struct SubtitleFacts<'a> {
    /* events, removed, discdb, text, remembered, reviewed as before */
    pub unread: BTreeMap<u32, String>, // scan stream -> reason
}
pub fn unread_detail(stream: u32, reason: &str) -> String; // "stream {stream} was not read: {reason}"

// crates/core/src/subtitle/text.rs (T5-R51)
pub fn subs_run(
    rec_tree: &dyn Tree,
    rec: &PathKey,
    text_tree: &dyn Tree,
    text: &PathKey,
    orig_lang: Option<&str>,
    clear_max_bytes: i64,
    rule: &Rule,
    unread: &[(i64, String)], // (summary.json's n, its why)
) -> SubsRun;

// crates/core/src/recording/files.rs
impl OcrSummary { pub fn unread(&self) -> Vec<(i64, String)>; } // entries with "read": false, as (n, why)

// crates/dev/src/cmd/decide.rs
pub struct FileFacts {
    /* level_md5, probes, subs_index, packets as before */
    pub unread: Result<Vec<(i64, String)>, String>, // <label>/subs-ocr/summary.json; Ok(empty) without one
}
```

`decide_subtitles` pushes one `Noted { note: Note::SubtitleTextUnread, stream: Some(s), detail: unread_detail(s, reason) }` per entry of `facts.unread`, in stream order, after the text's notes; it raises no review for them and compares no text while `facts.unread` is not empty. `FactsSummary` gains no field. `subtitle_section` keeps its private signature `fn subtitle_section(rec: &Recording, label: &str, text: Option<&Path>) -> SubtitleEntry` (Task 15 makes it pub with `clear_max`).

```rust
    /// A cap reason as step 10 writes it (design part 10.8); the numbers are made up.
    const CAP_REASON: &str = "time cap of 60.0 s reached after 12 of 20 events";

    #[test]
    fn an_unread_stream_gives_one_subtitle_text_unread_note_and_no_review() {
        assert_eq!(unread_detail(3, CAP_REASON), "stream 3 was not read: time cap of 60.0 s reached after 12 of 20 events");
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS]);
        let measured = facts(vec![(1, regular_events()), (2, sdh_events()), (3, forced_events())]);
        let read = decide_subtitles(&title, &measured, &Settings::default());
        let evidence = SubtitleFacts { unread: BTreeMap::from([(3, CAP_REASON.to_string())]), ..measured.clone() };
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        let mut notes = read.notes.clone();
        notes.push(Noted {
            note: Note::SubtitleTextUnread,
            stream: Some(3),
            detail: "stream 3 was not read: time cap of 60.0 s reached after 12 of 20 events".to_string(),
        });
        assert_eq!(decision.notes, notes);
        // The note is a fact: it raises no review, and the counts and timing decide as they did.
        assert_eq!(decision.reviews, read.reviews);
        assert_eq!(
            (decision.kept, decision.dropped, decision.case, decision.confidence),
            (read.kept, read.dropped, read.case, read.confidence)
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_title_with_an_unread_stream_uses_no_text_of_its_other_streams() {
        // Stream 2's text differs from the counts (a_title_without_unread_streams_decides_as_before); stream 1 was not
        // read, so the title's text adds no review (design part 10.8).
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS, SPA_PGS]);
        let text = BTreeMap::from([(2, verdict(Role::Regular))]);
        let evidence = SubtitleFacts {
            text: Some(&text),
            unread: BTreeMap::from([(1, "lazymkv-ocr exited with code 101".to_string())]),
            ..facts(vec![(1, regular_events()), (2, sdh_events())])
        };
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(
            decision.notes,
            vec![Noted {
                note: Note::SubtitleTextUnread,
                stream: Some(1),
                detail: "stream 1 was not read: lazymkv-ocr exited with code 101".to_string(),
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.reviews, Vec::<ReviewReason>::new());
        assert_eq!((decision.case, decision.confidence), (SubtitleCase::Alignment, 0.85));
        assert_eq!(
            decision.kept,
            vec![
                track(1, SubtitleRole::Regular, Some(1000), "alignment"),
                track(2, SubtitleRole::Sdh, Some(1200), "alignment"),
            ]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_title_without_unread_streams_decides_as_before() {
        let title = bluray(&[VIDEO, ENG_PGS, ENG_PGS, SPA_PGS]);
        let text = BTreeMap::from([(2, verdict(Role::Regular))]);
        let evidence = SubtitleFacts { text: Some(&text), ..facts(vec![(1, regular_events()), (2, sdh_events())]) };
        assert!(evidence.unread.is_empty());
        let decision = decide_subtitles(&title, &evidence, &Settings::default());
        assert_eq!(
            decision.notes,
            vec![Noted {
                note: Note::SubtitleTextDisagrees,
                stream: Some(2),
                detail: "stream 2: the text reads regular, the counts keep it as sdh (8.7 \"Text\")".to_string(),
            }]
        );
        assert_eq!(decision.reviews, vec![ReviewReason::SubtitleAmbiguous]);
        assert_eq!((decision.case, decision.confidence), (SubtitleCase::Ambiguous, 0.60));
    }
```

```rust
    #[test]
    fn a_subs_run_with_an_unread_stream_names_it_instead_of_phase_0s_hint() {
        let mut title = write_title(true);
        let pgs: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str::<serde_json::Value>(&title.files["rec/subs/sub-0.packets.json"]).unwrap()["packets"]
                .clone();
        title.add_stream(1, "eng", "HDMV PGS", pgs);
        let tree = title.tree();
        let (rec, text, rule) = (PathKey::new("rec"), PathKey::new("text"), Rule::default());
        let unread = [(1, "time cap of 60.0 s reached after 12 of 20 events".to_string())];
        let run = subs_run(&tree, &rec, &tree, &text, None, 64, &rule, &unread);
        assert_eq!((run.exit_code, run.stdout.len(), run.analysis.is_none()), (2, 0, true));
        assert_eq!(run.stderr, ["stream s1 eng: not read by the engine: time cap of 60.0 s reached after 12 of 20 events"]);
        assert!(!run.stderr.iter().any(|line| line.contains("ocr-subs.ps1")), "{:?}", run.stderr);
        // The engine's word refuses the title even where the stream's text is there, and a stream the index does not
        // list is named with the tag und.
        let unread = [(0, "lazymkv-ocr exited with code 101".to_string()), (7, "made-up reason".to_string())];
        let run = subs_run(&tree, &rec, &tree, &text, None, 64, &rule, &unread);
        assert_eq!(
            run.stderr,
            [
                "stream s0 eng: not read by the engine: lazymkv-ocr exited with code 101",
                "stream s7 und: not read by the engine: made-up reason",
            ]
        );
        // With no unread stream the stream without text is phase 0's input error with its hint, as the golden reads it.
        let run = subs_run(&tree, &rec, &tree, &text, None, 64, &rule, &[]);
        assert_eq!((run.exit_code, run.stderr.len()), (2, 1));
        assert!(run.stderr[0].starts_with("stream s1 eng: no OCR text (no sub-1.ocr.jsonl in "), "{:?}", run.stderr);
        assert!(run.stderr[0].ends_with("); read it with ocr-subs.ps1"), "{:?}", run.stderr);
    }
```

### Task 3: The Matroska reader of evidence.mks (design 10.3)

**Tier and risk:** opus; risk high: if the reader misreads mkvmerge's output, every bitmap stream of every job is unread (design 10.8), and Task 11's goldens are the first real-data check.
**Covers:** R2-decoders-1, 2 (the inflater is `miniz_oxide`), 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 28 (zlib content and the refusals); R3-worker-62 and R5-code-46 (these tests live in `lazymkv-core` and run on the three systems); R6-phase0-13; Review Focus 4.

Precondition: Task 2 is committed, pushed and green, and Task 1 gave `lazymkv-core` the dependency `miniz_oxide.workspace = true` (the 0.8 line, default features on, so `miniz_oxide::inflate::decompress_to_vec_zlib` and `miniz_oxide::deflate::compress_to_vec_zlib` exist). This task edits no `Cargo.toml` and no `Cargo.lock`.

The reader is ours, not a crate (design 10.3, [OCR-2]): EBML (Extensible Binary Meta Language) is Matroska's container syntax, and the evidence file is the subtitle-only file mkvmerge writes with its default compression (K1: zlib for PGS (Presentation Graphic Stream) and VobSub tracks). An event's `pts` (presentation timestamp) is in seconds. Everything here is a pure function of bytes (RP19): no file, process or clock. Every test file is made up by the test writer `core::testsupport::mks` or assembled by hand in the test; no byte comes from `corpus/owner` or the tuning dataset (RP21).

**Files:**
- Modify: `crates/core/src/subtitle/mod.rs:1-2` (the module doc gains "and the bitmap pipeline of design part 10 (`bitmap`)"), `crates/core/src/subtitle/mod.rs:4` (`pub mod bitmap;` after `pub mod align;`).
- Create: `crates/core/src/subtitle/bitmap/mod.rs` (the module doc, `pub mod mkv;`, `SubCodec`, `CODEC_PGS`, `CODEC_VOBSUB`; Task 4 adds `pgs`, `vobsub`, `Object` and `Bitmap` here).
- Create: `crates/core/src/subtitle/bitmap/mkv.rs` (the reader; its 17 tests in `mod tests` at the end).
- Modify: `crates/core/src/testsupport/mod.rs:1-4` (the module doc gains "Pull request 5's Task 3 adds the made-up Matroska writer `mks` (design part 10.3)."), and after line 4 `pub mod mks;`.
- Create: `crates/core/src/testsupport/mks.rs` (the writer; Task 4 adds the PGS and VobSub unit builders).
- Test: `crates/core/src/subtitle/bitmap/mkv.rs` `mod tests`.

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: Task 1's edge `lazymkv-core -> miniz_oxide` (0.8); `lazymkv-core`'s feature `testsupport` and `crates/core/src/lib.rs:25-26` (`#[cfg(any(test, feature = "testsupport"))] pub mod testsupport;`), unchanged.
- Produces (every later task relies on these names and types exactly):

```rust
// crates/core/src/subtitle/bitmap/mod.rs (design 10.1, 10.3; pure)
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SubCodec { Pgs, VobSub }
pub const CODEC_PGS: &str = "S_HDMV/PGS";
pub const CODEC_VOBSUB: &str = "S_VOBSUB";

// crates/core/src/subtitle/bitmap/mkv.rs (design 10.3)
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct IdxHeader { pub width: u32, pub height: u32, pub palette: [[u8; 3]; 16] } // palette[i] = [R, G, B]
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct SubBlock { pub pts: f64, pub size: u64, pub payload: Vec<u8> } // payload with the content encoding undone; size = payload.len()
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq)]
pub struct SubStream { pub track: u64, pub codec_id: String, pub codec: Option<SubCodec>, pub idx: Option<IdxHeader>, pub blocks: Vec<SubBlock> }
pub fn read_stream(bytes: &[u8], n: usize) -> Result<SubStream, String>; // the n-th subtitle track, counted from 0 in track order (T5-R3)
pub fn parse_idx(codec_private: &[u8]) -> Result<IdxHeader, String>;

// crates/core/src/testsupport/mks.rs (feature testsupport)
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MksEncoding { None, Zlib, HeaderStripping(Vec<u8>), Other(u64) }
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct MksTrack { pub number: u64, pub kind: u64, pub codec_id: String, pub codec_private: Vec<u8>, pub language: String, pub encoding: MksEncoding }
#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct MksBlock { pub track: u64, pub time_ms: i64, pub cluster_ms: i64, pub payload: Vec<u8>, pub laced: bool, pub group: bool }
impl MksBlock { pub fn new(track: u64, time_ms: i64, payload: Vec<u8>) -> MksBlock } // cluster_ms = time_ms.div_euclid(1000) * 1000; laced and group false
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Default)]
pub struct MksShape { pub void_elements: bool, pub crc32: bool, pub unknown_size_clusters: bool, pub cues_and_tags: bool, pub timestamp_scale: Option<u64> }
pub const ATTACHMENT_TRAP: [u8; 6] = [0xA3, 0x84, 0x81, 0x00, 0x00, 0x80];
pub fn mks(tracks: &[MksTrack], blocks: &[MksBlock], shape: &MksShape) -> Vec<u8>;
pub fn idx_text(width: u32, height: u32, palette: &[[u8; 3]; 16]) -> Vec<u8>;
```

The refusal texts are fixed and hold numbers and codec IDs only: `not a Matroska file`; `evidence.mks has no subtitle stream {n}`; `content encoding {kind} of track {track} is not zlib compression or header stripping` (`{kind}` is the `ContentCompAlgo` number, or the word `encryption` for an encrypted track); `track {track} has a laced block at {pts:.3} s`; `zlib content of track {track} does not inflate`; `the VobSub idx header has no size line`; `the VobSub idx header has no palette of 16 colours`. The worker (Task 8) prints them as exit 3's reason (call 5). `codec` is None for a codec other than the two; `read_stream` still reads such a stream's blocks, and the caller refuses it (T5-R11). Later tasks build files with `MksShape::default()` or `MksShape { <fields>, ..MksShape::default() }` and blocks with `MksBlock::new` or `MksBlock { <fields>, ..MksBlock::new(..) }`, so a field added later breaks no caller.
