```rust
pub fn read_stream(ocr: &Ocr, stream: &SubStream, args: &WorkerArgs, started: Instant) -> Result<RunTotals, String>; // Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8.
pub fn main_with(args: &[String], err: &mut dyn Write) -> i32;                          // 0 read, 2 argument error, 3 refused. Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8.
```

The binary's contract, which Task 9's driver and Task 15's engine read: `lazymkv-ocr <evidence.mks> --stream N --clear-max BYTES --out DIR` (call 5); N is ffprobe's subtitle-relative index, counted from 0 over the evidence file's subtitle tracks in track order (T5-R3); exit 0 when the stream was read, with `DIR\sub-<N>.ocr.jsonl` (one line per event, each written and flushed before the next event is read), `DIR\s<N>\f-<ms>.png` (one per distinct crop) and `DIR\sub-<N>.run.json` (written last, so its presence marks a finished read); exit 2 with the parser's message as standard error's first line and `USAGE` as its second; exit 3 with the bare reason as standard error's first and only line, which T5-R8 makes the note's reason, so it holds numbers, codec IDs and the reader's or ocrs's error and never a path or subtitle text.

The items of the Interfaces block, with these docs and rules (the tests pin only part of them):
- `OCRS_VERSION`: "The ocrs version this worker is built with, the workspace's `=0.13.1` pin (design part 10.7, [ARCH-13]); the two change together, and `engine` in every record names it (design part 10.12). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8."
- `Ocr`: "ocrs's engine over the two embedded models, loaded once per worker process (design part 10.7, K2). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8, T5-10." `load()`: `rten::Model::load_static_slice(lazymkv_ocr_models::DETECTION)` and the same for `RECOGNITION`, then `ocrs::OcrEngine::new(ocrs::OcrEngineParams { detection_model: Some(detection), recognition_model: Some(recognition), ..Default::default() })`, as phase 0's `experiments/ocrs-trial/src/main.rs:196-200` built it; any error is `Err(format!("the OCR models did not load: {error}"))`. If `load_static_slice` refuses the embedded ONNX (Open Neural Network Exchange) bytes, the task stops and goes to the controller and the owner (design 10.7 names that loader); it does not switch loaders or model formats.
- The image ocrs sees: both `recognize` and `detect` turn the `Grey` into RGB (red, green, blue) bytes, each grey value three times, and call `ocrs::ImageSource::from_bytes(&rgb, (image.width, image.height))` then `engine.prepare_input(source)`, the form phase 0's trial handed ocrs (`experiments/ocrs-trial/src/main.rs:136-137, 152-155`), so arm F and the shipped method see the same input form (K2).
- The rectangle types: `RotatedRect`, `RectF` and their constructors come from the module path Task 0 recorded in `decisions.txt` (`ocrs line types re-exported`: ocrs's own re-export; `ocrs line types rten-imageproc <version>`: `rten_imageproc`), T5-R63.
- `recognize(image, boxes)`: "Reads the line boxes of one crop with ocrs's `recognize_text`, each box given as one rectangle, in the boxes' order, which is top to bottom (design part 10.7). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8, T5-10." Each box becomes `vec![RotatedRect::from_rect(RectF::from_tlhw(y, x, height, width))]` (as `f32`); no boxes gives `Ok(vec![])` without calling ocrs. The result keeps each `Some(line)` as `line.to_string().trim()` and leaves out `None` and empty lines, phase 0's rule (`experiments/ocrs-trial/src/main.rs:142-149`), so `lines` is never joined (design 10.12). An ocrs error is `Err(error.to_string())`.
- `detect(image)`: "Reads an irregular crop through ocrs's detector: `detect_words`, `find_text_lines`, then `recognize_text` over the found lines (design part 10.6, P18). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8, T5-10." `detect_ms` times `prepare_input`, `detect_words` and `find_text_lines`; `recognize_ms` times `recognize_text`. `boxes` holds one `LineBox` per found line, in ocrs's line order: the union of its words' `bounding_rect()`, with left and top floored and clamped at 0, right and bottom ceiled and clamped to the image, `width = right - left`, `height = bottom - top`. `lines` follows `recognize`'s rule. `Detected`: "The detector's line boxes and lines of one crop, with the two stage times the record's `ms.detect` and `ms.recognize` take (design parts 10.6, 10.12). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8, T5-10."
- `engine_id()`: "The `engine` of every record and of `run.json`: ocrs's version and both models' SHA-256 (Secure Hash Algorithm 256) pins (design part 10.12). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8, T5-10." `EngineId { ocrs: OCRS_VERSION.to_string(), detection_sha256: DETECTION_SHA256.to_string(), recognition_sha256: RECOGNITION_SHA256.to_string() }`.
- `grey_png(image)`: "One 8-bit grey PNG of a crop, exactly as ocrs read it (design part 10.12, EVID-5). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8, T5-10." `png::Encoder` with `ColorType::Grayscale` and `BitDepth::Eight`, the crate's default compression and filter; an encoder error is `Err(error.to_string())`.
- `read_png_grey(bytes)`: "Reads an 8-bit grey PNG back, for arm R' of the trial and the goldens (design parts 10.4, 10.9). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8, T5-10, T5-11." `png::Decoder` over `std::io::Cursor::new(bytes)`; any colour type other than `Grayscale` or a bit depth other than 8 is `Err("not an 8-bit grey PNG")`; a decoding error is `Err(error.to_string())`. The `png` interface of the version in `Cargo.lock` is the judge of the calls' exact names.

Create `crates/ocr/tests/worker.rs`:

```rust
//! The OCR worker over made-up evidence files (design part 10.7; notes F1). Every bitmap is a block shape with no
//! glyph and no font (RP21); no test asserts recognised text. Runs on ubuntu on CI and on the mini PC.

use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::{Command, Output};

use lazymkv_core::subtitle::bitmap::evidence::{read_run_json, whole_records};
use lazymkv_core::subtitle::bitmap::mkv::read_stream as read_mks;
use lazymkv_core::subtitle::bitmap::{CODEC_PGS, CODEC_VOBSUB};
use lazymkv_core::testsupport::mks::{
    idx_text, mks, pgs_display_set, vobsub_unit, MksBlock, MksEncoding, MksShape, MksTrack,
};
use lazymkv_ocr::stream::{main_with, USAGE};
use lazymkv_ocr::{engine_id, read_png_grey};
use serde_json::Value;

const VIDEO: (u32, u32) = (1920, 1080);
/// Palette entry 1: Y 235, Cr 128, Cb 128, alpha 255, which prepares to grey 20 (design part 10.5).
const OPAQUE: (u8, [u8; 4]) = (1, [235, 128, 128, 255]);
/// The same colour with alpha 0, which prepares to white: an event with no dark pixel.
const TRANSPARENT: (u8, [u8; 4]) = (1, [235, 128, 128, 0]);
type Objects = &'static [(u16, u32, u32, u32, u32, u8)];
/// One line: a 300 x 40 block at (800, 900), below the frame's middle row 540.
const ONE: Objects = &[(0, 800, 900, 300, 40, 1)];
/// Two lines, 20 empty rows apart.
const TWO: Objects = &[(0, 700, 860, 400, 40, 1), (1, 700, 920, 300, 40, 1)];
/// Ink above and below the middle row: trigger 4 (design part 10.6).
const TOP_AND_BOTTOM: Objects = &[(0, 800, 100, 300, 40, 1), (1, 800, 900, 300, 40, 1)];
/// The size of a PGS clear display set (spec 8.7); the worker never decodes it.
const CLEAR_SET: [u8; 30] = [0x16; 30];
const RECORD_KEYS: [&str; 13] =
    ["frame", "file", "t", "pts", "lines", "text", "size", "boxes", "method", "trigger", "engine", "decoder", "ms"];

/// A fresh, empty folder under the system temporary folder for one test.
fn scratch(tag: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("lazymkv-ocr-{tag}-{}", std::process::id()));
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
    dir
}

/// A subtitle track (type 17) stored with zlib, as mkvmerge stores PGS and VobSub by default (K1).
fn subtitle(number: u64, codec_id: &str, codec_private: Vec<u8>, encoding: MksEncoding) -> MksTrack {
    MksTrack {
        number,
        kind: 17,
        codec_id: codec_id.to_string(),
        codec_private,
        language: "eng".to_string(),
        encoding,
    }
}

fn set(objects: Objects) -> Vec<u8> {
    pgs_display_set(VIDEO, objects, &[OPAQUE])
}

fn pgs_with(blocks: &[MksBlock]) -> Vec<u8> {
    mks(&[subtitle(1, CODEC_PGS, Vec::new(), MksEncoding::Zlib)], blocks, &MksShape::default())
}

/// ONE at 1 s, a clear at 3 s, TWO at 4 s, a clear at 6 s, TOP_AND_BOTTOM at 7 s and ONE again at 9 s.
fn pgs_file() -> Vec<u8> {
    pgs_with(&[
        MksBlock::new(1, 1000, set(ONE)),
        MksBlock::new(1, 3000, CLEAR_SET.to_vec()),
        MksBlock::new(1, 4000, set(TWO)),
        MksBlock::new(1, 6000, CLEAR_SET.to_vec()),
        MksBlock::new(1, 7000, set(TOP_AND_BOTTOM)),
        MksBlock::new(1, 9000, set(ONE)),
    ])
}

/// The reader's (pts, size) of every block larger than `clear_max`: the events the worker must record.
fn listed_events(bytes: &[u8], n: usize, clear_max: i64) -> Vec<(f64, u64)> {
    let stream = read_mks(bytes, n).unwrap();
    stream.blocks.iter().filter(|b| b.size as i64 > clear_max).map(|b| (b.pts, b.size)).collect()
}

fn path(p: &Path) -> &str {
    p.to_str().unwrap()
}

/// The built worker, started as the engine starts it: an empty environment but RTEN_NUM_THREADS=3 (V1, design 10.7).
fn run_binary(evidence: &Path, stream: usize, clear_max: i64, out: &Path, cwd: &Path) -> Output {
    let (stream, clear_max) = (stream.to_string(), clear_max.to_string());
    Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_lazymkv-ocr"))
        .args([path(evidence), "--stream", stream.as_str(), "--clear-max", clear_max.as_str(), "--out", path(out)])
        .current_dir(cwd)
        .env_clear()
        .env("RTEN_NUM_THREADS", "3")
        .output()
        .unwrap()
}

fn in_process(args: &[&str]) -> (i32, String) {
    let args: Vec<String> = args.iter().map(|arg| arg.to_string()).collect();
    let mut err = Vec::new();
    let code = main_with(&args, &mut err);
    (code, String::from_utf8(err).unwrap())
}

fn run_in_process(evidence: &Path, stream: usize, clear_max: i64, out: &Path) -> (i32, String) {
    let (stream, clear_max) = (stream.to_string(), clear_max.to_string());
    in_process(&[path(evidence), "--stream", &stream, "--clear-max", &clear_max, "--out", path(out)])
}

fn records(out: &Path, n: usize) -> (String, Vec<Value>) {
    let text = fs::read_to_string(out.join(format!("sub-{n}.ocr.jsonl"))).unwrap();
    let parsed = text.lines().map(|line| serde_json::from_str(line).unwrap()).collect();
    (text, parsed)
}

/// The names in a folder, sorted.
fn names(dir: &Path) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut names: Vec<String> =
        fs::read_dir(dir).unwrap().map(|e| e.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned()).collect();
    names.sort();
    names
}

fn strs<'a>(records: &'a [Value], key: &str) -> Vec<&'a str> {
    records.iter().map(|r| r[key].as_str().unwrap()).collect()
}

#[test]
fn the_worker_reads_a_made_up_pgs_stream_into_records_run_json_and_crops() {
    let root = scratch("pgs");
    let (evidence, out, cwd) = (root.join("evidence.mks"), root.join("out"), root.join("cwd"));
    fs::write(&evidence, pgs_file()).unwrap();
    fs::create_dir_all(&cwd).unwrap();
    let run = run_binary(&evidence, 0, 64, &out, &cwd);
    assert_eq!(run.status.code(), Some(0), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&run.stderr));
    assert!(run.stdout.is_empty(), "the worker prints nothing on standard output");

    let listed = listed_events(&pgs_file(), 0, 64);
    assert_eq!(listed.iter().map(|e| e.0).collect::<Vec<_>>(), [1.0, 4.0, 7.0, 9.0]);
    let (text, records) = records(&out, 0);
    assert_eq!(whole_records(&text), listed, "one record per event, in pts order, with the reader's sizes");
    for (i, record) in records.iter().enumerate() {
        let keys: BTreeSet<&str> = record.as_object().unwrap().keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
        assert_eq!(keys, RECORD_KEYS.into_iter().collect::<BTreeSet<_>>());
        assert_eq!(record["frame"], i);
        assert_eq!(record["t"], record["pts"]);
        assert!(record["lines"].is_array());
    }
    assert_eq!(strs(&records, "method"), ["rows", "rows", "detector", "rows"]);
    let triggers: Vec<Value> = records.iter().map(|r| r["trigger"].clone()).collect();
    assert_eq!(triggers, [Value::Null, Value::Null, Value::from(4), Value::Null]);
    let boxes: Vec<usize> = records.iter().map(|r| r["boxes"].as_array().unwrap().len()).collect();
    assert_eq!((boxes[0], boxes[1], boxes[3]), (1, 2, 1));
    assert_eq!(strs(&records, "file"), ["f-000001000.png", "f-000004000.png", "f-000007000.png", "f-000001000.png"]);

    let crops = names(&out.join("s0"));
    assert_eq!(crops, ["f-000001000.png", "f-000004000.png", "f-000007000.png"]);
    for name in &crops {
        read_png_grey(&fs::read(out.join("s0").join(name)).unwrap()).unwrap();
    }
    let one = read_png_grey(&fs::read(out.join("s0").join("f-000001000.png")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((one.width, one.height), (332, 72), "the 300 x 40 block grown by 16 on each side");

    let totals = read_run_json(&fs::read_to_string(out.join("sub-0.run.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((totals.events, totals.distinct, totals.rows, totals.detector), (4, 3, 3, [0, 0, 0, 1]));
    assert_eq!(totals.engine, engine_id());
    assert!(totals.wall_ms > 0);
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn repeated_bitmaps_share_one_crop_and_one_reading() {
    let root = scratch("repeat");
    let (evidence, out) = (root.join("evidence.mks"), root.join("out"));
    let blocks = [MksBlock::new(1, 1000, set(ONE)), MksBlock::new(1, 2000, set(ONE)), MksBlock::new(1, 5000, set(ONE))];
    fs::write(&evidence, pgs_with(&blocks)).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run_in_process(&evidence, 0, 64, &out), (0, String::new()));
    let (_, records) = records(&out, 0);
    assert_eq!(strs(&records, "file"), ["f-000001000.png"; 3]);
    for repeat in &records[1..] {
        assert_eq!(repeat["lines"], records[0]["lines"]);
        assert_eq!(repeat["boxes"], records[0]["boxes"]);
        assert_eq!(repeat["ms"]["recognize"], 0.0, "a repeat is not read again");
        assert_eq!(repeat["ms"]["detect"], Value::Null);
    }
    assert_eq!(names(&out.join("s0")), ["f-000001000.png"]);
    let totals = read_run_json(&fs::read_to_string(out.join("sub-0.run.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((totals.events, totals.distinct, totals.rows), (3, 1, 3));
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn a_made_up_vobsub_stream_reads_too() {
    let root = scratch("vobsub");
    let (evidence, out) = (root.join("evidence.mks"), root.join("out"));
    let mut palette = [[0u8; 3]; 16];
    palette[1] = [255, 255, 255];
    let unit = |width| vobsub_unit((100, 380, width, 40), 1, [0, 1, 0, 0], [0, 15, 0, 0]);
    // A SubRip track first, as MakeMKV's DVD closed captions come (R6-phase0-14), so the VobSub track is stream 1.
    let tracks = [
        subtitle(1, "S_TEXT/UTF8", Vec::new(), MksEncoding::None),
        subtitle(2, CODEC_VOBSUB, idx_text(720, 480, &palette), MksEncoding::Zlib),
    ];
    let blocks = [
        MksBlock::new(1, 500, b"sentinel".to_vec()),
        MksBlock::new(2, 2000, unit(200)),
        MksBlock::new(2, 6000, unit(240)),
    ];
    let bytes = mks(&tracks, &blocks, &MksShape::default());
    fs::write(&evidence, &bytes).unwrap();
    let listed = listed_events(&bytes, 1, 64);
    assert_eq!(listed.len(), 2, "both units are larger than 64 bytes");
    assert_eq!(run_in_process(&evidence, 1, 64, &out), (0, String::new()));
    let (text, records) = records(&out, 1);
    assert_eq!(whole_records(&text), listed);
    assert_eq!(strs(&records, "file"), ["f-000002000.png", "f-000006000.png"]);
    assert_eq!(names(&out), ["s1", "sub-1.ocr.jsonl", "sub-1.run.json"]);
    let first = read_png_grey(&fs::read(out.join("s1").join("f-000002000.png")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((first.width, first.height), (232, 72));
    let totals = read_run_json(&fs::read_to_string(out.join("sub-1.run.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((totals.events, totals.distinct), (2, 2));
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn an_argument_error_exits_2_with_the_usage() {
    let cases = [
        (vec![], "missing <evidence.mks>"),
        (vec!["e.mks", "--stream", "x", "--clear-max", "64", "--out", "o"], "--stream takes a whole number, not 'x'"),
        (vec!["e.mks", "--stream", "0", "--clear-max", "64"], "missing --out"),
        (vec!["e.mks", "--stream", "0", "--clear-max", "64", "--out", "o", "--fast", "1"], "unknown argument '--fast'"),
    ];
    for (args, first) in cases {
        assert_eq!(in_process(&args), (2, format!("{first}\n{USAGE}\n")), "{args:?}");
    }
}

#[test]
fn a_text_stream_is_refused_with_exit_3_naming_its_codec() {
    let root = scratch("text");
    let (evidence, out) = (root.join("evidence.mks"), root.join("out"));
    let tracks = [subtitle(1, "S_TEXT/UTF8", Vec::new(), MksEncoding::None)];
    fs::write(&evidence, mks(&tracks, &[MksBlock::new(1, 500, b"sentinel".to_vec())], &MksShape::default())).unwrap();
    let refused = "subtitle stream 0 has codec S_TEXT/UTF8, which is not PGS or VobSub\n".to_string();
    assert_eq!(run_in_process(&evidence, 0, 64, &out), (3, refused));
    assert!(!out.exists(), "a refused stream writes nothing");
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn a_laced_block_is_refused_with_exit_3() {
    let root = scratch("laced");
    let (evidence, out) = (root.join("evidence.mks"), root.join("out"));
    let laced = MksBlock { laced: true, ..MksBlock::new(1, 1000, set(ONE)) };
    fs::write(&evidence, pgs_with(&[laced])).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run_in_process(&evidence, 0, 64, &out), (3, "track 1 has a laced block at 1.000 s\n".to_string()));
    assert!(!out.exists());
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

/// Call 5: a content encoding other than zlib and header stripping refuses the stream with Task 3's sentence alone.
#[test]
fn another_content_encoding_is_refused_with_exit_3() {
    let root = scratch("encoding");
    let (evidence, out) = (root.join("evidence.mks"), root.join("out"));
    let tracks = [subtitle(1, CODEC_PGS, Vec::new(), MksEncoding::Other(1))];
    fs::write(&evidence, mks(&tracks, &[MksBlock::new(1, 1000, set(ONE))], &MksShape::default())).unwrap();
    let refused = "content encoding 1 of track 1 is not zlib compression or header stripping\n".to_string();
    assert_eq!(run_in_process(&evidence, 0, 64, &out), (3, refused));
    assert!(!out.exists(), "a refused stream writes nothing");
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

/// Call 5: a display set the decoder refuses (Task 4) refuses the stream, naming the event and the decoder's sentence.
#[test]
fn a_display_set_the_decoder_refuses_exits_3() {
    let root = scratch("undecodable");
    let (evidence, out) = (root.join("evidence.mks"), root.join("out"));
    // ONE's display set with its object segment's declared data length one more than it holds. A segment is its type
    // byte, a 2-byte length and its data; an object segment's data is its id (2), version (1), sequence flags (1),
    // data length (3, counting the 4 bytes of width and height), width (2), height (2) and the run-length data.
    let mut broken = set(ONE);
    let (mut at, mut rle) = (0, None);
    while at < broken.len() {
        let len = u16::from_be_bytes([broken[at + 1], broken[at + 2]]) as usize;
        if broken[at] == 0x15 {
            let declared = u32::from_be_bytes([0, broken[at + 7], broken[at + 8], broken[at + 9]]) + 1;
            broken[at + 7..at + 10].copy_from_slice(&declared.to_be_bytes()[1..]);
            rle = Some(len - 11);
            break;
        }
        at += 3 + len;
    }
    let rle = rle.expect("ONE's display set holds one object segment");
    fs::write(&evidence, pgs_with(&[MksBlock::new(1, 1000, broken)])).unwrap();
    let reason = format!("event 0 at 1.000 s does not decode: PGS object 0 holds {rle} bytes of run-length data, not {}\n", rle + 1);
    assert_eq!(run_in_process(&evidence, 0, 64, &out), (3, reason));
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn a_missing_stream_or_evidence_file_is_refused_with_exit_3() {
    let root = scratch("missing");
    let (evidence, out) = (root.join("evidence.mks"), root.join("out"));
    fs::write(&evidence, pgs_file()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run_in_process(&evidence, 5, 64, &out), (3, "evidence.mks has no subtitle stream 5\n".to_string()));
    let (code, err) = run_in_process(&root.join("absent.mks"), 0, 64, &out);
    assert_eq!(code, 3);
    assert!(err.starts_with("the evidence file could not be read: ") && err.lines().count() == 1, "{err}");
    assert!(!err.contains("absent.mks"), "the reason names no path: {err}");
    assert!(!out.exists());
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn an_event_without_dark_pixels_gets_a_record_with_no_crop_and_no_reading() {
    let root = scratch("blank");
    let (evidence, out) = (root.join("evidence.mks"), root.join("out"));
    let blank = pgs_display_set(VIDEO, ONE, &[TRANSPARENT]);
    fs::write(&evidence, pgs_with(&[MksBlock::new(1, 1000, set(ONE)), MksBlock::new(1, 2000, blank)])).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(run_in_process(&evidence, 0, 64, &out), (0, String::new()));
    let (_, records) = records(&out, 0);
    assert_eq!(records.len(), 2);
    let empty = &records[1];
    assert_eq!(
        (&empty["file"], &empty["lines"], &empty["boxes"], &empty["method"], &empty["trigger"]),
        (&Value::from(""), &Value::Array(vec![]), &Value::Array(vec![]), &Value::from("rows"), &Value::Null)
    );
    assert_eq!(empty["ms"]["recognize"], 0.0);
    assert_eq!(names(&out.join("s0")), ["f-000001000.png"]);
    let totals = read_run_json(&fs::read_to_string(out.join("sub-0.run.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((totals.events, totals.distinct, totals.rows), (2, 1, 2));
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn the_clear_max_argument_decides_which_packets_are_events() {
    let root = scratch("clear-max");
    let (evidence, out) = (root.join("evidence.mks"), root.join("out"));
    fs::write(&evidence, pgs_file()).unwrap();
    let smallest = listed_events(&pgs_file(), 0, 64).iter().map(|e| e.1).min().unwrap() as i64;
    let listed = listed_events(&pgs_file(), 0, smallest);
    // The two ONE sets (1 s and 9 s) are the smallest, one object each: at exactly --clear-max bytes they are clears.
    assert_eq!(listed.iter().map(|e| e.0).collect::<Vec<_>>(), [4.0, 7.0], "a packet of exactly --clear-max bytes is a clear");
    assert_eq!(run_in_process(&evidence, 0, smallest, &out), (0, String::new()));
    let (text, _) = records(&out, 0);
    assert_eq!(whole_records(&text), listed);
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}

#[test]
fn the_worker_writes_nothing_outside_out() {
    let root = scratch("outside");
    let (evidence, out, cwd) = (root.join("evidence.mks"), root.join("out"), root.join("cwd"));
    fs::write(&evidence, pgs_file()).unwrap();
    fs::create_dir_all(&cwd).unwrap();
    let run = run_binary(&evidence, 0, 64, &out, &cwd);
    assert_eq!(run.status.code(), Some(0), "{}", String::from_utf8_lossy(&run.stderr));
    assert_eq!(names(&root), ["cwd", "evidence.mks", "out"]);
    assert!(names(&cwd).is_empty(), "nothing in the working folder");
    assert_eq!(names(&out), ["s0", "sub-0.ocr.jsonl", "sub-0.run.json"]);
    assert_eq!(fs::read(&evidence).unwrap(), pgs_file(), "the evidence file is only read");
    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
}
```

- [ ] **Step 7: Implement `crates/ocr/src/stream.rs` and `crates/ocr/src/main.rs`**

The items of the Interfaces block, with these docs and rules:

`USAGE`: "The worker's command line (notes call 5). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8." `WorkerArgs`: "The worker's four arguments: the evidence file, the subtitle-relative stream number (T5-R3), the job's `sub_clear_max_bytes` (T5-R59) and the output folder (design part 10.2 step 3, B1 (the worker's folder)). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8."

`parse_args(args)`: "Reads the worker's arguments in any order (notes call 5). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8." One argument not starting with `--` is the evidence path; `--stream`, `--clear-max` and `--out` each take the next argument as their value. The messages, exactly:
- a flag with no next argument: `{flag} needs a value`;
- `--stream` not a `usize`: `--stream takes a whole number, not '{value}'`; `--clear-max` not an `i64` of 0 or more: `--clear-max takes a whole number of bytes, not '{value}'`;
- a flag given a second time: `{flag} is given twice`;
- a second path, or any other argument starting with `--`: `unknown argument '{argument}'`;
- after the loop, in this order: `missing <evidence.mks>`, `missing --stream`, `missing --clear-max`, `missing --out`.

`open_stream(bytes, n)`: "Reads subtitle stream `n` of the evidence file and refuses a codec other than PGS and VobSub, before any model is loaded (design parts 10.3, 10.8; T5-R11). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8." `lazymkv_core::subtitle::bitmap::mkv::read_stream(bytes, n)`; its error is returned unchanged (Task 3's fixed texts); a stream whose `codec` is None is `Err(format!("subtitle stream {n} has codec {codec_id}, which is not PGS or VobSub"))`.

`read_stream(ocr, stream, args, started)`: "Reads one stream's events into `sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl`, `s<n>\f-<ms>.png` and, last, `sub-<n>.run.json` in `args.out` (design parts 10.2 step 4, 10.5 to 10.7, 10.12). Every event is decoded and each distinct crop is read once; the stream's median line height is taken over every event before any event is read. Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8." With `n = args.stream`, in two passes:
1. **Decode and prepare, every event.** The events are the blocks with `size as i64 > args.clear_max` ("larger than", spec 8.7), numbered from 0 in file order; no other block is decoded or recorded. A PGS stream feeds the events in order to one `PgsDecoder::new()`; a VobSub stream calls `decode_vobsub(payload, idx)` with the stream's `idx`. A decoding error is `Err(format!("event {i} at {pts:.3} s does not decode: {error}"))`. Then `prepare`, `crop` and, for a crop, `crop_key` and `rows(&crop.image)`. Each event keeps its `pts`, `size`, `video_height`, the key and `Rows`, and the times `ms.decode` (the decoder call) and `ms.prepare` (`prepare`, `crop` and `crop_key`), measured with `std::time::Instant` in milliseconds as `f64`. The crop's image is kept in memory only for the first event with its key (design 10.5's memory figure); a later event with the same key keeps the first one's index.
2. **Read, in event order.** `median = median_line_height(&rows)` over every event that has a crop, repeats included (T5-R7). `create_dir_all(args.out.join(format!("s{n}")))`, then `sub-{n}.ocr.jsonl` is created (truncating), and for each event:
   - no crop: a record with `file` `""`, `lines` and `boxes` empty, `method` `Rows`, `trigger` None, `ms.lines` 0.0, `ms.detect` None, `ms.recognize` 0.0; no PNG;
   - a key's first event: `trigger(&rows, median, &crop, video_height)`; for `Some(k)`, `ocr.detect(&crop.image)` gives `boxes`, `lines`, `ms.detect = Some(detect_ms)` and `ms.recognize = recognize_ms`, with `method` `Detector` and `trigger` `Some(k)`; for None, `boxes = line_boxes(&crop.image, &rows)` and `lines = ocr.recognize(&crop.image, &boxes)?`, timed as `ms.recognize`, with `method` `Rows`, `trigger` None and `ms.detect` None. `ms.lines` times `trigger` and `line_boxes`. Then `grey_png(&crop.image)` is written to `s{n}\{crop_name(pts)}` before the record that names it;
   - a repeat: the first event's `file`, `lines`, `boxes`, `method` and `trigger`, its own `ms.decode` and `ms.prepare`, `ms.lines` 0.0, `ms.detect` None and `ms.recognize` 0.0.
   Every record has `frame` the event's number, its own `pts` and `size`, and `engine: engine_id()`; `record_line(&record)` is written with one `write_all` on the unbuffered `std::fs::File` before the next event is read, so a killed run leaves only whole lines and at most one torn last line (T5-R9). An ocrs error is `Err(format!("ocrs failed on event {i} at {pts:.3} s: {error}"))`; a write error is `Err(format!("could not write {name}: {error}"))` with the file name alone, never its folder.
3. **Totals.** `RunTotals { events, distinct: the number of PNGs written, rows: the records with method Rows, detector: the records with each trigger 1 to 4 at index k - 1, ms: each stage's sum over the records (detect over the Some values), engine: engine_id(), wall_ms: started.elapsed().as_millis() as u64 }`, written as `run_json(&totals)` to `sub-{n}.run.json` with `std::fs::write` after everything else, and returned.

`main_with(args, err)`: "The worker's run: exit 0 when the stream was read, 2 on an argument error with the message and the usage on `err`, 3 when the stream is refused with the reason alone on `err` (notes call 5; T5-R8 reads exit 3's first line as the note's reason). Def: T5-8. Use: T5-8." In this order: `started = Instant::now()`; `parse_args`, whose error writes `{message}\n{USAGE}\n` and returns 2; `std::fs::read(&args.evidence)`, whose error is the reason `the evidence file could not be read: {error}` (the `io::Error` alone, no path); `open_stream`; `Ocr::load()`; `std::fs::create_dir_all(&args.out)`, whose error is `the output folder could not be made: {error}`; `read_stream(&ocr, &stream, &args, started)`. Any reason writes `{reason}\n` and returns 3; success returns 0. Nothing is written to standard output, and no environment variable is read (the engine sets `RTEN_NUM_THREADS`, which rten reads itself).

`crates/ocr/src/main.rs`: its doc names design part 10.7 and K2; `main` collects `std::env::args_os().skip(1)` with `into_string()`, and an argument that is not valid Unicode writes `an argument is not valid Unicode\n{USAGE}\n` to standard error and exits 2; otherwise it exits with `lazymkv_ocr::stream::main_with(&args, &mut std::io::stderr())`.

The engine (Task 15) and `lazymkv-dev ocr-trial read` (Task 10) start `lazymkv-ocr` through one function, so the trial's arm R measures what ships (K2).
```rust
// lazymkv_platform (crates/platform/src/lib.rs)
/// What to start: one program with its arguments (spec 4.3, design part 4.2). `Default` is the empty spawn (no
/// program, no argument, no variable, normal priority), so a literal can end with `..Spawn::default()` and a field
/// added later leaves it unchanged (T5-R54). Def: T8, T5-9. Use: T11, T5-9, T5-13.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, Default)]
pub struct Spawn {
    /// The program to run, as a full path.
    pub program: PathBuf,
    /// The arguments, one string each.
    pub args: Vec<String>,
    /// Extra environment variables for the child, added after what the runner keeps of the inherited environment
    /// (on Windows only the names of `security::CHILD_ENV_NAMES`, V1, so a variable reaches a guarded child only
    /// through this list). The engine leaves this empty for every child but the OCR worker, whose one variable is
    /// `RTEN_NUM_THREADS=3` (S43; design part 10.7, K2; T5-R37).
    pub env: Vec<(String, String)>,
    /// Whether to start the child at below-normal priority. A no-op where the platform has no such class.
    pub below_normal: bool,
}

// lazymkv_tools (crates/tools/src/record.rs, re-exported at the crate root as lazymkv_tools::run_recorded_in;
// the module `record` stays private)
/// Runs `spawn` under `ctx.guard` exactly as `run_recorded` runs its program: the same four run files, the same
/// limit, cancel and line actions, the same errors (design parts 5.3, 7.2), with the caller's whole `Spawn`, its
/// `env` and `below_normal` included (T5-R37). Def: T5-9. Use: T5-9, T5-13.
pub fn run_recorded_in(
    ctx: &ToolCtx,
    spawn: &Spawn,
    out: &Path,
    limit: Option<Duration>,
    on_line: &mut dyn FnMut(&str) -> LineAction,
) -> io::Result<RunResult>;
// run_recorded keeps its signature; its doc's last line becomes: "It is `run_recorded_in` with
// `Spawn { program, args, below_normal, ..Spawn::default() }`, so no tool it runs gets an extra environment variable
// (S43). Def: T11, T5-9. Use: T13, T14, T23."

// lazymkv_tools::ocr (crates/tools/src/ocr.rs; re-exported at the crate root)
/// The worker's one environment variable: rten's thread count, the J4125's four cores less one, a fixed value of
/// spec 14 (design part 10.7, K2). Def: T5-9. Use: T5-9.
pub const RTEN_NUM_THREADS: (&str, &str) = ("RTEN_NUM_THREADS", "3");
/// The worker's command line `<evidence.mks> --stream N --clear-max BYTES --out DIR` (call 5): `evidence` and `out`
/// as `to_string_lossy` gives them, `stream` the subtitle-relative index of T5-R3, `clear_max` the job's
/// `sub_clear_max_bytes` (T5-R59). Def: T5-9. Use: T5-10, T5-15.
pub fn ocr_args(evidence: &Path, stream: i64, clear_max: i64, out: &Path) -> Vec<String>;
/// How one worker run ended (call 5, T5-R8). Def: T5-9. Use: T5-10, T5-15.
#[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum WorkerEnd {
    /// Exit 0: the stream was read.
    Read,
    /// Exit 3 with a first standard error line: the stream was refused; the line is the reason.
    Refused(String),
    /// Exit 2: the worker refused its arguments, an engine bug; the first standard error line, or empty.
    ArgumentError(String),
    /// Any other exit code (101 is a panic, 3 with no reason line included), or None when the run ended without one.
    Exited(Option<i32>),
    /// Killed once its cap passed (design part 10.8).
    TimedOut,
    /// Killed because the job's cancel flag was raised (design part 10.7, ENG-13).
    Cancelled,
}
/// T5-R8's reason for an end: `Refused(line)` gives the line; `ArgumentError(line)` gives
/// `lazymkv-ocr refused its arguments: <line>`, or `lazymkv-ocr refused its arguments` when the line is empty;
/// `Exited(Some(c))` gives `lazymkv-ocr exited with code <c>` and quotes no standard error (a panic's can hold
/// subtitle text, design part 10.12); `Exited(None)` gives `lazymkv-ocr ended without an exit code`; None for
/// `Read`, `TimedOut` (the caller writes `cap_reason`) and `Cancelled`. Def: T5-9. Use: T5-15.
pub fn end_reason(end: &WorkerEnd) -> Option<String>;
/// Runs the OCR worker once (design parts 5.3, 10.7, 10.8; K2; T5-R8, T5-R10, T5-R57): `program` with `args` under
/// `ctx.guard`, at below-normal priority with `RTEN_NUM_THREADS=3` as its only extra variable, recorded capture-style
/// at `capture` with `<capture>.stderr`, `.timing.jsonl` and `.exit.json` beside it (the run's wall time is
/// `.exit.json`'s `elapsed_ms`), and killed once `cap` has passed since its start, the model load included. No line
/// of the worker reaches `ctx.on_output` (design part 10.12). `cap` is the caller's `time_cap_s(events)` seconds,
/// a parameter and never a setting (T5-R10). Err only when the worker cannot start or its run cannot be recorded,
/// as `run_recorded`. Def: T5-9. Use: T5-10, T5-15.
pub fn run_worker(ctx: &ToolCtx, program: &Path, args: &[String], capture: &Path, cap: Duration) -> io::Result<WorkerEnd>;
```

`ToolCtx` carries the guard and the host, so Task 10 passes `lazymkv_platform::native_guard()` and Task 15 the engine's guard through this one function. `run_worker` creates no folder but the capture's parent (as `run_recorded` does) and deletes nothing: the output folder is the caller's to make and to delete (T5-R4).

- [ ] **Step 6: Write the driver tests over the stand-in.** Create `crates/fake-tools/tests/ocr_driver.rs`:

```rust
//! The OCR worker's driver `tools::ocr::run_worker` against the stand-in (design parts 5.3, 10.7, 10.8; T5-R8). The
//! scenario sits beside the copied stand-in, so no environment variable is passed (S15). The records are made-up
//! sentinel words, never subtitle text.

use lazymkv_core::ipc::OutputStream;
use lazymkv_core::settings::Settings;
use lazymkv_core::testsupport::{Scratch, ScratchExt};
use lazymkv_engine::testkit::{ci_factor, BusyRetry};
use lazymkv_platform::fakes::FakeHost;
use lazymkv_platform::{GuardedChild, ProcessGuard, Spawn, StdProcessGuard};
use lazymkv_tools::ocr::{end_reason, ocr_args, run_worker, WorkerEnd};
use lazymkv_tools::{run_recorded, with_suffix, CancelToken, LineAction, Limits, ToolCtx};
use std::fs;
use std::io;
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::sync::{mpsc, Arc, Mutex};
use std::time::Duration;

const NOW: u64 = 1_790_000_000;
const SENTINEL: &str = "text-sentinel-3e8f";
const USAGE: &str = "usage: lazymkv-ocr <evidence.mks> --stream N --clear-max BYTES --out DIR";

/// The stand-in copied as `lazymkv-ocr`, answering from `lazymkv-ocr.json` beside it.
fn stand_in(dir: &Scratch, scenario: &str) -> PathBuf {
    let tool = dir.0.join(format!("lazymkv-ocr{}", std::env::consts::EXE_SUFFIX));
    fs::copy(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake-tool"), &tool).unwrap();
    dir.write("lazymkv-ocr.json", scenario);
    tool
}

/// A process runner that keeps a copy of every spawn and starts it through `BusyRetry(StdProcessGuard)`.
#[derive(Default)]
struct Recording(Mutex<Vec<Spawn>>);

impl ProcessGuard for Recording {
    fn spawn(&self, spawn: &Spawn) -> io::Result<Box<dyn GuardedChild>> {
        self.0.lock().unwrap().push(spawn.clone());
        BusyRetry(StdProcessGuard).spawn(spawn)
    }
}

/// B1 (the worker's folder)'s layout: `<work>/evidence.mks`, the output `<work>/s0/`, the capture `<work>/s0.capture.txt`.
struct Work {
    dir: PathBuf,
    args: Vec<String>,
    out: PathBuf,
    capture: PathBuf,
}

fn work(scratch: &Scratch) -> Work {
    let dir = scratch.0.join("work").join("ocr-job-title");
    let out = dir.join("s0");
    fs::create_dir_all(&out).unwrap();
    let args = ocr_args(&dir.join("evidence.mks"), 0, 64, &out);
    Work { capture: dir.join("s0.capture.txt"), dir, args, out }
}

/// Runs the worker on its own thread and waits up to 30 s, so a kill that regressed fails the test instead of hanging
/// it; the bound proves a kill and is not scaled. Gives the end and every line `on_output` got.
fn run(guard: Arc<Recording>, tool: PathBuf, work: &Work, cap: Duration, cancel: CancelToken) -> (WorkerEnd, Vec<String>) {
    let (args, capture) = (work.args.clone(), work.capture.clone());
    let (sender, receiver) = mpsc::channel();
    std::thread::spawn(move || {
        let host = FakeHost::new("2026-11-06", NOW);
        let limits = Limits::from_settings(&Settings::default());
        let seen = Mutex::new(Vec::new());
        let on_output = |_: OutputStream, line: &str| seen.lock().unwrap().push(line.to_string());
        let ctx = ToolCtx { guard: &*guard, host: &host, limits: &limits, cancel, on_output: &on_output, on_progress: &|_: f64| {} };
        let end = run_worker(&ctx, &tool, &args, &capture, cap).map_err(|error| error.to_string());
        let _ = sender.send((end, seen.into_inner().unwrap()));
    });
    let (end, seen) = receiver.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(30)).expect("run_worker did not return within 30 s");
    (end.unwrap(), seen)
}

/// The cap of a run that must end before it: a wait that only waits, so it scales.
fn long() -> Duration {
    Duration::from_secs(20) * ci_factor()
}

#[test]
fn the_worker_gets_rten_num_threads_3_and_below_normal_priority() {
    let dir = Scratch::new("ocr-env");
    let tool = stand_in(&dir, r#"{"responses":[{"args_contain":["--stream"]}]}"#);
    let work = work(&dir);
    let guard = Arc::new(Recording::default());
    let (end, _) = run(Arc::clone(&guard), tool.clone(), &work, long(), CancelToken::default());
    assert_eq!(end, WorkerEnd::Read);
    let spawns = guard.0.lock().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(spawns.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(spawns[0].program, tool);
    assert_eq!(spawns[0].args, work.args);
    assert_eq!(spawns[0].env, [("RTEN_NUM_THREADS".to_string(), "3".to_string())]);
    assert!(spawns[0].below_normal);
}

/// S43 and R3-worker-10: only the worker gets a variable; every driver of design part 5.3 runs through `run_recorded`.
#[test]
fn no_other_tool_gets_an_environment_variable() {
    let dir = Scratch::new("ocr-env-other");
    let tool = dir.0.join(format!("mkvmerge{}", std::env::consts::EXE_SUFFIX));
    fs::copy(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_fake-tool"), &tool).unwrap();
    dir.write("mkvmerge.json", r#"{"responses":[{"args_contain":["-J"],"stdout":"out.txt"}]}"#);
    dir.write("out.txt", "{}\n");
    let guard = Recording::default();
    let host = FakeHost::new("2026-11-06", NOW);
    let limits = Limits::from_settings(&Settings::default());
    let ctx = ToolCtx {
        guard: &guard,
        host: &host,
        limits: &limits,
        cancel: CancelToken::default(),
        on_output: &|_: OutputStream, _: &str| {},
        on_progress: &|_: f64| {},
    };
    let args = ["-J".to_string(), "title.mkv".to_string()];
    for below_normal in [false, true] {
        let out = dir.0.join(format!("ident-{below_normal}.json"));
        run_recorded(&ctx, &tool, &args, &out, None, below_normal, &mut |_| LineAction::Continue).unwrap();
    }
    let spawns = guard.0.lock().unwrap();
    let seen: Vec<(bool, bool)> = spawns.iter().map(|spawn| (spawn.env.is_empty(), spawn.below_normal)).collect();
    assert_eq!(seen, [(true, false), (true, true)]);
}

#[test]
fn a_worker_exit_3_is_refused_with_its_first_stderr_line() {
    let dir = Scratch::new("ocr-exit-3");

    dir.write("err.txt", "track 2 has a laced block at 12.345 s\r\nsecond line\n");

    assert_eq!(end, WorkerEnd::Refused("track 2 has a laced block at 12.345 s".to_string()));

}

    assert_eq!(end, WorkerEnd::Exited(Some(3)));

    dir.write("err.txt", &format!("{USAGE}\n"));
    let (end, _) = run(Arc::default(), tool, &work(&dir), long(), CancelToken::default());
    assert_eq!(end, WorkerEnd::ArgumentError(USAGE.to_string()));
    assert_eq!(end_reason(&end), Some(format!("lazymkv-ocr refused its arguments: {USAGE}")));

/// Review Focus 2's driver half: a panic's standard error can hold text, so neither the reason nor a callback quotes it.
#[test]
fn a_worker_exit_101_is_exited_and_quotes_no_stderr() {
    let dir = Scratch::new("ocr-exit-101");
    let tool = stand_in(&dir, r#"{"responses":[{"args_contain":["--stream"],"stderr":"err.txt","exit_code":101}]}"#);
    dir.write("err.txt", &format!("thread 'main' panicked at {SENTINEL}\n"));
    let (end, seen) = run(Arc::default(), tool, &work(&dir), long(), CancelToken::default());
    assert_eq!(end, WorkerEnd::Exited(Some(101)));
    let reason = end_reason(&end).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(reason, "lazymkv-ocr exited with code 101");
    assert!(!reason.contains(SENTINEL));
    assert!(seen.is_empty(), "{seen:?}");
}

/// The cap is unscaled: it is the kill under test, not a wait (Global Constraints, Tests).
#[test]
fn a_worker_past_its_cap_is_timed_out() {
    let dir = Scratch::new("ocr-cap");
    let tool = stand_in(&dir, r#"{"responses":[{"args_contain":["--stream"],"stdout":"out.txt","hang_after_line":0}]}"#);
    dir.write("out.txt", "never\n");
    let work = work(&dir);
    let (end, _) = run(Arc::default(), tool, &work, Duration::from_millis(200), CancelToken::default());
    assert_eq!(end, WorkerEnd::TimedOut);
    assert_eq!(end_reason(&end), None);
    let exit: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(with_suffix(&work.capture, ".exit.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert!(exit["elapsed_ms"].as_u64().unwrap() >= 200, "{exit}");
}

#[test]
fn a_cancelled_worker_is_cancelled() {
    let dir = Scratch::new("ocr-cancel");
    let tool = stand_in(&dir, r#"{"responses":[{"args_contain":["--stream"],"stdout":"out.txt","hang_after_line":0}]}"#);
    dir.write("out.txt", "never\n");
    let token = CancelToken::default();
    token.cancel();
    let (end, _) = run(Arc::default(), tool, &work(&dir), long(), token);
    assert_eq!(end, WorkerEnd::Cancelled);
}

/// T5-R57: the capture's four files sit at the capture's path, outside `--out`, which holds only what the worker wrote.
#[test]
fn the_capture_is_written_beside_its_path_and_not_in_out() {
    let dir = Scratch::new("ocr-capture");
    let tool = stand_in(
        &dir,
        r#"{"responses":[{"args_contain":["--stream"],"stdout":"out.txt","stderr":"err.txt",
            "creates":[{"dir_arg_from_end":1,"name":"sub-0.ocr.jsonl","copy_from":"records-s0.txt"}]}]}"#,
    );
    dir.write("out.txt", "event 1 of 1\n");
    dir.write("err.txt", "loaded\n");
    dir.write("records-s0.txt", &format!("{{\"pts\":1.0,\"size\":900,\"text\":\"{SENTINEL}\"}}\n"));
    let work = work(&dir);
    let (end, _) = run(Arc::default(), tool, &work, long(), CancelToken::default());
    assert_eq!(end, WorkerEnd::Read);
    let names = |folder: &PathBuf| {
        let mut names: Vec<String> =
            fs::read_dir(folder).unwrap().map(|entry| entry.unwrap().file_name().to_string_lossy().into_owned()).collect();
        names.sort();
        names
    };
    assert_eq!(names(&work.out), ["sub-0.ocr.jsonl"]);
    assert_eq!(
        names(&work.dir),
        ["s0", "s0.capture.txt", "s0.capture.txt.exit.json", "s0.capture.txt.stderr", "s0.capture.txt.timing.jsonl"]
    );
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(&work.capture).unwrap(), "event 1 of 1\n");
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(with_suffix(&work.capture, ".stderr")).unwrap(), "loaded\n");
}

/// Design part 10.12: the worker's lines are kept in its capture only, never handed to `ToolCtx::on_output`, which
/// the engine forwards to the IPC (inter-process communication) snapshot.
#[test]
fn the_workers_output_reaches_no_output_callback() {
    let dir = Scratch::new("ocr-quiet");
    let tool = stand_in(&dir, r#"{"responses":[{"args_contain":["--stream"],"stdout":"out.txt","stderr":"err.txt"}]}"#);
    dir.write("out.txt", &format!("{SENTINEL}\n"));
    dir.write("err.txt", &format!("{SENTINEL}\n"));
    let work = work(&dir);
    let (end, seen) = run(Arc::default(), tool, &work, long(), CancelToken::default());
    assert_eq!(end, WorkerEnd::Read);
    assert!(seen.is_empty(), "{seen:?}");
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(&work.capture).unwrap(), format!("{SENTINEL}\n"));
}
```

```rust
use lazymkv_core::ipc::OutputStream;

/// One English PGS track of 40 made-up events whose block widths differ, so each is a distinct crop the worker would
/// read: block shapes only, no glyph and no font (RP21).
fn cap_kill_evidence() -> Vec<u8> {
    let track = MksTrack {
        number: 1,
        kind: 17,
        codec_id: "S_HDMV/PGS".to_string(),
        codec_private: Vec::new(),
        language: "eng".to_string(),
        encoding: MksEncoding::None,
    };
    let blocks: Vec<MksBlock> = (0..40u32)
        .map(|i| {
            let set = pgs_display_set((1920, 1080), &[(0, 400, 900, 600 + 8 * i, 60, 1)], &[(1, [16, 128, 128, 255])]);
            MksBlock::new(1, i64::from(i) * 2_000, set)
        })
        .collect();
    mks(&[track], &blocks, &MksShape::default())
}

            on_progress: &|_: f64| {},
        };
        let _ = sender.send(run_worker(&ctx, &program, &args, &at, Duration::from_millis(1)).map_err(|e| e.to_string()));
    });
    // The bound proves the kill, so it is not scaled.
    let end = receiver.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(30)).expect("the worker was not killed within 30 s of a 1 ms cap");
    assert_eq!(end, Ok(WorkerEnd::TimedOut));
    assert!(with_suffix(&capture, ".exit.json").exists());
}
```

  The script `scripts/phase0/engine-ocr-trial.ps1 -Step inventory|read|rows|compare|f3 [-Row <k>] [-Slug <slug>] [-Label <label>] [-Stream <n>] [-Evidence <dir>]`, started through `scripts/phase0/job.sh`: `-Row` (1 to 6) is required for every step but `f3`; the row's slug, label and stream are read from `trial-tracks.txt`, and a `-Slug`, `-Label` or `-Stream` given (Task 12 gives them) must equal that line's, else the run stops; the log names rows, never a slug or a label; `compare -Row <k>` compares every row of row k's title and is refused for a row that is not its title's first (rows 4 and 5 run as `-Row 4`); `f3` is Task 12 Step 10's report. Its last line is `RESULT ok` or `RESULT FAILED: <reason>`.

The subcommands' contracts (exit 2 is an argument error through `usage_error(err, "ocr-trial <sub>", USAGE[i], message)`; any other refusal writes `lazymkv-dev ocr-trial <sub>: <message>` to `err` and exits 1; stdout holds counts, file base names and times only, never a folder path or subtitle text):
- `inventory`: one line `frames <f>, Tesseract records <t>, F reading <k records | none>, evidence.mks <b> bytes from <the dataset copy | the staging path summary.json names | the phase 0 staging layout>, events <m>; R' <run | not run>; F <exists | to run>` and exit 0; or one `missing: ...` line per gap (below) and exit 1. `--where FILE` writes the chosen `evidence.mks` path and `"\n"` to FILE.
- `read`: `events <m> cap <c> s` (`<c>` with one decimal), then the start, then `wall <w> s from the worker's start to its exit` (one decimal), on `Read` the line `run.json wall_ms <w> events <e> distinct <d> rows <r> detector <t1>/<t2>/<t3>/<t4> ms decode <a> prepare <b> lines <c> detect <d> recognize <r>` (each `ms` with one decimal), and last `end Read` (exit 0) or `end TimedOut: <cap_reason>`, `end Refused: <reason>`, `end ArgumentError: <end_reason>`, `end Exited: <end_reason>`, `end Cancelled`, `end not started: <error>` (exit 1).
- `rows`: the records file (one compact JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) object per frame and a last `{"summary": {...}}` line) and the one stdout line `rows: frames <f>, blank <b>, rows <r>, detector <t1>/<t2>/<t3>/<t4>, load_ms <l>, ms_total <t>, wall_ms <w>`.
- `f-records`: the records file in `sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl` form and `records <k>, with text <x>, with pts <p>`.
- `summary`: `<dir>\summary.json` and `summary: <k> streams`.
- `parity`: `Parity.lines`, then `Parity.differences`, then `PARITY PASS` (exit 0) or `PARITY FAIL: <k> differences` (exit 1); exit 2 when either arm's `subs_run` exits 2 (its stderr lines go to `err`, prefixed `F: ` or `R: `).

```rust
#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::testutil::{write, Scratch, ScratchExt};
    use lazymkv_core::recording::files::read_jsonl;
    use lazymkv_core::recording::py_fixed;
    use lazymkv_core::subtitle::bitmap::evidence::{run_json, EngineId, RunTotals, StageTotals};
    use lazymkv_core::subtitle::bitmap::prepare::Grey;
    use lazymkv_core::subtitle::text::{ocr_records, OcrRecord};
    use lazymkv_platform::{GuardedChild, Spawn};
    use lazymkv_tools::ocr::ocr_args;
    use serde_json::{json, Value};
    use std::collections::BTreeMap;
    use std::fs;
    use std::io;
    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
    use std::sync::Mutex;

    /// Made-up words: no real subtitle text (RP21).
    const WORDS: [&str; 11] = ["babin", "dagon", "gikol", "kubal", "lodin", "bekan", "dulog", "gamin", "kodel", "labun", "bodig"];

    /// Event k's lines: a made-up sentence, and a sound cue as event 5 (as `subs`' tests).
    fn lines_of(k: usize) -> Vec<String> {
        if k == 5 {
            return vec!["(DOOR SLAMS)".to_string()];
        }
        vec![format!("We {} the {} and the {}.", WORDS[k % 11], WORDS[(3 * k + 1) % 11], WORDS[(7 * k + 2) % 11])]
    }

    fn path(p: &Path) -> String {
        p.display().to_string()
    }

    fn strings(words: &[&str]) -> Vec<String> {
        words.iter().map(|word| word.to_string()).collect()
    }

    /// (exit code, stdout, stderr) of `lazymkv-dev ocr-trial <args>` through the command table.
    fn trial(s: &Scratch, args: &[String]) -> (i32, String, String) {
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&s.0);
        let mut argv = vec!["ocr-trial".to_string()];
        argv.extend(args.iter().cloned());
        let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let code = crate::dispatch(&ctx, &argv, &mut out, &mut err);
        (code, String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(err).unwrap())
    }

    /// sub-<n>.packets.json of `events` displayed events, 4 s apart from 10 s, each followed by a 30-byte clear.
    fn packets(events: usize) -> String {
        let mut list = Vec::new();
        for k in 0..events {
            let start = 10.0 + 4.0 * k as f64;
            list.push(json!({"pts_time": py_fixed(start, 3), "duration_time": "2.500", "size": "4000"}));
            list.push(json!({"pts_time": py_fixed(start + 2.5, 3), "duration_time": "0.021", "size": "30"}));
        }
        json!({ "packets": list }).to_string()
    }

    /// The recording rec/disc-a/all-tracks: subs/index.json with one "HDMV PGS" stream per (n, language), each with
    /// 30 events in its packet list.
    fn recording(s: &Scratch, streams: &[(i64, &str)]) -> PathBuf {
        let rec = s.0.join("rec/disc-a/all-tracks");
        let index: Vec<Value> = streams
            .iter()
            .map(|(n, language)| json!({"n": n, "track_id": 3 + n, "language": language, "codec": "HDMV PGS",
                "track_name": null, "forced": false, "default": false}))
            .collect();
        write(&rec.join("subs/index.json"), Value::Array(index).to_string());
        for (n, _) in streams {
            write(&rec.join(format!("subs/sub-{n}.packets.json")), packets(30));
        }
        rec
    }

    /// `dir`/sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl for `recording`'s 30 events, event k read as `lines_of(k)` or as `edit`'s lines for
    /// its event, each record at its packet's pts.
    fn records(dir: &Path, n: i64, edit: Option<(usize, &[&str])>) {
        let mut text = String::new();
        for k in 0..30usize {
            let pts = 10.0 + 4.0 * k as f64;
            let lines: Vec<String> = match edit {
                Some((at, lines)) if at == k => strings(lines),
                _ => lines_of(k),
            };
            let file = format!("f-{:09}.png", (pts * 1000.0) as u64);
            text.push_str(&json!({"frame": k, "file": file, "t": pts, "pts": pts, "lines": lines}).to_string());
            text.push('\n');
        }
        write(&dir.join(format!("sub-{n}.ocr.jsonl")), text);
    }

    #[derive(Clone, Copy)]
    struct Inputs {
        frames: usize,
        tesseract: bool,
        f: bool,
        dataset_evidence: bool,
        packets: bool,
    }

    const FULL: Inputs = Inputs { frames: 3, tesseract: true, f: false, dataset_evidence: true, packets: true };

    /// The trial's made-up inputs for stream 0: `recording`'s rec/disc-a/all-tracks, and in the dataset folder
    /// data/disc-a/all-tracks/subs-ocr/ `frames` files s0/f-<k:08>.png, the Tesseract reading sub-0.ocr.jsonl (3
    /// records), arm F's ocrs-s0.jsonl (3 records and a summary line) and a 100-byte evidence.mks, as `i` asks.
    /// Returns (rec, text).
    fn inputs(s: &Scratch, i: Inputs) -> (PathBuf, PathBuf) {
        let rec = recording(s, &[(0, "eng")]);
        if !i.packets {
            fs::remove_file(rec.join("subs/sub-0.packets.json")).unwrap();
        }
        let text = s.0.join("data/disc-a/all-tracks/subs-ocr");
        fs::create_dir_all(&text).unwrap();
        for k in 0..i.frames {
            write(&text.join(format!("s0/f-{k:08}.png")), "png");
        }
        let record = |k: usize| format!("{{\"frame\": {k}, \"file\": \"f-{k:08}.png\", \"lines\": []}}\n");
        if i.tesseract {
            write(&text.join("sub-0.ocr.jsonl"), (0..3).map(record).collect::<String>());
        }
        if i.f {
            write(&text.join("ocrs-s0.jsonl"), (0..3).map(record).collect::<String>() + "{\"summary\": {\"frames\": 3}}\n");
        }
        if i.dataset_evidence {
            write(&text.join("evidence.mks"), [0u8; 100]);
        }
        (rec, text)
    }

    fn inventory(s: &Scratch, rec: &Path, text: &Path, more: &[&str]) -> (i32, String, String) {
        let staging = path(&s.0.join("staging"));
        let mut args = strings(&["inventory", "--rec", &path(rec), "--text", &path(text), "--stream", "0", "--staging", &staging]);
        args.extend(strings(more));
        trial(s, &args)
    }

    #[test]
    fn inventory_stops_on_a_missing_tesseract_reading_evidence_or_packet_list() {
        for (case, want) in [
            (Inputs { tesseract: false, ..FULL }, "missing: sub-0.ocr.jsonl (the Tesseract reading)"),
            (
                Inputs { dataset_evidence: false, ..FULL },
                "missing: evidence.mks (no dataset copy, no path in summary.json, none in the phase 0 staging layout)",
            ),
            (Inputs { packets: false, ..FULL }, "missing: subs/sub-0.packets.json (the packet list)"),
        ] {
            let s = Scratch::new("trial-inventory-missing");
            let (rec, text) = inputs(&s, case);
            let (code, out, err) = inventory(&s, &rec, &text, &[]);
            assert_eq!(code, 1, "{out}{err}");
            assert!(out.lines().any(|line| line == want), "{out}");
            assert!(!out.contains(&path(&s.0)), "the inventory prints no folder path: {out}");
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn inventory_reports_r_prime_not_run_without_frames() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-inventory-no-frames");
        let (rec, text) = inputs(&s, Inputs { frames: 0, f: true, ..FULL });
        let (code, out, err) = inventory(&s, &rec, &text, &[]);
        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (0, ""));
        assert_eq!(
            out,
            "frames 0, Tesseract records 3, F reading 3 records, evidence.mks 100 bytes from the dataset copy, \
             events 30; R' not run; F exists\n"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn inventory_stops_when_neither_frames_nor_an_f_reading_exist() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-inventory-no-arm-f");
        let (rec, text) = inputs(&s, Inputs { frames: 0, f: false, ..FULL });
        let (code, out, _) = inventory(&s, &rec, &text, &[]);
        assert_eq!(code, 1);
        assert!(out.lines().any(|line| line == "missing: s0/f-*.png and ocrs-s0.jsonl (parity cannot be judged on this track)"), "{out}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn inventory_takes_evidence_from_the_staging_folder_when_summary_json_names_none() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-inventory-staging");
        let (rec, text) = inputs(&s, Inputs { dataset_evidence: false, ..FULL });
        write(&rec.join("subs-ocr/summary.json"), "\u{feff}{\"slug\": \"disc-a\", \"streams\": []}\r\n");
        let staged = s.0.join("staging/disc-a/all-tracks/evidence.mks");
        write(&staged, [0u8; 250]);
        let where_file = path(&s.0.join("where.txt"));
        let (code, out, _) = inventory(&s, &rec, &text, &["--where", &where_file]);
        assert_eq!(code, 0, "{out}");
        assert!(out.contains(", evidence.mks 250 bytes from the phase 0 staging layout, "), "{out}");
        assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(&where_file).unwrap(), format!("{}\n", path(&staged)));
    }

    #[test]
    fn inventory_prefers_the_dataset_copy_then_the_path_summary_json_names() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-inventory-order");
        let (rec, text) = inputs(&s, FULL);
        let named = s.0.join("elsewhere/evidence.mks");
        write(&named, [0u8; 180]);
        write(&s.0.join("staging/disc-a/all-tracks/evidence.mks"), [0u8; 250]);
        write(&rec.join("subs-ocr/summary.json"), json!({"evidence": path(&named), "streams": []}).to_string());
        let (_, out, _) = inventory(&s, &rec, &text, &[]);
        assert!(out.contains(", evidence.mks 100 bytes from the dataset copy, "), "{out}");
        fs::remove_file(text.join("evidence.mks")).unwrap();
        let (_, out, _) = inventory(&s, &rec, &text, &[]);
        assert!(out.contains(", evidence.mks 180 bytes from the staging path summary.json names, "), "{out}");
    }

    /// Keeps each Spawn and starts nothing, so a test sees what arm R would start.
    struct Recorder(Mutex<Vec<Spawn>>);

    impl ProcessGuard for Recorder {
        fn spawn(&self, spawn: &Spawn) -> io::Result<Box<dyn GuardedChild>> {
            self.0.lock().unwrap().push(spawn.clone());
            Err(io::Error::other("recorded, not started"))
        }
    }

    fn read_args(s: &Scratch) -> Vec<String> {
        strings(&[
            &path(&s.0.join("evidence.mks")), "--stream", "0", "--clear-max", "64",
            "--packets", &path(&s.0.join("sub-0.packets.json")), "--out", &path(&s.0.join("r")),
        ])
    }

    #[test]
    fn read_starts_the_sibling_worker_below_normal_with_rten_num_threads_3_and_the_fixed_cap() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-read-spawn");
        s.write("evidence.mks", [0u8; 16]);
        s.write("sub-0.packets.json", packets(887));
        let guard = Recorder(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let code = read_with(&guard, &ClockHost, &read_args(&s), &mut out, &mut err);
        let out = String::from_utf8(out).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(code, 1, "{out}");
        assert!(out.starts_with("events 887 cap 1800.6 s\n"), "{out}");
        let last = out.lines().last().unwrap();
        assert!(last.starts_with("end not started: ") && last.contains("recorded, not started"), "{out}");
        let spawned = guard.0.lock().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(spawned.len(), 1);
        let worker = std::env::current_exe().unwrap().with_file_name(format!("lazymkv-ocr{}", std::env::consts::EXE_SUFFIX));
        assert_eq!(spawned[0].program, worker);
        assert_eq!(spawned[0].args, ocr_args(&s.0.join("evidence.mks"), 0, 64, &s.0.join("r")));
        assert_eq!(spawned[0].env, vec![("RTEN_NUM_THREADS".to_string(), "3".to_string())]);
        assert!(spawned[0].below_normal);
        assert!(s.0.join("r").is_dir(), "read makes --out before the start");
    }

    #[test]
    fn read_refuses_an_out_folder_that_already_holds_a_file() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-read-not-empty");
        s.write("evidence.mks", [0u8; 16]);
        s.write("sub-0.packets.json", packets(3));
        s.write("r/sub-0.ocr.jsonl", "");
        let guard = Recorder(Mutex::new(Vec::new()));
        let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        assert_eq!(read_with(&guard, &ClockHost, &read_args(&s), &mut out, &mut err), 1);
        assert_eq!(
            String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(),
            "end not started: --out already holds files; the trial reads each track once, into an empty folder\n"
        );
        assert!(guard.0.lock().unwrap().is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn rows_reads_made_up_block_frames_into_records() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-rows");
        let white = Grey { width: 1280, height: 720, pixels: vec![255; 1280 * 720] };
        let mut block = white.clone();
        for y in 600..640usize {
            for x in 440..840usize {
                block.pixels[y * 1280 + x] = 0;
            }
        }
        for (k, frame) in [&white, &block, &block].into_iter().enumerate() {
            write(&s.0.join(format!("frames/f-{k:08}.png")), lazymkv_ocr::grey_png(frame).unwrap());
        }
        let out_file = s.0.join("rows-s0.jsonl");
        let (code, out, err) = trial(&s, &strings(&["rows", &path(&s.0.join("frames")), "--out", &path(&out_file)]));
        assert_eq!(code, 0, "{err}");
        assert!(out.starts_with("rows: frames 3, blank 1, "), "{out}");
        let lines: Vec<Value> =
            fs::read_to_string(&out_file).unwrap().lines().map(|line| serde_json::from_str(line).unwrap()).collect();
        assert_eq!(lines.len(), 4);
        assert_eq!((&lines[0]["frame"], &lines[0]["file"]), (&json!(0), &json!("f-00000000.png")));
        assert_eq!((&lines[0]["lines"], &lines[0]["method"]), (&json!([]), &Value::Null));
        for k in 1..3 {
            assert_eq!(lines[k]["frame"], json!(k));
            assert!(lines[k]["lines"].is_array());
            assert!(matches!(lines[k]["method"].as_str(), Some("rows") | Some("detector")), "{}", lines[k]["method"]);
            assert!(lines[k]["ms"]["recognize"].is_number());
        }
        let summary = &lines[3]["summary"];
        assert_eq!((summary["frames"].as_u64(), summary["blank"].as_u64()), (Some(3), Some(1)));
    }

    /// sub-0.frames.json as ocr-subs.ps1 writes it in Windows PowerShell 5.1: a byte order mark and CRLF line ends.
    fn frames_json(rec: &Path, entries: &[Value]) {
        let body: Vec<String> = entries.iter().map(Value::to_string).collect();
        write(&rec.join("subs-ocr/sub-0.frames.json"), format!("\u{feff}[\r\n{}\r\n]\r\n", body.join(",\r\n")));
    }

    /// Arm F's per-frame records as ocrs-trial writes them: no time, a last summary line.
    const F_INPUT: &str = "{\"frame\": 0, \"file\": \"f-00000000.png\", \"lines\": [], \"ms\": 10}\n\
        {\"frame\": 1, \"file\": \"f-00000001.png\", \"lines\": [\"We babin the dagon.\"], \"ms\": 12}\n\
        {\"summary\": {\"frames\": 2}}\n";

    fn f_records(s: &Scratch, rec: &Path) -> (i32, String, String) {
        s.write("ocrs-s0.jsonl", F_INPUT);
        let (input, output) = (path(&s.0.join("ocrs-s0.jsonl")), path(&s.0.join("f/sub-0.ocr.jsonl")));
        trial(s, &strings(&["f-records", "--rec", &path(rec), "--stream", "0", "--in", &input, "--out", &output]))
    }

    #[test]
    fn f_records_take_pts_and_t_from_frames_json_by_frame_number() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-f-records");
        let rec = s.0.join("rec/disc-a/all-tracks");
        frames_json(&rec, &[
            json!({"frame": 1, "file": "f-00000001.png", "t": 0.5, "pts": 61.603, "chars": 16, "lines": 1}),
            json!({"frame": 0, "file": "f-00000000.png", "t": 0.25, "pts": 61.353, "chars": 0, "lines": 0}),
        ]);
        let (code, out, err) = f_records(&s, &rec);
        assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (0, "records 2, with text 1, with pts 2\n"), "{err}");
        assert_eq!(
            fs::read_to_string(s.0.join("f/sub-0.ocr.jsonl")).unwrap(),
            [
                r#"{"frame":0,"file":"f-00000000.png","t":0.25,"pts":61.353,"lines":[]}"#,
                r#"{"frame":1,"file":"f-00000001.png","t":0.5,"pts":61.603,"lines":["We babin the dagon."]}"#,
                "",
            ]
            .join("\n")
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn f_records_from_a_frames_json_without_pts_keep_t_for_the_proof_of_concept_pairing() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-f-records-poc");
        let rec = s.0.join("rec/disc-a/all-tracks");
        frames_json(&rec, &[json!({"frame": 0, "t": 0.25, "lines": 0}), json!({"frame": 1, "t": 0.5, "lines": 1})]);
        let (code, out, _) = f_records(&s, &rec);
        assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (0, "records 2, with text 1, with pts 0\n"));
        let text = fs::read_to_string(s.0.join("f/sub-0.ocr.jsonl")).unwrap();
        assert!(!text.contains("\"pts\""), "{text}");
        assert_eq!(
            ocr_records(&read_jsonl(&text).unwrap(), &BTreeMap::new()).unwrap(),
            vec![OcrRecord { t: 0.5, pts: false, lines: vec!["We babin the dagon.".to_string()] }]
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn f_records_stop_on_a_frame_with_neither_t_nor_pts_or_one_frames_json_lacks() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-f-records-stop");
        let rec = s.0.join("rec/disc-a/all-tracks");
        frames_json(&rec, &[json!({"frame": 0, "t": 0.25, "lines": 0}), json!({"frame": 1, "lines": 1})]);
        let (code, _, err) = f_records(&s, &rec);
        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (1, "lazymkv-dev ocr-trial f-records: frame 1 has neither t nor pts in sub-0.frames.json\n"));
        assert!(!s.0.join("f/sub-0.ocr.jsonl").exists());
        frames_json(&rec, &[json!({"frame": 0, "t": 0.25, "lines": 0})]);
        let (code, _, err) = f_records(&s, &rec);
        assert_eq!((code, err.as_str()), (1, "lazymkv-dev ocr-trial f-records: frame 1 is not in sub-0.frames.json\n"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn summary_lists_each_read_stream_with_counts_and_no_text() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-summary");
        let rec = recording(&s, &[(0, "eng")]);
        let totals = RunTotals {
            events: 2,
            distinct: 2,
            rows: 2,
            detector: [0; 4],
            ms: StageTotals { decode: 1.0, prepare: 1.0, lines: 1.0, detect: 0.0, recognize: 5.0 },
            engine: EngineId { ocrs: "0.13.1".to_string(), detection_sha256: "d".repeat(64), recognition_sha256: "e".repeat(64) },
            wall_ms: 900,
        };
        s.write("engine/sub-0.run.json", run_json(&totals));
        s.write(
            "engine/sub-0.ocr.jsonl",
            "{\"frame\":0,\"file\":\"f-000010000.png\",\"t\":10.0,\"pts\":10.0,\"text\":\"text-sentinel-3e8f\",\"lines\":[\"text-sentinel-3e8f\"],\"size\":4000}\n\
             {\"frame\":1,\"file\":\"f-000014000.png\",\"t\":14.0,\"pts\":14.0,\"text\":\"\",\"lines\":[],\"size\":4000}\n",
        );
        let (code, out, err) = trial(&s, &strings(&["summary", "--dir", &path(&s.0.join("engine")), "--rec", &path(&rec)]));
        assert_eq!((code, out.as_str()), (0, "summary: 1 streams\n"), "{err}");
        let text = fs::read_to_string(s.0.join("engine/summary.json")).unwrap();
        assert!(!text.contains("text-sentinel-3e8f"), "{text}");
        assert!(text.ends_with("}\n"));
        let summary: Value = serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap();
        let stream = &summary["streams"][0];
        assert_eq!((&stream["n"], &stream["codec"], &stream["read"]), (&json!(0), &json!("HDMV PGS"), &json!(true)));
        assert_eq!((&stream["with_text"], &stream["exit"], &stream["wall_ms"]), (&json!(1), &json!(0), &json!(900)));
    }

    fn measures(run: &SubsRun, at: usize) -> &lazymkv_core::subtitle::text::Measures {
        &run.tracks[at].measured.as_ref().expect("the stream is measured").m
    }

    #[test]
    fn parity_passes_on_equal_arms_and_fails_when_one_count_differs() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-parity-count");
        let rec = recording(&s, &[(0, "eng")]);
        let (f_dir, r_dir) = (s.0.join("f"), s.0.join("r"));
        records(&f_dir, 0, None);
        records(&r_dir, 0, None);
        let args = strings(&["parity", "--rec", &path(&rec), "--f", &path(&f_dir), "--r", &path(&r_dir)]);
        let (code, out, err) = trial(&s, &args);
        assert_eq!(code, 0, "{out}{err}");
        assert!(out.ends_with("PARITY PASS\n"), "{out}");
        // Arm R reads event 5's sound cue as dialogue.
        records(&r_dir, 0, Some((5, &["We babin the dagon."])));
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&s.0);
        let f = arm(&ctx, &path(&rec), &path(&f_dir));
        let r = arm(&ctx, &path(&rec), &path(&r_dir));
        let (fm, rm) = (measures(&f, 0), measures(&r, 0));
        assert_ne!(fm.SO, rm.SO);
        let found = parity(&f, &r, &Rule::default()).unwrap();
        assert!(found.differences.contains(&format!("s0: SO F {} R {}", fm.SO, rm.SO)), "{:?}", found.differences);
        let (code, out, _) = trial(&s, &args);
        assert_eq!(code, 1);
        assert!(out.ends_with(&format!("PARITY FAIL: {} differences\n", found.differences.len())), "{out}");
        assert!(!out.contains("babin") && !out.contains(&path(&s.0)), "parity prints numbers only: {out}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn parity_fails_when_a_stopword_share_crosses_its_threshold() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-parity-share");
        let rec = recording(&s, &[(0, "eng")]);
        records(&s.0.join("f"), 0, None);
        records(&s.0.join("r"), 0, None);
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&s.0);
        let mut f = arm(&ctx, &path(&rec), &path(&s.0.join("f")));
        let mut r = arm(&ctx, &path(&rec), &path(&s.0.join("r")));
        let share = |run: &mut SubsRun, x: f64| run.tracks[0].measured.as_mut().unwrap().m.shares.insert("en".to_string(), x);
        share(&mut f, 0.21);
        share(&mut r, 0.19);
        assert_eq!(
            parity(&f, &r, &Rule::default()).unwrap().differences,
            vec!["s0: share en F 0.210 R 0.190 on two sides of 0.200".to_string()]
        );
        share(&mut r, 0.25);
        assert!(parity(&f, &r, &Rule::default()).unwrap().differences.is_empty());
    }

    #[test]
    fn parity_fails_when_a_cb_direction_changes_band() {
        let s = Scratch::new("trial-parity-cb");
        let rec = recording(&s, &[(0, "eng"), (1, "spa")]);
        for (dir, n) in [("f", 0), ("f", 1), ("r", 0), ("r", 1)] {
            records(&s.0.join(dir), n, None);
        }
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&s.0);
        let mut f = arm(&ctx, &path(&rec), &path(&s.0.join("f")));
        let mut r = arm(&ctx, &path(&rec), &path(&s.0.join("r")));
        assert_eq!(f.analysis.as_ref().unwrap().pairs.len(), 1);
        f.analysis.as_mut().unwrap().pairs[0].pair.cb = (Some(0.65), Some(0.55));
        r.analysis.as_mut().unwrap().pairs[0].pair.cb = (Some(0.55), Some(0.55));
        assert_eq!(
            parity(&f, &r, &Rule::default()).unwrap().differences,
            vec!["pair s0 s1: CB s0 in s1 F 0.650 R 0.550 on two sides of 0.600".to_string()]
        );
    }
}
```
