### Task 15: Step 10's OCR runs, the time cap and the unread streams (design 10.2 steps 3 to 5, 10.7, 10.8; B1 (the worker's folder); call 18; T5-R4, T5-R8 to T5-R12, T5-R35, T5-R48, T5-R51, T5-R55, T5-R57 to T5-R59)

The engine starts the OCR (optical character recognition) worker `lazymkv-ocr` once for each English or no-language bitmap subtitle stream of a title that needs step 10, one stream at a time, in a local work folder under the data folder, moves what a read stream wrote into the staged tuning folder through the checked copy, writes the counts into the job folder, and decides with the text; a stream that passes its cap, is refused, crashes or disagrees with ffprobe is unread, gets the note `subtitle_text_unread` and leaves no text behind. Decide's S32 refusal goes.

**Tier and risk:** opus (integration and judgment: the engine, dev's readers, the stand-in and six scenarios meet here); risk high: S32 goes, so every two-stream disc now decides; subtitle text must reach no job folder, log, note or IPC (inter-process communication) snapshot (design 10.12); and the worker is killed and its output moved across volumes.

**Covers:** R1-evidence-18, 19 (subs-ocr), 22, 30; R2-decoders-12, 14, 46, 47, 48, 50, 61, 63 (the engine's subtitles section), 65, 66, 70; R3-worker-5 (other codes), 9, 11 to 20, 22 to 28, 38, 39, 40, 60 (the cap seam), 64; R4-commands-63, 64; R5-code-18, 20 (the S32 test), 31 (subtitles), 35, 39 to 44, 78; R6-phase0-14, 45, 46; Review Focus 2 and 3 (the Review Focus 3 test of a torn move is Task 18's).

Precondition: Task 14 is committed, pushed and green (CI, continuous integration, on three systems; CodeQL at 0). This task edits no `Cargo.toml` and no `Cargo.lock`, and nothing under `crates/core/src/subtitle/bitmap/`, `crates/ocr/`, `crates/ocr-models/` or `crates/tools/src/ocr.rs` (frozen from the trial's build on, T5-R54).

The rules this task pins, each from its source:
- **Which streams** (T5-R11, design 10.2 step 3): every entry of the title's `subs\index.json` whose language is `eng`, `en`, `und`, empty or absent and whose codec is not a text codec (`core::subtitle::text::is_text_codec`), in index order. A text stream is never given to the worker and gets no note (spec 8.7 sets it aside); a bitmap codec other than PGS (Presentation Graphic Stream) or VobSub goes to the worker, which refuses it with exit 3.
- **Where** (B1 (the worker's folder), T5-R4, T5-R57): the title's work folder is `<data>\work\ocr-<job id>-<title key>\` (Task 14's `work_dir(work_root, "ocr", job_id, key)`), holding `evidence.mks` (copied from `<staging>\<job id>\evidence\<title key>.mks` with `copy_checked`), each run's output folder `s<n>\` given as `--out`, and each run's capture `s<n>.capture.txt` with its `.stderr`, `.timing.jsonl` and `.exit.json`. The read output lands in `<staging>\<job id>\tuning\<title key>\subs-ocr\`; the counts (`sub-<n>.frames.json`, `summary.json`) in the job folder's `<title key>\subs-ocr\`. No capture file and no text reaches the job folder. The work folder is deleted when the title's runs end, and `<data>\work\` at engine start.
- **The cap** (design 10.8, call 6, T5-R9, T5-R10, T5-R58): `cap(events)` seconds, `events` the packets of `<title key>\subs\sub-<n>.packets.json` larger than the job's `sub_clear_max_bytes`; the engine's `cap` is `time_cap_s(events)` unless `EngineConfig.ocr_cap_override` is set, which only the testkit harness sets. A killed run's reason is `cap_reason(cap_s, k, events)`, `k` the whole lines of its `sub-<n>.ocr.jsonl` read before its folder is deleted.
- **How a run ends** (T5-R8, call 5): exit 0 and the cross-check `check_events` passing is read; exit 3 is unread with the first standard error line (Task 9's `WorkerEnd::Refused`); exit 2 fails the step with `lazymkv-ocr refused its arguments: <line>`; any other code is unread with `lazymkv-ocr exited with code <c>`, a run with no code with `lazymkv-ocr ended without an exit code`, and no standard error is quoted; a cancel kills the worker, deletes the title's work folder and ends as `cancelled by the owner`; a worker that is not beside the engine fails the step with `OCR_MISSING`.
- **The order** (T5-R12, design 10.2 step 5): each read stream's files are moved into the staged `subs-ocr\` after its run; once every run has ended, `summary.json` is written into the job folder through `write_atomic` and then copied into the staged `subs-ocr\` with `copy_checked`, the staged copy last, since Task 18's C3 reads it as the folder's completeness marker.
- **The threshold** (T5-R59): the job's own `sub_clear_max_bytes` goes to the worker (`--clear-max`), to `check_events`, to the cap's event count and to the text rule's subtitles section (`subtitle_section`'s `clear_max`).

/// T5-R48: a response may name files to create before its first line; without the key it creates none first.
#[test]
fn creates_first_parses_and_defaults_to_none() {
    let scenario: Scenario = serde_json::from_str(
        r#"{"responses":[
            {"args_contain":["--stream"],"hang_after_line":0,
             "creates_first":[{"dir_arg_from_end":1,"name":"sub-0.ocr.jsonl","copy_from":"records.txt"}]},
            {"args_contain":["-J"]}
        ]}"#,
    )
    .unwrap();
    assert_eq!(scenario.responses[0].creates_first.len(), 1);
    assert_eq!(scenario.responses[0].creates_first[0].name.as_deref(), Some("sub-0.ocr.jsonl"));
    assert!(scenario.responses[0].creates.is_empty());
    assert!(scenario.responses[1].creates_first.is_empty());
}

In `crates/fake-tools/tests/replay.rs`, after `a_hanging_run_sleeps_until_killed` (add `use lazymkv_engine::testkit::ci_factor;` and `use std::time::Instant;`):

```rust
/// T5-R48: the files a response creates first exist while it hangs, so a stand-in worker can be killed after writing
/// its records. The wait for the file scales by ci_factor; the 150 ms check that it still runs is the hang test's.
#[test]
fn files_created_first_exist_while_the_run_hangs() {
    let dir = Scratch::new("fake-first");
    let tool = stand_in(&dir.0, "lazymkv-ocr");
    dir.write(
        "lazymkv-ocr.json",
        r#"{"responses":[{"args_contain":["--stream"],"hang_after_line":0,
            "creates_first":[{"dir_arg_from_end":1,"name":"sub-0.ocr.jsonl","copy_from":"records.txt"}]}]}"#,
    );
    dir.write("records.txt", "{\"pts\":1.0,\"size\":900}\n");
    let out = dir.0.join("out");
    let mut child = retry_busy(|| {
        Command::new(&tool)
            .args(["evidence.mks", "--stream", "0", "--clear-max", "64", "--out", out.to_str().unwrap()])
            .env_remove("LAZYMKV_FAKE_DIR")
            .spawn()
    })
    .unwrap();
    let file = out.join("sub-0.ocr.jsonl");
    let deadline = Instant::now() + Duration::from_secs(10) * ci_factor();
    while !file.is_file() {
        assert!(Instant::now() < deadline, "sub-0.ocr.jsonl was not created within 10 s");
        std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(20));
    }
    std::thread::sleep(Duration::from_millis(150) * ci_factor());
    assert!(child.try_wait().unwrap().is_none(), "the stand-in exited before it was killed");
    child.kill().unwrap();
    child.wait().unwrap();

The helpers, after `no_token`:

```rust
/// The made-up word of every stand-in record and of the panicking stand-in's standard error (RP21: never subtitle text).
const SENTINEL: &str = "text-sentinel-3e8f";
/// The refused stand-in's first standard error line, the reason its exit 3 gives (T5-R8).
const REFUSAL: &str = "content encoding 3 of track 3 is not zlib compression or header stripping";
/// The cap scenarios with the harness's override of 2 s (T5-R58).
const CAP: [&str; 2] = ["movie-direct-two-subs-cap", "movie-direct-two-subs-cap-2s"];

/// movie-direct with `movie-direct-two-subs` and `overlays` copied over it.
fn two_subs(overlays: &[&str], settings: Value) -> Harness {
    let mut variants = vec!["movie-direct-two-subs"];
    variants.extend_from_slice(overlays);
    harness(&variants, settings)
}

fn job_id(h: &Harness) -> String {
    format!("{}-1", h.fingerprint("movie-direct").to_ascii_lowercase())
}

/// Inserts the disc and stops the engine once the job's DecisionDone is persisted, before its actions run.
fn decided(h: &Harness) -> String {
    h.insert("tok0", "movie-direct");
    h.run_until_event("DecisionDone", |event| matches!(event, Event::DecisionDone { .. }));
    job_id(h)
}

/// A file at the final path holds the job with path_collision, so it waits in NeedsReview with its engine running.
fn held(h: &Harness) -> String {
    let target = final_path(h);
    fs::create_dir_all(target.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
    fs::write(&target, b"already here").unwrap();
    run_to(h, "NeedsReview")
}

/// `<staging>/<job id>/tuning/<key>/subs-ocr`, where the text lives (design part 10.12 item 1).
fn staged_ocr(h: &Harness, id: &str) -> PathBuf {
    h.staging().join(id).join("tuning").join(KEY).join("subs-ocr")
}

/// `<data>/work/ocr-<job id>-<key>`, the title's work folder (B1 (the worker's folder), T5-R4).
fn work_of(h: &Harness, id: &str) -> PathBuf {
    h.data().join("work").join(format!("ocr-{id}-{KEY}"))
}

fn unread_notes(h: &Harness, id: &str) -> Vec<Noted> {
    let decision = h.record(id).titles[0].decision.clone().expect("the title was decided");
    decision.notes.into_iter().filter(|noted| noted.note == Note::SubtitleTextUnread).collect()
}

fn unread(stream: u32, reason: &str) -> Noted {
    Noted { note: Note::SubtitleTextUnread, stream: Some(stream), detail: format!("stream {stream} was not read: {reason}") }
}

/// The reason of a run killed at the cap scenarios' override after `read` of its 10 events.
fn cap_reason_of(read: usize) -> String {
    let cap = 2.0 * f64::from(ci_factor());
    format!("time cap of {cap:.1} s reached after {read} of 10 events")
}

/// Every file under `dir` whose bytes hold `needle`.
fn holding(dir: &Path, needle: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    let found = |name: &String| fs::read(dir.join(name)).unwrap().windows(needle.len()).any(|w| w == needle.as_bytes());
    files_under(dir).into_iter().filter(found).collect()
}

fn ocr_spawns(h: &Harness) -> Vec<Spawn> {
    h.spawns().into_iter().filter(|spawn| spawn.program.file_stem().is_some_and(|stem| stem == "lazymkv-ocr")).collect()
}

fn replay_files(dir: &Path) -> PlanOptions {
    PlanOptions {
        settings: Some(dir.join("settings.json")),
        tmdb_search: Some(dir.join("tmdb-search.json")),
        tmdb_record: Some(dir.join("tmdb-record.json")),
        remembered: None,
    }
}

/// `lazymkv-dev decide`'s inputs over the finished job folder, with `text` as its `--text`.
fn read_back(h: &Harness, id: &str, text: Option<&Path>) -> DecideInputs {
    let dir = h.job_dir(id);
    let ctx = Ctx::for_test(h.data());
    let (rec, label) = rec_folder(&ctx, &dir.join(KEY).display().to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|r| panic!("{}", r.line));
    read_decide_inputs(&ctx, &rec, &label, text, None, &replay_files(&dir)).unwrap_or_else(|r| panic!("{}", r.line))
}

fn set(names: &[&str]) -> BTreeSet<String> {
    names.iter().map(|name| name.to_string()).collect()
}
```

The S32 test at `:353-361` is replaced by the first of these tests; the rest follow it:

```rust
/// Design part 10.2 steps 3 to 5 (S32 removed): both English PGS streams are read, their text and crops land in the
/// staged folder, the counts in the job folder, and decide's subtitles section is the text rule's.
#[test]
fn two_english_subtitle_streams_are_read_by_the_worker_and_decided_with_their_text() {
    let h = two_subs(&[], json!({}));
    let id = held(&h);
    let label = h.job_dir(&id).join(KEY);
    let doc = json_of(&label.join("decide.json"));
    assert_eq!(doc["subtitles"]["reading"], json!("subs-ocr"));
    let streams: Vec<(i64, String, i64)> = doc["subtitles"]["streams"]
        .as_array()
        .unwrap()
        .iter()
        .map(|s| (s["n"].as_i64().unwrap(), s["status"].as_str().unwrap().to_string(), s["events"].as_i64().unwrap()))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(streams, [(0, "read".to_string(), 2), (1, "read".to_string(), 2)]);
    assert!(unread_notes(&h, &id).is_empty());
    assert_eq!(files_under(&label.join("subs-ocr")), set(&["sub-0.frames.json", "sub-1.frames.json", "summary.json"]));
    let frames = json_of(&label.join("subs-ocr").join("sub-0.frames.json"));
    let keys: Vec<&str> = frames[1].as_object().unwrap().keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
    assert_eq!((frames.as_array().unwrap().len(), keys, &frames[1]["lines"]),
               (2, vec!["frame", "file", "t", "pts", "chars", "lines", "markers"], &json!(2)));
    let staged = staged_ocr(&h, &id);
    assert_eq!(files_under(&staged), set(&[
        "s0/f-000001000.png", "s0/f-000005000.png", "s1/f-000002000.png", "s1/f-000006000.png",
        "sub-0.ocr.jsonl", "sub-0.run.json", "sub-1.ocr.jsonl", "sub-1.run.json", "summary.json",
    ]));
    assert_eq!(fs::read(staged.join("sub-0.ocr.jsonl")).unwrap(), fs::read(h.tools().join("records-s0.txt")).unwrap());
    assert!(!work_of(&h, &id).exists());
    let log = fs::read_to_string(h.job_dir(&id).join("job.log")).unwrap();
    assert!(!log.contains("subtitle evidence (step 10) is not built in this version"), "{log}");
}

/// Design part 10.7, K2, R5-code-35: one run per stream, the next only after the last ended, below normal with
/// RTEN_NUM_THREADS=3 alone, in the title's work folder with the job's sub_clear_max_bytes.
#[test]
fn the_worker_runs_once_per_english_or_no_language_stream_one_at_a_time_below_normal_with_rten_num_threads_3() {
    let h = two_subs(&[], json!({}));
    let id = decided(&h);
    let work = work_of(&h, &id);
    let spawns = ocr_spawns(&h);
    assert_eq!(spawns.len(), 2);
    for (n, spawn) in spawns.iter().enumerate() {
        let want = [
            work.join("evidence.mks").to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
            "--stream".to_string(),
            n.to_string(),
            "--clear-max".to_string(),
            "64".to_string(),
            "--out".to_string(),
            work.join(format!("s{n}")).to_string_lossy().into_owned(),
        ];
        assert_eq!(spawn.args, want);
        assert_eq!(spawn.program, h.tools().join(format!("lazymkv-ocr{}", std::env::consts::EXE_SUFFIX)));
        assert_eq!(spawn.env, [("RTEN_NUM_THREADS".to_string(), "3".to_string())]);
        assert!(spawn.below_normal);
    }
    let log = fs::read_to_string(h.job_dir(&id).join("job.log")).unwrap();
    let at = |needle: &str| log.find(needle).unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("job.log lacks {needle}: {log}"));
    assert!(at("run lazymkv-ocr s0: ") < at("ended lazymkv-ocr s0: exit 0 after "));
    assert!(at("ended lazymkv-ocr s0: exit 0 after ") < at("run lazymkv-ocr s1: "));
    assert!(at("run lazymkv-ocr s1: ") < at("ended lazymkv-ocr s1: exit 0 after "));
}

/// Design part 10.8, T5-R9, T5-R58: past its cap the worker is killed, its partial output deleted, and the note's
/// detail counts its whole records; the note raises no review, so the decision's reviews are those of the same folders
/// with the unread streams taken out.
#[test]
fn a_worker_past_its_cap_leaves_the_stream_unread_with_its_note_and_no_review() {
    let h = two_subs(&CAP, json!({}));
    let id = decided(&h);
    assert_eq!(unread_notes(&h, &id)[0], unread(2, &cap_reason_of(3)));
    assert_eq!(files_under(&staged_ocr(&h, &id)), set(&["summary.json"]));
    assert!(!work_of(&h, &id).exists());
    let mut inputs = read_back(&h, &id, None);
    assert_eq!(inputs.file.unread, Ok(vec![(0, cap_reason_of(3)), (1, cap_reason_of(3))]));
    inputs.file.unread = Ok(Vec::new());
    let DecisionEntry::Results(without) = decide_doc(&inputs).decision else { panic!("the decision was skipped") };
    let decision = h.record(&id).titles[0].decision.clone().unwrap();
    assert_eq!(decision.reviews, without.decision.reviews);
    assert!(without.decision.notes.iter().all(|noted| noted.note != Note::SubtitleTextUnread));
}

/// Review Focus 2, T5-R9: a kill in the middle of a record counts only the whole records before it.

fn a_killed_worker_with_a_torn_last_record_counts_only_whole_records() {
    let h = two_subs(&CAP, json!({}));
    let records = fs::read_to_string(h.tools().join("records-cap-s1.txt")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!((records.matches('\n').count(), records.ends_with('\n')), (3, false), "the fixture's fourth record is torn");
    let id = decided(&h);
    assert_eq!(unread_notes(&h, &id)[1], unread(3, &cap_reason_of(3)));
}

/// Review Focus 2, T5-R8, design part 10.12: a panic's standard error can hold text, so the reason is the exit code

fn a_worker_that_panics_leaves_the_stream_unread_with_its_exit_code_and_no_stderr_text() {
    let h = two_subs(&["movie-direct-two-subs-panic"], json!({}));
    assert!(fs::read_to_string(h.tools().join("panic-s1.txt")).unwrap().contains(SENTINEL));
    let id = held(&h);
    assert_eq!(unread_notes(&h, &id), [unread(3, "lazymkv-ocr exited with code 101")]);
    let jobs = h.data().join("jobs");
    assert_eq!(holding(&jobs, SENTINEL), Vec::<String>::new());
    assert!(!h.engine_log().contains(SENTINEL));
    assert!(!Client::open(&h).snapshot().to_string().contains(SENTINEL));
    assert!(files_under(&jobs).iter().all(|name| !name.contains("capture")), "{:?}", files_under(&jobs));
}

/// Review Focus 2, design part 10.3: records the listing does not have leave the stream unread with numbers only.
#[test]
fn a_worker_that_writes_more_records_than_events_is_unread_by_the_cross_check() {
    let h = two_subs(&["movie-direct-two-subs-extra"], json!({}));
    let id = decided(&h);
    assert_eq!(unread_notes(&h, &id)[1], unread(3, "3 events recorded, 2 listed"));
    assert!(!staged_ocr(&h, &id).join("sub-1.ocr.jsonl").exists());
}

/// Design part 10.3, call 24: the sizes are compared too, never count and order alone.
#[test]
fn a_size_disagreement_with_ffprobe_leaves_the_stream_unread() {
    let h = two_subs(&["movie-direct-two-subs-extra"], json!({}));
    let id = decided(&h);
    assert_eq!(unread_notes(&h, &id)[0], unread(2, "event 1: size 1300 recorded, 1200 listed"));
    assert!(!staged_ocr(&h, &id).join("sub-0.ocr.jsonl").exists());
}

/// T5-R8, call 5: exit 3's first standard error line is the note's reason.
#[test]
fn an_exit_3_refusal_is_the_notes_reason() {
    let h = two_subs(&["movie-direct-two-subs-refused"], json!({}));
    let id = decided(&h);
    assert_eq!(unread_notes(&h, &id), [unread(3, REFUSAL)]);
}

/// T5-R8, Step 11 item e: a worker that exits 0 and writes no records leaves each stream unread with that sentence.
#[test]
fn a_worker_that_exits_0_without_records_leaves_each_stream_unread() {
    let h = two_subs(&["movie-direct-two-subs-silent"], json!({}));
    let id = decided(&h);
    assert_eq!(
        unread_notes(&h, &id),
        [unread(2, "lazymkv-ocr wrote no sub-0.ocr.jsonl"), unread(3, "lazymkv-ocr wrote no sub-1.ocr.jsonl")]
    );
    assert_eq!(files_under(&staged_ocr(&h, &id)), set(&["summary.json"]));
    assert!(!work_of(&h, &id).exists());
}

/// Design parts 10.8, 10.12, P19: an unread stream's partial records go; summary.json says why, with its exit code,
/// in the job folder and, byte for byte, in the staged folder.
#[test]
fn an_unread_stream_keeps_no_records_and_summary_json_says_why() {
    let h = two_subs(&["movie-direct-two-subs-panic"], json!({}));
    let id = decided(&h);
    let label = h.job_dir(&id).join(KEY);
    let staged = staged_ocr(&h, &id);
    assert_eq!(files_under(&staged), set(&[
        "s0/f-000001000.png", "s0/f-000005000.png", "sub-0.ocr.jsonl", "sub-0.run.json", "summary.json",
    ]));
    assert!(!label.join("subs-ocr").join("sub-1.frames.json").exists());
    let summary = json_of(&label.join("subs-ocr").join("summary.json"));
    let index = json_of(&label.join("subs").join("index.json"));
    let s1 = &summary["streams"][1];
    assert_eq!((&s1["n"], &s1["codec"], &s1["read"], &s1["why"], &s1["exit"]),
               (&json!(1), &index[1]["codec"], &json!(false), &json!("lazymkv-ocr exited with code 101"), &json!(101)));
    assert_eq!((&summary["streams"][0]["read"], &summary["streams"][0]["exit"]), (&json!(true), &json!(0)));
    assert_eq!(fs::read(staged.join("summary.json")).unwrap(), fs::read(label.join("subs-ocr").join("summary.json")).unwrap());
}

/// T5-R51: the title's subtitles section is the unread line, with no text, and the read stream's records are kept.
#[test]
fn a_title_with_an_unread_stream_has_the_unread_line_as_its_subtitles_section() {
    let h = two_subs(&["movie-direct-two-subs-refused"], json!({}));
    let id = decided(&h);
    let decide = h.job_dir(&id).join(KEY).join("decide.json");
    assert_eq!(json_of(&decide)["subtitles"], json!({"skipped": format!("stream s1 eng: not read by the engine: {REFUSAL}")}));
    assert!(!fs::read_to_string(&decide).unwrap().contains(SENTINEL));
    let staged = staged_ocr(&h, &id);
    assert!(fs::read_to_string(staged.join("sub-0.ocr.jsonl")).unwrap().contains(SENTINEL));
    assert!(!staged.join("sub-1.ocr.jsonl").exists());
}

/// T5-R59: the job's own sub_clear_max_bytes reaches the worker, the cross-check and the subtitles section, so a
/// 50-byte packet is an event at 40 for all three. (The text's reviews stay out at any threshold but 64: dev's
/// `text_decisions` uses no text when `settings.text_rule()` is not the default, RP15.)
#[test]
fn a_job_whose_clear_max_is_not_64_decides_with_the_workers_events() {
    let h = two_subs(&["movie-direct-two-subs-clear-40"], json!({"sub_clear_max_bytes": 40}));
    let id = decided(&h);
    for spawn in ocr_spawns(&h) {
        assert!(spawn.args.windows(2).any(|pair| pair == ["--clear-max", "40"]), "{:?}", spawn.args);
    }
    assert!(unread_notes(&h, &id).is_empty());
    let staged = fs::read_to_string(staged_ocr(&h, &id).join("sub-1.ocr.jsonl")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(staged.lines().count(), 3);
    let doc = json_of(&h.job_dir(&id).join(KEY).join("decide.json"));
    assert_eq!((&doc["subtitles"]["streams"][0]["events"], &doc["subtitles"]["streams"][1]["events"]), (&json!(2), &json!(3)));
}

/// T5-R12: the staged summary.json, C3's marker, lands only after the job folder's: when the job folder's cannot be
/// written the step fails and the staged folder holds the streams' files but no summary.json.
#[test]
fn the_staged_summary_json_is_written_after_the_job_folders() {
    let h = two_subs(&[], json!({}));
    let id = job_id(&h);
    let blocker = h.job_dir(&id).join(KEY).join("subs-ocr").join("summary.json");
    let s1 = work_of(&h, &id).join("s1").display().to_string();
    let made = blocker.clone();
    h.on_spawn(&[&s1], move || fs::create_dir_all(&made).unwrap());
    let id = run_to(&h, "Failed");
    let record = h.record(&id);
    assert_eq!(record.state, State::Failed { class: FailureClass::Unknown, from: Box::new(State::Inspecting) });
    let message = record.message.unwrap();
    assert!(message.starts_with(&format!("{}: ", blocker.display())), "{message}");
    let staged = staged_ocr(&h, &id);
    assert!(staged.join("sub-0.ocr.jsonl").is_file() && staged.join("sub-1.ocr.jsonl").is_file());
    assert!(!staged.join("summary.json").exists());
    assert!(!work_of(&h, &id).exists());
}

/// Design part 10.12 item 3: the text is in the staged folder and in no file under jobs\, engine.log or the snapshot.
#[test]
fn no_ocr_text_reaches_the_job_folder_logs_state_or_snapshot() {
    let h = two_subs(&[], json!({}));
    let id = held(&h);
    assert!(fs::read_to_string(staged_ocr(&h, &id).join("sub-0.ocr.jsonl")).unwrap().contains(SENTINEL));
    assert_eq!(holding(&h.data().join("jobs"), SENTINEL), Vec::<String>::new());
    assert!(!h.engine_log().contains(SENTINEL));
    assert!(!Client::open(&h).snapshot().to_string().contains(SENTINEL));
}

/// T5-R57: the worker's capture is written to the work folder only and deleted with it.
#[test]
fn no_worker_capture_reaches_the_job_folder() {
    let h = two_subs(&[], json!({}));
    let id = decided(&h);
    for root in [h.data().join("jobs"), h.staging().to_path_buf()] {
        let files = files_under(&root);
        assert!(files.iter().all(|name| !name.contains("capture")), "{files:?}");
    }
    assert!(!work_of(&h, &id).exists());
}

/// Design part 10.7, ENG-13: a cancel kills the running worker, deletes its partial files and ends the job as
/// cancelled by the owner.
#[test]
fn a_cancel_kills_the_worker_and_deletes_its_work_folder() {
    let h = two_subs(&["movie-direct-two-subs-cap"], json!({}));
    let mut c = Client::open(&h);
    c.snapshot();
    h.insert("tok0", "movie-direct");
    h.deliver();
    let id = job_id(&h);
    let first = work_of(&h, &id).join("s0").join("sub-0.ocr.jsonl");
    h.wait("the worker's first records", |_| first.is_file());
    c.ok("cancel", json!({"job": id}));
    let record = h.record(&id);
    assert!(matches!(record.state, State::Failed { class: FailureClass::Unknown, .. }), "{:?}", record.state);
    assert_eq!(record.message.as_deref(), Some("cancelled by the owner"));
    h.wait("the work folder removed", |h| !work_of(h, &id).exists());
    assert_eq!(files_under(&staged_ocr(&h, &id)), BTreeSet::new());
}

/// T5-R8: a worker that is not beside the engine fails the decision before any extraction.
#[test]
fn a_missing_worker_fails_the_decision_with_ocr_missing() {
    let h = two_subs(&[], json!({}));
    fs::remove_file(h.tools().join(format!("lazymkv-ocr{}", std::env::consts::EXE_SUFFIX))).unwrap();
    let id = run_to(&h, "Failed");
    let record = h.record(&id);
    assert_eq!(record.state, State::Failed { class: FailureClass::Unknown, from: Box::new(State::Inspecting) });
    assert_eq!(record.message.as_deref(), Some("lazymkv-ocr is not beside the engine, so step 10 cannot read subtitles"));
    assert!(!h.staging().join(&id).join("evidence").exists());
    assert!(ocr_spawns(&h).is_empty());
}

```rust
/// Design part 5.10, T5-R51: a held two-stream job with one stream unread, approved after a restart, decides from the
/// staged text and summary.json's unread stream with dev's readers, exactly as `lazymkvctl decide` does over the same
/// folders.
#[test]
fn a_held_job_approved_after_a_restart_reads_the_staged_text_and_the_unread_streams() {
    let h = harness(&["movie-direct", "movie-direct-two-subs", "movie-direct-two-subs-panic"], settings());
    fs::create_dir_all(final_path(&h).parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
    fs::write(final_path(&h), b"owner's").unwrap();
    h.insert("tok0", DISC);
    h.run_until("NeedsReview");
    let id = only_job(&h);
    let dir = h.job_dir(&id);
    h.restart();
    fs::remove_file(final_path(&h)).unwrap();
    let mut c = Client::open(&h);
    c.snapshot();
    c.ok("review_action", json!({"job": id, "action": "approve"}));
    let decisions = |h: &Harness| {
        transitions(&h.job_dir(&id)).iter().filter(|line| matches!(line.event, Some(Event::DecisionDone { .. }))).count()
    };
    h.wait("the decision made again", |h| decisions(h) == 2);
    assert!(fs::read_to_string(dir.join("job.log")).unwrap().contains(
        "decide inputs read back from the job folder with lazymkv-dev's readers (design part 5.10)"));
    let staged = h.staging().join(&id).join("tuning").join(KEY).join("subs-ocr");
    let ctx = Ctx::for_test(h.data());
    let (rec, label) = rec_folder(&ctx, &dir.join(KEY).display().to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|r| panic!("{}", r.line));
    let options = PlanOptions {
        settings: Some(dir.join("settings.json")),
        tmdb_search: Some(dir.join("tmdb-search.json")),
        tmdb_record: Some(dir.join("tmdb-record.json")),
        remembered: None,
    };
    let read = read_decide_inputs(&ctx, &rec, &label, Some(&staged), None, &options).unwrap_or_else(|r| panic!("{}", r.line));
    assert_eq!(read.file.unread, Ok(vec![(1, "lazymkv-ocr exited with code 101".to_string())]));
    let mut written: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_slice(&fs::read(dir.join(KEY).join("decide.json")).unwrap()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(written["subtitles"],
               json!({"skipped": "stream s1 eng: not read by the engine: lazymkv-ocr exited with code 101"}));
    let object = written.as_object_mut().unwrap();
    object.remove("audio_rule_version");
    object.remove("lazymkv_version");
    assert_eq!(
        dumps(&written, Style::INDENT1_ASCII),
        dumps(&serde_json::to_value(decide_doc(&read)).unwrap(), Style::INDENT1_ASCII)
    );
}

/// Review Focus 3, T5-R4: what a crashed run left in the work folder is deleted when the engine starts.
#[test]
fn engine_start_removes_a_leftover_work_folder() {
    let h = harness(&["movie-direct"], settings());
    let leftover = h.data().join("work").join(format!("ocr-x-{KEY}")).join("s0");
    fs::create_dir_all(&leftover).unwrap();
    fs::write(leftover.join("sub-0.ocr.jsonl"), b"{\"pts\":1.0,\"size\":900}\n").unwrap();
    h.restart();
    assert!(!h.data().join("work").exists());
    assert!(!h.engine_log().contains("could not be removed"), "{}", h.engine_log());
}

/// Review Focus 3, design part 10.7: a forced stop during a worker run kills the worker and leaves no work folder. The
/// cap is 60 s here, so an engine that ends within 30 s killed it; the bound proves the kill and is not scaled.
#[test]
fn a_stop_during_a_worker_run_kills_it_and_leaves_no_work_folder() {
    let h = harness(&["movie-direct", "movie-direct-two-subs", "movie-direct-two-subs-cap"], settings());
    h.insert("tok0", DISC);
    let id = format!("{}-1", h.fingerprint(DISC).to_ascii_lowercase());
    let work = h.data().join("work").join(format!("ocr-{id}-{KEY}"));
    let first = work.join("s0").join("sub-0.ocr.jsonl");
    h.wait("the worker's first records", |_| first.is_file());
    h.shutdown_handle().shutdown(true);
    assert!(h.wait_for_exit(Duration::from_secs(30)), "the engine did not stop within 30 s");
    assert!(!work.exists());
}

This task ports the pure half of `scripts/phase0/audio-levels.ps1` into `core::audio::pass`: the ffmpeg filter graph and command, the series files with the .NET Framework number format, the `streamhash.txt` reader, the centre-channel rule, the manifest, the peak and proxy checks and `audio-proxy.json`. | -99.94 | -99.9 | -100 | -100.0 | -3 | -3.0 |
| -20.0499999 | -20.0 | -20.04999999999999 | -20.1 | | |

Where a printed string differs from the table, `EDGES` takes the printed one. If `-0.04` and `-0.000000` print `-0.0`, Step 8's sign rule is "a minus sign whenever the value is negative" instead of "only when the rounded value is not zero"; any other difference that neither form of Step 8's rule gives stops the task and goes to the owner with the 17 lines (call 9: never adjust to pass). A second line that is not `Desktop`, or a `[Environment]::Version` not starting `4.`, also goes to the owner: the oracle is not phase 0's runtime.
Evidence (to `.superpowers/pr5/pr5-mini-pc-runs.txt`): `<yyyy-MM-dd>, SSH, Windows PowerShell 5.1 (Desktop, CLR 4.0.30319) printed the 0.0 format of net_fixed1's 17 edge values: <k> as the plan predicted, <17 - k> differ: <input> <printed>, ...` (or `none differ`).

//! Tests of core::audio::pass against scripts/phase0/audio-levels.ps1: its graph, command, series files, stream hashes,
//! centre rule, manifest, proxy checks and audio-proxy.json, over made-up streams. The edge values of net_fixed1 are
//! what Windows PowerShell 5.1 printed on the mini PC (Task 16 Step 1).

use serde_json::json;

use super::*;
use crate::audio::dataset::levels_args;
use crate::audio::levels::{parse_proxy, parse_streams};
use crate::recording::{MemTree, PathKey};
use crate::testsupport::probe_streams_json;

/// Phase 0's level chain up to its file name (audio-levels.ps1 lines 265 to 267).
const TAIL: &str = "aresample=8000,highpass=f=300,lowpass=f=3400,asetnsamples=n=160:p=0,astats=metadata=1:reset=1:measure_perchannel=none:measure_overall=RMS_level,ametadata=print:key=lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level:file=";

/// Phase 0's proxy chain up to its file name, at `gain` dB (lines 270 to 272).
fn to_proxy(gain: i32) -> String {
    format!("aresample=8000,volume={gain}dB,asetnsamples=n=8000:p=0,astats=metadata=1:reset=0:measure_perchannel=none:measure_overall=Peak_level,ametadata=print:key=lavfi.astats.Overall.Peak_level:file=")
}

/// A made-up `ffmpeg -hide_banner -layouts` output: a DESCRIPTION section, then the NAME DECOMPOSITION table.
const LAYOUTS: &str = "Individual channels:\nNAME           DESCRIPTION\nFL             front left\nFR             front right\nFC             front center\nLFE            low frequency\nSL             side left\nSR             side right\nBL             back left\nBR             back right\n\nStandard channel layouts:\nNAME           DECOMPOSITION\nmono           FC\nstereo         FL+FR\n2.1            FL+FR+LFE\n5.1            FL+FR+FC+LFE+BL+BR\n5.1(side)      FL+FR+FC+LFE+SL+SR\n";

/// A made-up file: video, a 5.1 main, a stereo and a mono candidate, a subtitle stream.
const THREE: &str = r#"{"streams": [
  {"index": 0, "codec_type": "video", "codec_name": "hevc"},
  {"index": 1, "codec_type": "audio", "codec_name": "truehd", "channels": 6, "channel_layout": "5.1(side)", "tags": {"language": "eng"}},
  {"index": 2, "codec_type": "audio", "codec_name": "ac3", "channels": 2, "channel_layout": "stereo", "tags": {"language": "eng"}},

  {"index": 4, "codec_type": "subtitle", "codec_name": "hdmv_pgs_subtitle"}]}"#;

const MONO_PAIR: &str = r#"{"streams": [

  {"index": 2, "codec_type": "audio", "codec_name": "ac3", "channels": 1, "channel_layout": "mono"}]}"#;

const ODD: &str = r#"{"streams": [

  {"index": 2, "codec_type": "audio", "codec_name": "dts", "profile": "DTS-HD MA", "channels": 2, "channel_layout": "stereo", "tags": {"language": "eng"}},

fn streams(json: &str) -> Vec<PassStream> {

#[test]
fn the_graph_is_phase_0s_for_a_main_with_centre_and_two_candidates() {
    let s = streams(THREE);
    assert_eq!(s.iter().map(|x| x.index).collect::<Vec<i64>>(), vec![1, 2, 3]);
    let g = graph(&s, 1, &[2, 3], &layouts(), true, GAIN_FIRST_DB);
    let p = to_proxy(-18);
    let expected = [
        "[0:1]asplit=4[s1b0][s1b1][s1b2][s1b3]".to_string(),
        format!("[s1b0]aformat=channel_layouts=mono,{TAIL}raw-main-mix.txt[o0]"),
        format!("[s1b1]pan=mono|c0=FC,{TAIL}raw-main-fc.txt[o1]"),
        format!("[s1b2]aformat=channel_layouts=mono,{p}peak-0.txt,aformat=sample_fmts=s32[p0]"),
        format!("[s1b3]pan=mono|c0=FC,{p}peak-1.txt,aformat=sample_fmts=s32[p1]"),
        "[0:2]asplit=3[s2b0][s2b1][s2b2]".to_string(),
        format!("[s2b0]aformat=channel_layouts=mono,{TAIL}raw-cand-2.txt[o2]"),
        format!("[s2b1]aformat=channel_layouts=mono,{p}peak-2.txt,aformat=sample_fmts=s32[p2]"),
        format!("[s2b2]pan=mono|c0=0.5*c0-0.5*c1,{p}peak-3.txt,aformat=sample_fmts=s32[p3]"),
        "[0:3]asplit=2[s3b0][s3b1]".to_string(),
        format!("[s3b0]aformat=channel_layouts=mono,{TAIL}raw-cand-3.txt[o3]"),
        format!("[s3b1]aformat=channel_layouts=mono,{p}peak-4.txt,aformat=sample_fmts=s32[p4]"),
    ];
    assert_eq!(g.text, expected.join(";"));
    let series: Vec<(&str, &str)> = g.series.iter().map(|x| (x.name.as_str(), x.raw.as_str())).collect();
    assert_eq!(series, vec![("main-mix", "raw-main-mix.txt"), ("main-fc", "raw-main-fc.txt"),
                            ("cand-2", "raw-cand-2.txt"), ("cand-3", "raw-cand-3.txt")]);
    let tracks: Vec<(i64, &str, &str, &str)> =
        g.proxy.iter().map(|t| (t.stream, t.series.as_str(), t.language.as_str(), t.peak.as_str())).collect();
    assert_eq!(tracks, vec![(1, "mix", "eng", "peak-0.txt"), (1, "fc", "eng", "peak-1.txt"), (2, "mix", "eng", "peak-2.txt"),
                            (2, "side", "eng", "peak-3.txt"), (3, "mix", "spa", "peak-4.txt")]);
}

/// The proxy half of the command for THREE's five tracks, written to `audio-proxy.mka.partial`.
fn proxy_part() -> Vec<String> {
    let mut v: Vec<String> = (0..5).flat_map(|k| ["-map".to_string(), format!("[p{k}]")]).collect();
    v.extend(["-c:a", "flac", "-compression_level", "5", "-bits_per_raw_sample", "24"].map(String::from));
    let tracks = [(1, "mix", "eng"), (1, "fc", "eng"), (2, "mix", "eng"), (2, "side", "eng"), (3, "mix", "spa")];
    for (k, (n, series, lang)) in tracks.iter().enumerate() {
        for value in [format!("LAZYMKV_SOURCE_STREAM={n}"), format!("LAZYMKV_SERIES={series}"), format!("language={lang}")] {
            v.extend([format!("-metadata:s:a:{k}"), value]);
        }
    }
    v.extend(["-f", "matroska", "audio-proxy.mka.partial"].map(String::from));
    v
}

#[test]
fn the_command_has_phase_0s_parts_in_order() {
    let head: Vec<String> =
        ["-v", "warning", "-nostats", "-nostdin", "-i", "title_t00.mkv", "-/filter_complex", "graph.txt"].map(String::from).to_vec();
    let g = graph(&streams(THREE), 1, &[2, 3], &layouts(), true, GAIN_FIRST_DB);
    let mut want = head.clone();
    for k in 0..4 {
        want.extend(["-map".to_string(), format!("[o{k}]"), "-f".to_string(), "null".to_string(), format!("o{k}")]);
    }
    for n in 1..=3 {
        want.extend(["-map".to_string(), format!("0:{n}")]);
    }
    want.extend(["-c", "copy", "-f", "streamhash", "-hash", "md5", "streamhash.txt"].map(String::from));
    want.extend(proxy_part());
    assert_eq!(ffmpeg_args("title_t00.mkv", &g, true, Some("audio-proxy.mka.partial")), want);
    let redo = graph(&streams(THREE), 1, &[2, 3], &layouts(), false, GAIN_REDO_DB);
    let mut want = head;
    want.extend(proxy_part());
    assert_eq!(ffmpeg_args("title_t00.mkv", &redo, false, Some("audio-proxy.mka.partial")), want);
}

/// A made-up raw ametadata file: -inf, a half, nan, a value below the floor, an exact binary tie, a peak line and an
/// indented RMS line (neither is read).
const RAW: &[&str] = &[
    "frame:0    pts:0       pts_time:0",
    "lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=-inf",
    "frame:1    pts:160     pts_time:0.02",
    "lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=-23.450000",
    "frame:2    pts:320     pts_time:0.04",
    "lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=nan",
    "frame:3    pts:480     pts_time:0.06",
    "lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=-123.500000",
    "frame:4    pts:640     pts_time:0.08",
    "lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=-12.250000",
    "lavfi.astats.Overall.Peak_level=-3.000000",
    " lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=-5.000000",
];
const HEADER: &str = "# lazymkv audio levels v2: frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400 unit=dB floor=-100 series=main-mix file=My_Title_t00.mkv";

#[test]
fn a_series_file_has_the_v2_header_crlf_lines_and_minus_100_for_inf_and_nan() {
    let raw = RAW.join("\n") + "\n";
    let want = [HEADER, "-100.0", "-23.5", "-100.0", "-100.0", "-12.3"].join("\r\n") + "\r\n";
    assert_eq!(series_file(&raw, "main-mix", "My Title \t t00.mkv"), Ok(want));
    assert!(series_file(&raw, "main-mix", "").unwrap().starts_with(
        "# lazymkv audio levels v2: frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400 unit=dB floor=-100 series=main-mix file=-\r\n"));
    assert_eq!(series_file("frame:0\n", "cand-2", "x.mkv"), Err("cand-2.txt holds no level".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(series_file("lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=abc\n", "main-fc", "x.mkv"),
               Err("raw-main-fc.txt: abc is not a number".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(series_file("lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=Infinity\n", "main-fc", "x.mkv"),
               Err("raw-main-fc.txt: Infinity is not a number".to_string()));
}

#[test]
fn a_raw_file_with_crlf_and_a_trailing_blank_line_gives_the_same_series() {
    // Review Focus 5: .NET's File.ReadLines ends a line at CRLF, LF or CR, and a blank line holds no value.
    let want = series_file(&(RAW.join("\n") + "\n"), "main-mix", "My Title t00.mkv").unwrap();
    assert_eq!(series_file(&(RAW.join("\r\n") + "\r\n\r\n"), "main-mix", "My Title t00.mkv").unwrap(), want);
    assert_eq!(series_file(&(RAW.join("\r") + "\r"), "main-mix", "My Title t00.mkv").unwrap(), want);
    assert_eq!(series_file(&RAW.join("\n"), "main-mix", "My Title t00.mkv").unwrap(), want, "no newline after the last line");
    assert!(want.ends_with("-12.3\r\n") && !want.contains("\r\n\r\n") && !want.starts_with('\u{feff}'));
}

/// (ffmpeg's text, what Windows PowerShell 5.1 printed for it on the mini PC in Step 1).
const EDGES: &[(&str, &str)] = &[
    ("-12.25", "-12.3"), ("-12.250000", "-12.3"), ("-0.25", "-0.3"), ("-23.45", "-23.5"), ("-1.15", "-1.2"),
    ("-7.650000", "-7.7"), ("-64.349999", "-64.3"), ("-0.05", "-0.1"), ("-0.04", "0.0"), ("-0.000000", "0.0"),
    ("0.000000", "0.0"), ("-99.95", "-100.0"), ("-99.94", "-99.9"), ("-100", "-100.0"), ("-3", "-3.0"),
    ("-20.0499999", "-20.0"), ("-20.04999999999999", "-20.1"),
];

#[test]
fn net_fixed1_matches_dotnet_framework_on_the_edge_values() {
    // Review Focus 5, T5-R19: ties on the binary value, 15-digit inputs and values that round to zero.
    for (text, printed) in EDGES {
        assert_eq!(net_fixed1(text), *printed, "{text}");
    }
    // Rust's {:.1} rounds the binary value half to even, so it is not the port's formatter (R6-phase0-56).
    assert_eq!(format!("{:.1}", -12.25_f64), "-12.2");
    assert_eq!(format!("{:.1}", -1.15_f64), "-1.1");
}

#[test]
fn streamhash_with_a_missing_stream_is_refused_with_both_counts() {
    let two = format!("0,a,MD5={H0}\n1,a,MD5={H1}\n");
    assert_eq!(parse_streamhash(&two, 3), Err("streamhash.txt holds 2 of 3 stream hashes".to_string()));
    let three = format!("0,a,MD5={H0}\r\n1,a,MD5={H1}\r\n2,a,MD5={H2}\r\n");
    assert_eq!(parse_streamhash(&three, 3), Ok(vec![(0, H0.to_string()), (1, H1.to_string()), (2, H2.to_string())]));
    // A repeated k counts once; a short hash, an indented line and a k past the count are not counted.
    let noisy = format!("0,a,MD5={H0}\n0,a,MD5={H0}\n1,a,MD5=abc\n 2,a,MD5={H2}\n5,a,MD5={H2}\n");
    assert_eq!(parse_streamhash(&noisy, 3), Err("streamhash.txt holds 1 of 3 stream hashes".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(parse_streamhash(&format!("0,A,md5={H0}\n"), 1), Ok(vec![(0, H0.to_string())]), "-match ignores case");
}

/// A made-up peak file of astats with reset=0: one running peak per second.
fn peaks(values: &[&str]) -> String {
    values
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .map(|(k, v)| format!("frame:{k}    pts:{}     pts_time:{k}\nlavfi.astats.Overall.Peak_level={v}\n", k * 8000))
        .collect()
}

#[test]
fn a_peak_at_minus_0_1_is_clipped_and_minus_0_11_is_not() {
    assert_eq!(peak_clipped(&peaks(&["-20.000000", "-0.100000"])), Ok(true));
    assert_eq!(peak_clipped(&peaks(&["-20.000000", "-0.110000"])), Ok(false));
    assert_eq!(peak_clipped(&peaks(&["0.000000"])), Ok(true));
    assert_eq!(peak_clipped(&peaks(&["-inf"])), Ok(false));
    assert_eq!(last_peak(&peaks(&["-30.000000", " -0.110000 "])), Some("-0.110000".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(last_peak("frame:0\n"), None);
    assert_eq!(peak_clipped("frame:0\n"), Err("holds no peak".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(peak_clipped(&peaks(&["x"])), Err("holds the peak x, which is not a number".to_string()));
}

#[test]
fn a_guessed_layout_is_recorded_and_finds_its_centre() {
    let s = streams(ODD);
    let l = layouts();
    let got: Vec<Centre> = s.iter().map(|x| centre(x, &l)).collect();
    let guess = |name: &str| Some(name.to_string());
    assert_eq!(got, vec![
        Centre { has_fc: true, guessed: guess("5.1") },
        Centre { has_fc: false, guessed: None },
        Centre { has_fc: false, guessed: None },
        Centre { has_fc: false, guessed: guess("2.1") },
        Centre { has_fc: false, guessed: None },
        Centre { has_fc: true, guessed: None },
    ]);
    let text = manifest_text("My Title t00.mkv", 1000, 42.5, &s[0], &s[1..2], &l, &[(1, 250), (2, 249)],
                             &[(1, H0.to_string()), (2, H1.to_string())]);
    let want: Vec<String> = vec![
        "# lazymkv audio-levels v2 (experiment 13)".to_string(),
        "file=My_Title_t00.mkv bytes=1000 seconds=42 frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400".to_string(),
        format!("main=1 codec=pcm_s24le profile=- channels=6 layout=unknown layout_guessed=5.1 language=eng fc=yes frames=250 md5={H0}"),
        format!("cand=2 codec=dts profile=DTS-HD_MA channels=2 layout=stereo language=eng frames=249 md5={H1}"),
    ];
    assert_eq!(text, want.join("\r\n") + "\r\n");
    let g = graph(&s, 1, &[2], &l, true, GAIN_FIRST_DB);
    assert!(g.text.contains(&format!("[s1b1]pan=mono|c0=FC,{TAIL}raw-main-fc.txt[o1]")), "{}", g.text);
}

#[test]
fn the_layout_table_is_read_from_the_name_decomposition_section_only() {
    let none = "ffmpeg -layouts printed no table of channel layouts (no NAME DECOMPOSITION section)";
    assert_eq!(parse_layouts("").err().as_deref(), Some(none));
    assert_eq!(parse_layouts("NAME           DESCRIPTION\nquad           FL+FR+FC+LFE\n").err().as_deref(), Some(none));
    let four = streams(r#"{"streams": [{"index": 1, "codec_type": "audio", "channels": 4, "channel_layout": "quad"},
                                         {"index": 2, "codec_type": "audio", "channels": 4}]}"#);
    let with_quad = parse_layouts(&format!("{LAYOUTS}quad           FL+FR+FC+BC\n")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(centre(&four[0], &with_quad), Centre { has_fc: true, guessed: None });
    assert_eq!(centre(&four[0], &layouts()), Centre { has_fc: false, guessed: None }, "quad is not in that table");
    assert_eq!(centre(&four[1], &layouts()), Centre { has_fc: false, guessed: None }, "4.0 is not in that table");
}

#[test]
fn main_and_candidates_read_levels_args_first_line() {
    let mut tree = MemTree::new(".", "tmp");
    tree.insert_file("some-film/dub-first/ffprobe-streams.json", probe_streams_json(&[
        ("dts", Some("DTS-HD MA"), 6, "spa"), ("truehd", None, 8, "eng"), ("ac3", None, 2, "eng"),
        ("ac3", None, 6, "fra"), ("ac3", None, 2, "fra")]));
    tree.insert_file("some-film/tmdb.json", r#"{"original_language": "es"}"#);
    let lines = levels_args(&tree, &PathKey::new("some-film"), "dub-first").unwrap();
    let jobs: Vec<&String> = lines.iter().filter(|l| l.starts_with("scripts/phase0/job.sh")).collect();
    assert_eq!(jobs.len(), 2);
    assert_eq!(main_and_candidates(jobs[0]), Some((1, vec![2, 3])), "T5-R38: the first job line is the pass");
    assert_eq!(main_and_candidates(jobs[1]), Some((4, vec![5])));
    assert_eq!(main_and_candidates("scripts/phase0/job.sh audio-levels.ps1 l -Slug s -Label t -Main 3"), Some((3, vec![])));
    assert_eq!(main_and_candidates("scripts/phase0/wait.sh audio-levels-some-film-dub-first"), None);
    assert_eq!(main_and_candidates("  stream 1: dts DTS-HD MA 6 ch lang=spa"), None);
    assert_eq!(main_and_candidates("scripts/phase0/job.sh audio-levels.ps1 l -Slug s -Label t -Main x"), None);
}

#[test]
fn the_main_and_candidates_are_checked_with_phase_0s_refusals() {
    let all = parse_streams(THREE).unwrap().streams;
    assert_eq!(check_main_and_candidates(&all, 1, &[2, 3]), Ok(()));
    let refused = |main: i64, cands: &[i64]| check_main_and_candidates(&all, main, cands).unwrap_err();
    assert_eq!(refused(1, &[1]), "stream 1 is the main stream and cannot also be a candidate");
    assert_eq!(refused(1, &[2, 2]), "a candidate stream is listed twice: 2,2");
    assert_eq!(refused(1, &[7]), "the file has no stream 7");
    assert_eq!(refused(0, &[]), "stream 0 is video, not audio");
    assert_eq!(refused(1, &[4]), "stream 4 is subtitle, not audio");
}

/// proxy-check.json as ffprobe writes it for two tracks of stream 2 (mix, side), edited by `edit`.
fn check_json(edit: impl Fn(&mut Vec<serde_json::Value>)) -> String {
    let track = |index: i64, series: &str, duration: &str| json!({"index": index, "codec_name": "flac", "codec_type": "audio",
        "sample_fmt": "s32", "sample_rate": "8000", "channels": 1, "bits_per_raw_sample": "24",
        "tags": {"LAZYMKV_SOURCE_STREAM": "2", "LAZYMKV_SERIES": series, "language": "eng", "DURATION": duration}});
    let mut streams = vec![track(0, "mix", "01:02:03.500000000"), track(1, "side", "00:00:01.000000000")];
    edit(&mut streams);
    serde_json::to_string_pretty(&json!({"programs": [], "streams": streams})).unwrap()
}

fn mix_and_side() -> Vec<ProxyTrack> {
    let t = |series: &str, k: usize| ProxyTrack { stream: 2, series: series.to_string(), language: "eng".to_string(), peak: format!("peak-{k}.txt") };
    vec![t("mix", 0), t("side", 1)]
}

#[test]
fn the_proxy_check_wants_one_flac_8000_hz_mono_24_bit_track_per_series_with_its_tags_and_a_duration() {
    let want = mix_and_side();
    assert_eq!(proxy_check(&check_json(|_| {}), &want), Ok(vec![3723.5, 1.0]));
    assert_eq!(proxy_check(&check_json(|s| { s.pop(); }), &want),
               Err("proxy check failed: the proxy has 1 tracks, 2 were written".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(proxy_check(&check_json(|s| s[1]["sample_rate"] = json!("48000")), &want),
               Err("proxy check failed: proxy track 1 (stream 2 side) is audio flac 48000 Hz 1 ch 24 bit, not flac 8000 Hz 1 ch 24 bit".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(proxy_check(&check_json(|s| s[0]["tags"]["LAZYMKV_SERIES"] = json!("fc")), &want),
               Err("proxy check failed: proxy track 0 (stream 2 mix) is tagged stream 2 fc".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(proxy_check(&check_json(|s| { s[1]["tags"].as_object_mut().unwrap().remove("DURATION"); }), &want),
               Err("proxy check failed: proxy track 1 (stream 2 side) has no duration (the file was not finished)".to_string()));
    let lower = check_json(|s| s[0]["tags"] = json!({"lazymkv_source_stream": "2", "lazymkv_series": "mix", "duration": "00:00:02.5"}));
    assert_eq!(proxy_check(&lower, &want), Ok(vec![2.5, 1.0]), "tag names are read as PowerShell reads them, ignoring case");
}

fn source(md5: &str) -> ProxySourceStream {
    ProxySourceStream { codec: "ac3".to_string(), profile: String::new(), channels: 2, layout: "stereo".to_string(),
        layout_guessed: String::new(), language: "eng".to_string(), title: String::new(), sample_rate: "48000".to_string(),
        sample_fmt: "fltp".to_string(), bits_per_raw_sample: String::new(), start_time: "0.000000".to_string(), md5: md5.to_string() }
}

/// A made-up record of one stereo stream (its mix and side tracks).
fn record(proxy: Option<ProxyFile>, gain_db: i32, gains_tried: Vec<i32>) -> ProxyRecord {
    let track = |k: usize, series: &str, peak: &str| ProxyTrackFacts { track: k, source_stream: 1, series: series.to_string(),
        duration_s: 12.3456, peak_dbfs: peak.to_string(), source: source(H0) };
    ProxyRecord {
        slug: "job-a".to_string(), label: "t00".to_string(), created: "2026-11-06 10:00:00".to_string(),
        source: ProxySource { file: "title_t00.mkv".to_string(), bytes: 1000, modified: "2026-11-06 09:00:00".to_string(),
                              duration_s: "12.345000".to_string(), audio_streams: 1 },
        pass: ProxyPass { seconds: 42, ffmpeg: "ffmpeg version 9.0.2".to_string(), levels_folder: "audio-levels-20ms-1".to_string() },
        gain_db, proxy,
        tracks: vec![track(0, "mix", "-0.050000"), track(1, "side", "-6.000000")],
        gains_tried,
    }
}

#[test]
fn audio_proxy_json_without_a_proxy_records_both_gains_and_parses_with_dev() {
    let text = proxy_json(&record(None, GAIN_REDO_DB, vec![GAIN_FIRST_DB, GAIN_REDO_DB]));
    assert!(text.starts_with("{\n  \"format\": \"lazymkv audio proxy v1\",\n"), "{text}");
    assert!(text.ends_with("}\n") && !text.ends_with("}\n\n"));
    let v: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&text).unwrap();
    let keys: Vec<&str> = v.as_object().unwrap().keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
    assert_eq!(keys, ["format", "slug", "label", "created", "source", "pass", "encoding", "proxy", "not_kept", "tracks", "gains_tried"]);
    let enc: Vec<&str> = v["encoding"].as_object().unwrap().keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
    assert_eq!(enc, ["codec", "sample_rate", "channels", "bits", "compression_level", "gain_db", "mix", "fc", "side", "chain", "read"]);
    let track_keys: Vec<&str> = v["tracks"][0].as_object().unwrap().keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
    assert_eq!(track_keys, ["track", "source_stream", "series", "duration_s", "peak_dbfs", "source"]);
    let src = json!({"codec": "ac3", "profile": "", "channels": 2, "layout": "stereo", "layout_guessed": "", "language": "eng",
        "title": "", "sample_rate": "48000", "sample_fmt": "fltp", "bits_per_raw_sample": "", "start_time": "0.000000", "md5": H0});
    let src_keys: Vec<&str> = v["tracks"][0]["source"].as_object().unwrap().keys().map(String::as_str).collect();
    assert_eq!(src_keys, ["codec", "profile", "channels", "layout", "layout_guessed", "language", "title", "sample_rate",
                          "sample_fmt", "bits_per_raw_sample", "start_time", "md5"]);
    assert_eq!(v, json!({
        "format": "lazymkv audio proxy v1", "slug": "job-a", "label": "t00", "created": "2026-11-06 10:00:00",
        "source": {"file": "title_t00.mkv", "bytes": 1000, "modified": "2026-11-06 09:00:00", "duration_s": "12.345000", "audio_streams": 1},
        "pass": {"seconds": 42, "ffmpeg": "ffmpeg version 9.0.2", "levels_folder": "audio-levels-20ms-1"},
        "encoding": {"codec": "flac", "sample_rate": 8000, "channels": 1, "bits": 24, "compression_level": 5, "gain_db": -30,
            "mix": "aformat=channel_layouts=mono on the decoded stream, as in the level chain",
            "fc": "pan=mono|c0=FC, for every stream whose layout has FC besides other channels",
            "side": "pan=mono|c0=0.5*c0-0.5*c1, for every two-channel stream (the mix is 0.5*c0+0.5*c1)",
            "chain": "aresample=8000,volume=-30dB,aformat=sample_fmts=s32",
            "read": "add 30 dB in float, convert to the source stream's sample_fmt, then measure (lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy)"},
        "proxy": null,
        "not_kept": "video and subtitle streams; channels other than the mixdown, the centre and a stereo pair's side signal; sound above 4 kHz; object-audio metadata; the packets themselves (their MD5 is kept)",
        "tracks": [
            {"track": 0, "source_stream": 1, "series": "mix", "duration_s": 12.346, "peak_dbfs": "-0.050000", "source": src.clone()},
            {"track": 1, "source_stream": 1, "series": "side", "duration_s": 12.346, "peak_dbfs": "-6.000000", "source": src}],
        "gains_tried": [-18, -30]
    }));
    // dev's reader (core::audio::levels, which decide's read_level_md5 and levels-from-proxy use) reads it.
    let p = parse_proxy(&text).unwrap();
    assert!(p.kept_no_proxy());
    assert_eq!(p.gains_tried, Some(vec![-18, -30]));
    assert_eq!(p.encoding.get("gain_db").and_then(|g| g.as_i64()), Some(-30));
    let tracks: Vec<(Option<i64>, Option<&str>)> = p.tracks.iter().map(|t| (t.source_stream.as_i64(), t.series.as_deref())).collect();
    assert_eq!(tracks, vec![(Some(1), Some("mix")), (Some(1), Some("side"))]);
    assert_eq!(p.tracks[0].source.as_ref().unwrap().get("md5").and_then(|m| m.as_str()), Some(H0));
    let kept = parse_proxy(&proxy_json(&record(Some(ProxyFile { bytes: 5000, tracks: 2 }), GAIN_FIRST_DB, vec![GAIN_FIRST_DB]))).unwrap();
    assert!(!kept.kept_no_proxy());
    assert_eq!(kept.proxy, Some(json!({"file": "audio-proxy.mka", "bytes": 5000, "tracks": 2})));
    assert_eq!(kept.gains_tried, Some(vec![-18]));
    assert_eq!(kept.encoding.get("read").and_then(|r| r.as_str()),
               Some("add 18 dB in float, convert to the source stream's sample_fmt, then measure (lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy)"));
}
```

  - `parse_layouts`: each line trimmed and split on whitespace runs; only lines of exactly two columns are read; a line whose first column is `NAME` (ASCII case-insensitive) sets "in the table" to whether its second column is `DECOMPOSITION` (case-insensitive) and is not itself an entry; in the table, the first column (ASCII-lowercased) maps to the second split on `+`.
  - `centre`: the channels are the table's for `layout` (looked up lowercased); else, when `layout` matches `(?i)^[0-9]+ channels \(([^()]+)\)$`, the group split on `+` with each part cut at its first `@`; else, when the table holds the guess for `channels` (1 mono, 2 stereo, 3 2.1, 4 4.0, 5 5.0, 6 5.1, 7 6.1, 8 7.1), the table's channels and `guessed` that name; else none. `has_fc` is "some channel equals `FC` (ASCII case-insensitive) and there are more than one".

  - `ffmpeg_args`: `-v warning -nostats -nostdin -i <file> -/filter_complex graph.txt`, then with `levels` `-map [o<k>] -f null o<k>` per series, `-map 0:<n>` per stream of `graph.proxy`'s `mix` tracks in order, and `-c copy -f streamhash -hash md5 streamhash.txt`; then, when `proxy_partial` is Some, `-map [p<k>]` per track, `-c:a flac -compression_level 5 -bits_per_raw_sample 24`, per track the three `-metadata:s:a:<k>` pairs (`LAZYMKV_SOURCE_STREAM=<n>`, `LAZYMKV_SERIES=<series>`, `language=<language>`), and `-f matroska <proxy_partial>`. Each word is one argument; nothing is quoted (the program is started without a shell).
  - `series_file`: lines are the text split at CRLF, LF or CR, with no empty line after a final line end (as `File.ReadLines`); only lines starting with `lavfi.astats.Overall.RMS_level=` (no trim) are read; a value holding `inf` or `nan` writes `-100.0`; any other value whose `trim()` does not parse to a finite f64 is Err `raw-<series>.txt: <value> is not a number`; a parsed value below -100 writes `-100.0`, else `net_fixed1(value)`; the header is the test's `HEADER` with `series=<series>` and `file=<word>`, where `<word>` is `file_name` with each run of whitespace (`char::is_whitespace`) replaced by `_`, or `-` when `file_name` is empty; every line ends `\r\n`; no value is Err `<series>.txt holds no level`.
  - `net_fixed1` (the rule the tests sample but do not determine; T5-R19, R6-phase0-56): `v = value.trim().parse::<f64>()`, "" when that fails or `v` is not finite. Write `|v|` with 15 significant digits, `format!("{:.14e}", v.abs())`, as the 15-digit integer `m` (the digits without the point) and the exponent `e`. The value tenths are `n = m` times 10 to the power `e - 13` when `e >= 13`; otherwise, with `d = 10u128.pow(13 - e)`, `n = (m + d / 2) / d` when `13 - e <= 15`, else `n = 0` (half away from zero on the 15 digits). The text is `-` when `v < 0` and `n > 0`, then `n / 10`, `.`, `n % 10`; arithmetic in `u128`. Only if Step 1 printed `-0.0` for `-0.04` is the `-` written instead whenever `v.is_sign_negative()`.
  - `parse_streamhash`: lines as `series_file` splits them; a line matching `(?i)^([0-9]+),a,MD5=([0-9a-f]{32})$` with `k < audio_streams` sets `k`'s hash (a later line for the same `k` replaces it, the hash kept as written); fewer than `audio_streams` distinct `k` is Err `streamhash.txt holds <m> of <n> stream hashes`; Ok sorted by `k`.
  - `manifest_text`: the test's four line forms; `seconds` written as `seconds.round_ties_even() as i64` (PowerShell's `[int]`); each of codec, profile, layout and language written as `series_file`'s `<word>` (`-` when absent or empty); ` layout_guessed=<name>` after the layout when `centre(stream, layouts).guessed` is Some, for the main stream and each candidate; ` fc=yes` or ` fc=no` on the main line only; `frames=` and `md5=` from the two lists by stream number (empty when absent); `MANIFEST_LINE` followed by ` (experiment 13)` as the first line; every line ends `\r\n`.
  - `last_peak` and `peak_clipped`: lines as `series_file` splits them; the text after `lavfi.astats.Overall.Peak_level=` on the last line that starts with it, trimmed; clipped when the trimmed text holds neither `inf` nor `nan` and parses to a value `>= CLIP_DBFS`.
  - `proxy_check`: a JSON value is compared as its text (a string as written, a number in its decimal form, absent or null as ""); tag names are matched ASCII case-insensitively; per track `k` with `where` = `proxy track {k} (stream {stream} {series})`, in this order: the count (`proxy check failed: the proxy has {got} tracks, {want} were written`), the format (`codec_type` audio, `codec_name` flac, `sample_rate` 8000, `channels` 1, `bits_per_raw_sample` 24, else `proxy check failed: {where} is {codec_type} {codec_name} {sample_rate} Hz {channels} ch {bits_per_raw_sample} bit, not flac 8000 Hz 1 ch 24 bit`), the tags (else `proxy check failed: {where} is tagged stream {source} {series}`), the duration (`DURATION` matching `^([0-9]+):([0-9]{2}):([0-9]{2}(\.[0-9]+)?)$` gives hours times 3600 plus minutes times 60 plus seconds; none or not above 0 is `proxy check failed: {where} has no duration (the file was not finished)`); JSON that does not parse is `proxy check failed: proxy-check.json does not parse: {serde_json's error}`.
  - `proxy_json`: a `serde_json::Value` built with `json!` in phase 0's key order (the test's three key lists; `proxy` is `null` or `{"file": "audio-proxy.mka", "bytes", "tracks"}`), `encoding.chain` = `aresample=8000,volume={gain_db}dB,aformat=sample_fmts=s32`, `encoding.read` = `add {-gain_db} dB in float, convert to the source stream's sample_fmt, then measure (lazymkv-dev levels-from-proxy)`, `mix`, `fc`, `side` and `not_kept` as the test's strings (audio-levels.ps1 lines 434 to 436 and 441), each track's `duration_s` as `(d * 1000.0).round_ties_even() / 1000.0`, then `serde_json::to_string_pretty` and `"\n"`.

### Task 17: Step 10a's two passes, the -30 dB redo and the decision inputs (design 5.7, 7.6, 5.10; C1, call 22; T5-R13, T5-R38, T5-R39, T5-R48, T5-R55 to T5-R57)

Every kept title of every job now gets spec 6.4's step 10a. With `keep_tuning_evidence` on, one `ffmpeg` pass over the staged file writes phase 0's level folder and the compact audio proxy as FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec) in Matroska, made again at -30 dB (decibels) when it clips at -18 dB (C1) and kept as a proxy-less `audio-proxy.json` when it clips at -30 dB too (call 22). With the setting off, one pass hashes the audio packets without decoding. Each pass runs in a local work folder (T5-R39), and its files reach the job folder and the staged tuning folder only through Task 14's checked copy, the staged level folder's `audio-proxy.json` last (T5-R13). The decision inputs then carry the packet MD5 (Message Digest 5) values and the level measures, in memory and after a restart, and dev's reader learns the bare `streamhash.txt` of a setting-off job (design part 5.10). The job.log line of S33 goes. Task 16 gave the pure pieces (`core::audio::pass`); this task runs them.

**Tier and risk:** opus; risk high (a whole title's decode in the engine, every job's file phase gains a pass, the staged folder's write order is C3's marker, S33 goes).

**Covers:** R1-evidence-1, 2, 3 (the command run), 5, 6, 7 (the pass's failure classes), 8, 9, 10, 13, 14, 15, 18, 19, 20, 31; R5-code-19, 20 (the S33 test), 26, 28, 31 (audio), 32, 33, 78 (the `ffmpeg` stand-in's answers), 79; R6-phase0-54, 59.

#[test]
fn an_in_cwd_target_is_the_bare_name_and_a_path_is_refused() {
    let create = |json: &str| serde_json::from_str::<Create>(json).unwrap();
    let pass = args(&["-v", "warning", "-i", "raw.mkv", "-/filter_complex", "graph.txt"]);
    assert_eq!(create(r#"{"in_cwd":"peak-0.txt","copy_from":"s"}"#).target(&pass), Ok(PathBuf::from("peak-0.txt")));
    let path = "creates: in_cwd names a file of the working folder, not a path".to_string();
    assert_eq!(create(r#"{"in_cwd":"redo/peak-0.txt","copy_from":"s"}"#).target(&pass), Err(path.clone()));
    assert_eq!(create(r#"{"in_cwd":"..\\peak-0.txt","copy_from":"s"}"#).target(&pass), Err(path));
    assert_eq!(

    );
}

```rust
/// A rip label as a job run with keep_tuning_evidence off leaves it (design parts 5.10, 7.1): no level folder, a bare
/// streamhash.txt, and the probe whose audio streams, in file order, its lines name (streams 1 and 3; 2 is a subtitle).
fn bare_label(streamhash: &str, probe: bool) -> MemTree {
    let mut tree = MemTree::new("rec", "rec");
    if probe {
        tree.insert_file(
            "t00-00800/ffprobe-streams.json",
            concat!(
                r#"{"streams":[{"index":0,"codec_type":"video","codec_name":"h264"},"#,
                r#"{"index":1,"codec_type":"audio","codec_name":"dts","channels":6},"#,
                r#"{"index":2,"codec_type":"subtitle","codec_name":"hdmv_pgs_subtitle"},"#,
                r#"{"index":3,"codec_type":"audio","codec_name":"ac3","channels":2}]}"#
            ),
        );
    }
    tree.insert_file("t00-00800/streamhash.txt", streamhash);
    tree
}

const HASHES: &str = "0,a,MD5=0f343b0931126a20f133d67c2b018a3b\n1,a,MD5=9e107d9d372bb6826bd81d3542a419d6\n";

#[test]
fn decide_reads_a_bare_streamhash_txt_when_no_level_folder_holds_md5s() {
    let label = PathKey::new("t00-00800");
    assert_eq!(
        read_level_md5(&bare_label(HASHES, true), &label),
        Ok(vec![
            (Some(1), Some("0f343b0931126a20f133d67c2b018a3b".to_string())),
            (Some(3), Some("9e107d9d372bb6826bd81d3542a419d6".to_string())),
        ])
    );
    // A level folder that holds MD5 values wins, and the bare file is not read.
    let mut tree = bare_label(HASHES, true);
    tree.insert_file(
        "t00-00800/audio-levels-20ms-1/manifest.txt",
        concat!(
            "# lazymkv audio-levels v2 (experiment 13)\n",
            "file=title_t00.mkv bytes=16 seconds=0 frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400\n",
            "main=1 codec=dts profile=- channels=6 layout=- layout_guessed=5.1 language=eng fc=yes frames=5 ",
            "md5=d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e\n"
        ),
    );
    assert_eq!(read_level_md5(&tree, &label), Ok(vec![(Some(1), Some("d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e".to_string()))]));
}

#[test]
fn a_bare_streamhash_txt_that_cannot_name_its_streams_is_refused() {
    let label = PathKey::new("t00-00800");
    let tree = bare_label(HASHES, false);
    let shown = tree.display(&label.join("streamhash.txt"));
    assert_eq!(read_level_md5(&tree, &label), Err(format!("{shown}: no ffprobe-streams.json beside it names its audio streams")));
    let tree = bare_label("0,a,MD5=0f343b0931126a20f133d67c2b018a3b\n", true);
    assert_eq!(read_level_md5(&tree, &label), Err(format!("{shown}: streamhash.txt holds 1 of 2 stream hashes")));
}

/// A rip label as a job run with keep_tuning_evidence on leaves it before its dataset copy (design part 7.5, T5-R13):
/// the level folder of main 1 and candidate 2 holds the manifest of those two and a streamhash.txt naming all three
/// audio streams of the probe, and no audio-proxy.json yet. Without the probe the folder's streamhash.txt adds nothing.
fn level_label(probe: bool) -> MemTree {
    let mut tree = MemTree::new("rec", "rec");
    if probe {
        tree.insert_file(
            "t00-00800/ffprobe-streams.json",
            concat!(
                r#"{"streams":[{"index":0,"codec_type":"video","codec_name":"h264"},"#,
                r#"{"index":1,"codec_type":"audio","codec_name":"dts","channels":6},"#,
                r#"{"index":2,"codec_type":"audio","codec_name":"ac3","channels":2},"#,
                r#"{"index":3,"codec_type":"audio","codec_name":"ac3","channels":2}]}"#
            ),
        );
    }
    tree.insert_file(
        "t00-00800/audio-levels-20ms-1-2/manifest.txt",
        concat!(
            "# lazymkv audio-levels v2 (experiment 13)\n",
            "file=title_t00.mkv bytes=16 seconds=0 frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400\n",
            "main=1 codec=dts profile=- channels=6 layout=- layout_guessed=5.1 language=eng fc=yes frames=5 ",
            "md5=0f343b0931126a20f133d67c2b018a3b\n",
            "cand=2 codec=ac3 profile=- channels=2 layout=stereo language=eng frames=5 ",
            "md5=9e107d9d372bb6826bd81d3542a419d6\n"
        ),
    );
    tree.insert_file(
        "t00-00800/audio-levels-20ms-1-2/streamhash.txt",
        concat!(
            "0,a,MD5=0f343b0931126a20f133d67c2b018a3b\n",
            "1,a,MD5=9e107d9d372bb6826bd81d3542a419d6\n",

}

fn a_level_folder_without_audio_proxy_json_gives_every_streams_md5_from_its_streamhash_txt() {
    let label = PathKey::new("t00-00800");
    let md5 = |text: &str| Some(text.to_string());
    let (main, cand) = ((Some(1), md5("0f343b0931126a20f133d67c2b018a3b")), (Some(2), md5("9e107d9d372bb6826bd81d3542a419d6")));
    // Stream 3 is neither main nor candidate: only the folder's streamhash.txt names its MD5 (spec 6.4 step 10a, D13).

    );
    assert_eq!(read_level_md5(&level_label(false), &label), Ok(vec![main, cand]));
}

```rust
/// The level folder step 10a writes for movie-direct: main stream 1, no candidate (levels-args' first line).
const LEVELS: &str = "audio-levels-20ms-1";

/// The files of movie-direct's level folder in the job folder, in name order: phase 0's names for a main stream with
/// a centre channel and no candidate, without the audio-proxy.json that only the dataset copy adds (T5-R13).
const LEVEL_FILES: [&str; 10] = [
    "command.txt", "ffmpeg.txt", "ffprobe.txt", "graph.txt", "main-fc.txt", "main-mix.txt", "manifest.txt",
    "proxy-check.json", "streamhash.txt", "streams.json",
];

/// movie-direct's one audio stream's packet MD5 (corpus/scenarios/movie-direct/streamhash-1.txt).
const MD5: &str = "0f343b0931126a20f133d67c2b018a3b";

/// The harness's tuning evidence on (its defaults keep it off, R5-code-79).
fn evidence_on() -> Value {
    json!({"keep_tuning_evidence": true})
}

/// `<staging>/<job id>/tuning/<KEY>`, the staged tuning folder (design part 7.5).
fn staged(h: &Harness, id: &str) -> PathBuf {
    h.staging().join(id).join("tuning").join(KEY)
}

/// `<data>/work/levels-<job id>-<KEY>`, step 10a's work folder (T5-R39).
fn work(h: &Harness, id: &str) -> PathBuf {
    h.data().join("work").join(format!("levels-{id}-{KEY}"))
}

fn job_log(h: &Harness, id: &str) -> String {
    fs::read_to_string(h.job_dir(id).join("job.log")).unwrap()
}

/// The spawns whose arguments hold every needle, each as a substring of some argument (as the stand-ins match).
fn spawns_holding(h: &Harness, needles: &[&str]) -> Vec<Spawn> {
    h.spawns().into_iter().filter(|s| needles.iter().all(|n| s.args.iter().any(|a| a.contains(n)))).collect()
}

/// R-B1: decide.json without its two extra keys is what dev's readers render over the finished job folder.
fn assert_dev_renders_decide_json(h: &Harness, id: &str) {
    let dir = h.job_dir(id);
    let ctx = Ctx::for_test(h.data());
    let (rec, label) = rec_folder(&ctx, &dir.join(KEY).display().to_string()).unwrap_or_else(|r| panic!("{}", r.line));
    let options = PlanOptions {
        settings: Some(dir.join("settings.json")),
        tmdb_search: Some(dir.join("tmdb-search.json")),
        tmdb_record: Some(dir.join("tmdb-record.json")),
        remembered: None,
    };
    let read = read_decide_inputs(&ctx, &rec, &label, None, None, &options).unwrap_or_else(|r| panic!("{}", r.line));
    let mut written = json_of(&dir.join(KEY).join("decide.json"));
    let object = written.as_object_mut().unwrap();
    object.remove("audio_rule_version");
    object.remove("lazymkv_version");
    assert_eq!(
        dumps(&written, Style::INDENT1_ASCII),
        dumps(&serde_json::to_value(decide_doc(&read)).unwrap(), Style::INDENT1_ASCII)
    );
}

```rust
#[test]
fn step_10a_writes_the_level_folder_and_the_proxy_into_the_staged_folder_and_the_level_folder_into_the_job_folder() {
    let h = harness(&[], evidence_on());
    let id = run_to(&h, "Filed");
    let (levels, tuning) = (h.job_dir(&id).join(KEY).join(LEVELS), staged(&h, &id));
    assert_eq!(files_under(&levels), LEVEL_FILES.iter().map(|name| name.to_string()).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>());
    let mut expected: BTreeSet<String> = LEVEL_FILES.iter().map(|name| format!("{LEVELS}/{name}")).collect();
    expected.extend([format!("{LEVELS}/audio-proxy.json"), "audio-proxy.mka".to_string(), "audio-proxy.json".to_string()]);
    assert_eq!(files_under(&tuning), expected);
    for name in LEVEL_FILES {
        assert_eq!(fs::read(levels.join(name)).unwrap(), fs::read(tuning.join(LEVELS).join(name)).unwrap(), "{name}");
    }
    assert_eq!(fs::read(tuning.join("audio-proxy.mka")).unwrap(), b"lazymkv-test-proxy");
    assert_eq!(fs::read(tuning.join(LEVELS).join("audio-proxy.json")).unwrap(), fs::read(tuning.join("audio-proxy.json")).unwrap());
    let proxy = json_of(&tuning.join("audio-proxy.json"));
    assert_eq!((&proxy["format"], &proxy["slug"], &proxy["label"]), (&json!("lazymkv audio proxy v1"), &json!(id), &json!(KEY)));
    assert_eq!((&proxy["encoding"]["gain_db"], &proxy["proxy"]["file"]), (&json!(-18), &json!("audio-proxy.mka")));
    let tracks: Vec<(&Value, &Value)> =
        proxy["tracks"].as_array().unwrap().iter().map(|t| (&t["source_stream"], &t["series"])).collect();
    assert_eq!(tracks, [(&json!(1), &json!("mix")), (&json!(1), &json!("fc"))]);
    assert_eq!(fs::read_to_string(levels.join("streamhash.txt")).unwrap(), format!("0,a,MD5={MD5}\n"));
    let mix = fs::read_to_string(levels.join("main-mix.txt")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(mix.split("\r\n").skip(1).collect::<Vec<_>>(), ["-20.1", "-21.4", "-100.0", "-35.6", "-19.9", ""]);
    assert!(!h.job_dir(&id).join(KEY).join("streamhash.txt").exists(), "the bare copy is the setting-off pass's");
    let pass = spawns_holding(&h, &["-/filter_complex"]);
    assert_eq!(pass.len(), 1);
    assert!(pass[0].below_normal && pass[0].args.iter().any(|a| a == "graph.txt"));
    assert_eq!(pass[0].cwd.as_deref(), Some(work(&h, &id).as_path()));
    assert!(!work(&h, &id).exists());
    assert_eq!(fs::read_dir(h.data().join("work")).unwrap().count(), 0);
}

#[test]
fn the_staged_level_folders_audio_proxy_json_is_written_last() {
    let h = harness(&[], evidence_on());
    let id = format!("{}-1", h.fingerprint("movie-direct").to_ascii_lowercase());
    // A folder where the copy beside audio-proxy.mka lands: its rename fails, so the copies stop there.
    let blocker = staged(&h, &id).join("audio-proxy.json");
    h.on_spawn(&["-/filter_complex"], move || fs::create_dir_all(&blocker).unwrap());
    h.insert("tok0", "movie-direct");
    h.wait("DecisionFailed", |h| events(h, &id).iter().any(|e| matches!(e, Event::DecisionFailed { .. })));
    let tuning = staged(&h, &id);
    for name in LEVEL_FILES {
        assert!(tuning.join(LEVELS).join(name).is_file(), "{name}");
    }
    assert!(tuning.join("audio-proxy.mka").is_file());
    assert!(!tuning.join(LEVELS).join("audio-proxy.json").exists(), "C3's marker comes after every other file");
    assert!(!h.job_dir(&id).join(KEY).join(LEVELS).join("audio-proxy.json").exists());
}

#[test]
fn a_proxy_that_clips_at_minus_18_is_made_again_at_minus_30_and_nothing_else_changes() {
    let plain = harness(&[], evidence_on());
    let plain_id = run_to(&plain, "Filed");
    let h = harness(&["movie-direct-clip"], evidence_on());
    let id = run_to(&h, "Filed");
    let tuning = staged(&h, &id);
    assert_eq!(fs::read(tuning.join("audio-proxy.mka")).unwrap(), b"lazymkv-test-proxy-redo");
    let proxy = json_of(&tuning.join("audio-proxy.json"));
    assert_eq!((&proxy["encoding"]["gain_db"], &proxy["proxy"]["file"]), (&json!(-30), &json!("audio-proxy.mka")));
    let passes = spawns_holding(&h, &["-/filter_complex"]);
    assert_eq!(passes.len(), 2, "the first pass and the redo");
    assert!(passes[0].args.iter().any(|a| a == "null") && !passes[1].args.iter().any(|a| a == "null"), "only the first measures");
    assert_eq!(passes[1].cwd.as_deref(), Some(work(&h, &id).join("redo").as_path()));
    let (levels, plain_levels) = (h.job_dir(&id).join(KEY).join(LEVELS), plain.job_dir(&plain_id).join(KEY).join(LEVELS));
    for name in ["main-mix.txt", "main-fc.txt", "streamhash.txt", "graph.txt"] {
        assert_eq!(fs::read(levels.join(name)).unwrap(), fs::read(plain_levels.join(name)).unwrap(), "{name}");
    }
    let audio = |h: &Harness, id: &str| json_of(&h.job_dir(id).join(KEY).join("decide.json"))["audio"].clone();
    assert_eq!(audio(&h, &id), audio(&plain, &plain_id));
    let line = format!("{KEY}: the audio proxy of stream 1 (mix) clips at -18 dB, so the title's proxy is made again at -30 dB");
    assert!(job_log(&h, &id).contains(&line));
}
