```rust
    /// One job, `a-1` in `folder`, with the title t00-00800, its dataset copy `done` or not, and `tuning-root` as its own
    /// settings' `tuning_root`.
    fn one_job(folder: PathBuf, done: bool) -> impl Fn(&str) -> Option<CommandJob> {
        rooted_job(folder, done, Some("tuning-root"))
    }

    /// `one_job` with its own settings' `tuning_root` given (ENG-19).
    fn rooted_job(folder: PathBuf, done: bool, root: Option<&str>) -> impl Fn(&str) -> Option<CommandJob> {
        let root = root.map(str::to_string);
        move |id: &str| {
            (id == "a-1").then(|| CommandJob {
                folder: folder.clone(),
                keys: vec!["t00-00800".to_string()],
                dataset_done: done,
                tuning_root: root.clone(),
            })
        }
    }

    /// `<root>\recordings=<root>\dataset`, the engine's `--evidence` value (design part 9.5; G2).
    fn trees(root: &str) -> String {
        format!("{}={}", text(Path::new(root).join("recordings")), text(Path::new(root).join("dataset")))
    }

    /// Design part 9.5's table: `retune --jobs` is `retune --evidence <tuning_root>\recordings=<tuning_root>\dataset`,
    /// then the client's words without `--jobs`.
    #[test]
    fn retune_jobs_is_relayed_with_the_tuning_trees_first() {
        let job = one_job(PathBuf::from("jobs").join("a-1"), false);
        let given = words(&["retune", "--jobs", "--spec", "spec.md"]);
        let expected = vec!["retune".to_string(), "--evidence".to_string(), trees("tuning-root"), "--spec".to_string(),
                            "spec.md".to_string()];
        assert_eq!(child_words(&given, &job, Some("tuning-root")), Ok(expected));
    }

    /// G2: the client's `--evidence` values follow the engine's, in the order given, so retune reads them all.
    #[test]
    fn the_clients_evidence_follows_the_engines_and_accumulates() {
        let job = one_job(PathBuf::from("jobs").join("a-1"), false);
        let given = words(&["retune", "--jobs", "--evidence", "clone", "--subtitles", "--evidence", "more=text", "--spec",
                            "spec.md"]);
        let mut expected = vec!["retune".to_string(), "--evidence".to_string(), trees("tuning-root")];
        expected.extend(words(&["--evidence", "clone", "--subtitles", "--evidence", "more=text", "--spec", "spec.md"]));
        assert_eq!(child_words(&given, &job, Some("tuning-root")), Ok(expected));
    }

    /// T5-R32: no tuning_root, an empty one or one of spaces refuses `retune --jobs` naming the setting.
    #[test]
    fn retune_jobs_without_tuning_root_is_refused_naming_it() {
        assert_eq!(RETUNE_NO_TUNING_ROOT, "retune --jobs needs tuning_root in the engine's settings (design part 9.5)");
        let job = one_job(PathBuf::from("jobs").join("a-1"), false);
        for root in [None, Some(""), Some("   ")] {
            assert_eq!(child_words(&words(&["retune", "--jobs", "--spec", "spec.md"]), &job, root),
                       Err(RETUNE_NO_TUNING_ROOT.to_string()), "{root:?}");
        }
    }

    /// Call 14 and T5-R14: `--text <tuning_root>\dataset` after the replay flags once the dataset copy is done, never
    /// before, never without a tuning_root and never for plan; the root is the job's own settings' `tuning_root`, where
    /// its copy landed (ENG-19), not the engine's; a client's own `--text` comes after it and wins.
    #[test]
    fn decide_job_gets_text_once_the_dataset_copy_is_done_and_not_before() {
        let s = Scratch::new("relay-text");
        s.write("a-1/settings.json", "{}");
        let folder = s.0.join("a-1");
        let replay = vec!["--settings".to_string(), text(folder.join("settings.json"))];
        let mut head = vec!["decide".to_string(), "--rec".to_string(), text(folder.join("t00-00800"))];
        head.extend(replay.clone());
        let given = words(&["decide", "--job", "a-1", "--title", "t00-00800"]);
        let mut with_text = head.clone();
        with_text.extend(["--text".to_string(), text(Path::new("tuning-root").join("dataset"))]);
        assert_eq!(child_words(&given, &one_job(folder.clone(), true), Some("tuning-root")), Ok(with_text.clone()));
        assert_eq!(child_words(&given, &one_job(folder.clone(), false), Some("tuning-root")), Ok(head.clone()));
        // The owner moved the engine's tuning_root after the copy landed: the job's own root still names its dataset.
        assert_eq!(child_words(&given, &one_job(folder.clone(), true), Some("moved-root")), Ok(with_text.clone()));
        assert_eq!(child_words(&given, &one_job(folder.clone(), true), None), Ok(with_text.clone()));
        assert_eq!(child_words(&given, &rooted_job(folder.clone(), true, None), Some("tuning-root")), Ok(head.clone()));
        assert_eq!(child_words(&given, &rooted_job(folder.clone(), true, Some("  ")), Some("tuning-root")), Ok(head));
        let mut mine = given.clone();
        mine.extend(words(&["--text", "mine"]));
        with_text.extend(words(&["--text", "mine"]));
        assert_eq!(child_words(&mine, &one_job(folder.clone(), true), Some("tuning-root")), Ok(with_text));
        let mut plan = vec!["plan".to_string(), text(folder.clone())];
        plan.extend(replay);
        assert_eq!(child_words(&words(&["plan", "--job", "a-1"]), &one_job(folder, true), Some("tuning-root")), Ok(plan));
    }
```

```rust
/// `retune --jobs` through the relay (design part 9.5; G2, G3; calls 13, 25; T5-R32, T5-R53, T5-R60).
mod retune_jobs {
    use super::*;

    /// The spec retune reads, an absolute path, so lazymkvctl sends it again unchanged.
    const SPEC: &str = concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../../docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-04-lazymkv-design.md");
    /// A refresh manifest of made-up bytes, which only the refresh of a held job writes (T5-R16).
    const MANIFEST: &[u8] = b"made-up manifest bytes the relay never rewrites\n";

    fn recordings(h: &Harness) -> PathBuf { h.tuning().join("recordings") }

    /// The engine's `--evidence` value, `<tuning>/recordings=<tuning>/dataset`.
    fn trees(h: &Harness) -> String {
        format!("{}={}", text(recordings(h)), text(h.tuning().join("dataset")))
    }

    /// `<tuning>/recordings/<id>/` as the refresh leaves it: the job folder's `state.json` and each of `files`.
    fn mirror(h: &Harness, id: &str, files: &[&str]) -> PathBuf {
        let folder = recordings(h).join(id);
        fs::create_dir_all(&folder).unwrap();
        for file in ["state.json"].iter().chain(files) {
            fs::copy(h.job_dir(id).join(file), folder.join(file)).unwrap();
        }
        folder
    }

    /// An orphan `<tuning>/recordings/gone-1/`, no job of the engine's: the filed job's `state.json`,
    /// `lookup-status.txt` and three TMDb copies, its `tmdb.json` made stale, and `MANIFEST`.
    fn orphan(h: &Harness, id: &str) -> PathBuf {
        let folder = recordings(h).join("gone-1");
        fs::create_dir_all(&folder).unwrap();
        for file in ["state.json", "lookup-status.txt", "tmdb.json", "tmdb-record.json", "tmdb-search.json"] {
            fs::copy(h.job_dir(id).join(file), folder.join(file)).unwrap();
        }
        let mut copy = json_of(&folder.join("tmdb.json"));
        copy["fetched_at"] = json!("2026-01-01");
        fs::write(folder.join("tmdb.json"), serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&copy).unwrap()).unwrap();
        fs::write(folder.join(".lazymkv-refresh.json"), MANIFEST).unwrap();
        folder
    }

    fn record_asks(h: &Harness) -> usize {
        let url = lazymkv_clients::record_url(TmdbIdentity { kind: TmdbKind::Movie, id: 900001 });
        h.http().requests().iter().filter(|(u, _)| *u == url).count()
    }

    /// G2 end to end: lazymkvctl sends the clone made absolute, the engine puts its trees first, and one child
    /// carries both folders, with and without `--subtitles` (retune ignores the TEXTDIR half without it, T5-R53).
    #[test]
    fn retune_jobs_reads_the_engines_recordings_and_a_client_evidence_folder_in_one_run() {
        let (h, _) = filed();
        let scratch = Scratch::new("relay-retune-clone");
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&scratch.0);
        for extra in [&[][..], &["--subtitles"][..]] {
            let connector = h.client();
            let mut argv: Vec<String> = ["retune", "--jobs", "--evidence", "clone"].map(str::to_string).into();
            argv.extend(extra.iter().map(|word| word.to_string()));
            argv.extend(["--spec".to_string(), SPEC.to_string()]);
            let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
            let code = run(&argv, Env { ctx: &ctx, connector: Some(&connector), stdin: &mut &b""[..], out: &mut out,
                                        err: &mut err });
            let printed = (code, String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(), String::from_utf8(err).unwrap());
            assert_eq!(printed, (0, "relay retune line 1\n".to_string(), String::new()), "{extra:?}");
            let mut expected =
                vec!["retune".to_string(), "--evidence".to_string(), trees(&h), "--evidence".to_string(),
                     text(scratch.0.join("clone"))];
            expected.extend(extra.iter().map(|word| word.to_string()));
            expected.extend(["--spec", SPEC, "--spec", SPEC].map(str::to_string));
            assert_eq!(ctl_spawns(&h).pop().unwrap().args, expected, "{extra:?}");
        }
    }

    /// T5-R53: the engine's `--evidence DIR=TEXTDIR` names the text, so retune refuses a relayed `--text` with exit 2.
    #[test]
    fn retune_jobs_with_text_exits_2_naming_evidence_dir_equals_textdir() {
        let (h, _) = filed();
        let mut c = client(&h);
        let (_, reply) = c.command(&["retune", "--jobs", "--subtitles", "--text", "ocr", "--spec", SPEC]);
        assert_eq!(reply, exit(0, 1));
        let args = ctl_spawns(&h).pop().unwrap().args;
        let scratch = Scratch::new("relay-retune-text");
        let (mut out, mut err) = (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
        let code = lazymkv_dev::dispatch(&Ctx::for_test(&scratch.0), &args, &mut out, &mut err);
        let err = String::from_utf8(err).unwrap();
        assert_eq!((code, out.is_empty()), (2, true), "{err}");
        assert!(err.ends_with("lazymkv-dev retune: error: argument --text: not with --evidence DIR=TEXTDIR, which \
                               names the text already\n"), "{err}");
    }

    /// G3: a held job's stale copy is fetched into its job folder and refreshed into the recordings tree before the
    /// child starts (the spawn's action reads the tree's copy at the spawn).
    #[test]
    fn a_stale_copy_of_an_engine_job_is_fetched_into_its_job_folder_and_copied_across_before_the_child() {
        let (h, id) = filed();
        stale(&h, &id, "tmdb-record.json");
        let folder = mirror(&h, &id, &["tmdb-record.json"]);
        let seen = Arc::new(Mutex::new(None));
        {
            let (seen, copy) = (Arc::clone(&seen), folder.join("tmdb-record.json"));
            h.on_spawn(&["retune"], move || *seen.lock().unwrap() = Some(fs::read(&copy).unwrap()));
        }
        let mut c = client(&h);
        let (outputs, reply) = c.command(&["retune", "--jobs", "--spec", SPEC]);
        assert_eq!(reply, exit(0, 1));
        assert_eq!(outputs, [pair("stdout", "relay retune line 1")]);
        let job_copy = h.job_dir(&id).join("tmdb-record.json");
        assert_eq!(json_of(&job_copy)["fetched_at"], json!("2026-10-23"));
        assert_eq!(seen.lock().unwrap().take(), Some(fs::read(&job_copy).unwrap()),
                   "the recordings copy was refreshed before the child started");
        let log = fs::read_to_string(h.job_dir(&id).join("job.log")).unwrap();
        assert!(log.contains("the TMDb copy tmdb-record.json was fetched again"), "{log}");
    }

    /// G3 and R4-commands-44: without a token a held job's stale copy refuses the run with exit 3 naming the job and
    /// the copy; no child runs and the job stays Filed.
    #[test]
    fn without_a_token_a_stale_engine_copy_exits_3_naming_it() {
        let (h, id) = filed();
        stale(&h, &id, "tmdb-record.json");
        mirror(&h, &id, &["tmdb-record.json"]);
        no_token(&h);
        let mut c = client(&h);
        let (outputs, reply) = c.command(&["retune", "--jobs", "--spec", SPEC]);
        assert_eq!(reply, exit(3, 1));
        let line = format!("lazymkvctl: job {id}: tmdb-record.json: the TMDb copy is more than six months old \
                            (fetched_at 2026-01-01) and could not be fetched again: no tmdb_token is set");
        assert_eq!(outputs, [pair("stderr", &line)]);
        assert!(ctl_spawns(&h).is_empty());
        assert_eq!(h.state_of(&id), "Filed");
    }

    /// Call 25 and T5-R60: an orphan's stale copy is fetched into the recordings folder itself as the answer's pretty
    /// JSON and a final newline, through `<name>.partial`, and the refresh manifest is left as it was.
    #[test]
    fn an_orphans_stale_copy_is_fetched_into_its_recordings_folder() {
        let (h, id) = filed();
        let folder = orphan(&h, &id);
        let before = record_asks(&h);
        let mut c = client(&h);
        let (outputs, reply) = c.command(&["retune", "--jobs", "--spec", SPEC]);
        assert_eq!(reply, exit(0, 1));
        let fetched = format!("lazymkvctl: {}: the TMDb copy tmdb.json was fetched again", folder.display());
        assert_eq!(outputs, [pair("stderr", &fetched), pair("stdout", "relay retune line 1")]);
        let bytes = fs::read(folder.join("tmdb.json")).unwrap();
        let mut pretty = serde_json::to_vec_pretty(&json_of(&folder.join("tmdb.json"))).unwrap();
        pretty.push(b'\n');
        assert_eq!(bytes, pretty);
        assert_eq!(json_of(&folder.join("tmdb.json"))["fetched_at"], json!("2026-10-23"));
        assert_eq!(bytes, fs::read(h.job_dir(&id).join("tmdb.json")).unwrap(), "the answer the job folder holds");
        assert_eq!(record_asks(&h), before + 1);
        for entry in fs::read_dir(&folder).unwrap() {
            let name = entry.unwrap().file_name();
            assert!(!name.to_string_lossy().ends_with(".partial"), "{name:?}");
        }
        assert_eq!(fs::read(folder.join(".lazymkv-refresh.json")).unwrap(), MANIFEST);
        assert!(!h.job_dir("gone-1").exists());
    }

    /// Call 25: an orphan whose fetch fails is a standard-error line and the child still runs; the run is not exit 3.
    #[test]
    fn an_orphan_whose_fetch_fails_is_unmeasured_and_the_run_does_not_exit_3() {
        let (h, id) = filed();
        let folder = orphan(&h, &id);
        let stale_bytes = fs::read(folder.join("tmdb.json")).unwrap();
        no_token(&h);
        let mut c = client(&h);
        let (outputs, reply) = c.command(&["retune", "--jobs", "--spec", SPEC]);
        assert_eq!(reply, exit(0, 1));
        let line = format!("lazymkvctl: {}: tmdb.json: the TMDb copy is more than six months old (fetched_at \
                            2026-01-01) and could not be fetched again: no tmdb_token is set; retune reports the \
                            folder as unmeasured", folder.display());
        assert_eq!(outputs, [pair("stderr", &line), pair("stdout", "relay retune line 1")]);
        assert_eq!(ctl_spawns(&h).len(), 1);
        assert_eq!(fs::read(folder.join("tmdb.json")).unwrap(), stale_bytes);
    }
}
```

```rust
    /// `retune --jobs` (design part 9.5; G3, call 25): `child_words` accepted it, so the engine's settings hold a
    /// `tuning_root`; every job the owner holds goes to `spawn_retune_refetch` with its refetch, which lists
    /// `<tuning_root>\recordings` on its own thread, and the command runs with no child until its
    /// `Msg::CommandRefetched`. Def: T5-22. Use: T5-22.
    fn retune_jobs(&mut self, client: u64, id: Option<u64>, words: Vec<String>) {
        let root = self.store.settings().0.tuning_root.unwrap_or_default();
        let jobs: Vec<(String, CommandRefetch)> = self.jobs.iter().map(|(job_id, job)| (job_id.clone(), CommandRefetch {
            job_dir: self.store.job_dir(job_id),
            plan: job.record.plan.clone(),
            lookups: Arc::clone(&job.lookups),
            http: Arc::clone(&self.parts.http),
            token: self.parts.secrets.get("tmdb_token"),
            today: self.parts.host.local_date(),
            store: Arc::clone(&self.store),
        })).collect();
        let work = RetuneRefetch {
            recordings: Path::new(&root).join("recordings"),
            jobs,
            http: Arc::clone(&self.parts.http),
            token: self.parts.secrets.get("tmdb_token"),
            today: self.parts.host.local_date(),
        };
        self.command = Some(RunningCommand { client, id, kill: None });
        spawn_retune_refetch(work, client, id, words, self.sender.clone());
    }
```

```rust
use super::licenses::{licenses_text, CRATE_NOTICES, MIT_TEXT, TMDB_ADDRESS, TMDB_NOTICE};
use super::models::export_models;
use lazymkv_ocr_models::{
    ATTRIBUTION, DETECTION, DETECTION_LEN, DETECTION_NAME, DETECTION_SHA256, LICENCE_TEXT, RECOGNITION,
    RECOGNITION_LEN, RECOGNITION_NAME, RECOGNITION_SHA256,
};
use sha2::{Digest, Sha256};

/// `text` with a final newline, added when it has none (as licenses_text ends each part).
fn ended(text: &str) -> String {
    if text.ends_with('\n') { text.to_string() } else { format!("{text}\n") }
}

fn sha256_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String {
    Sha256::digest(bytes).iter().map(|byte| format!("{byte:02x}")).collect()
}

/// The four parts every `licenses` prints, in order; licenses_text joins its parts with "\n".
fn four_parts() -> Vec<String> {
    vec![
        format!("lazymkv: the MIT License\n\n{}", ended(MIT_TEXT)),
        format!("The ocrs models: CC-BY-SA-4.0\n\n{ATTRIBUTION}\n{}", ended(LICENCE_TEXT)),
        format!("The Movie Database (TMDB)\n\n{TMDB_NOTICE}\n{TMDB_ADDRESS}\n"),
        ended(CRATE_NOTICES),
    ]
}

#[test]
fn licenses_prints_its_five_parts_in_order() {
    let s = Scratch::new("ctl-licenses-five");
    s.write("release/licenses/zlib.txt", "made-up zlib licence\n");
    s.write("release/licenses/GPL-2.0.txt", "made-up GPL licence");
    s.write("release/licenses/nested/inner.txt", "made-up nested file\n");
    let exe = s.0.join("release").join("bin").join("lazymkvctl.exe");
    let mut parts = four_parts();
    parts.push("Bundled tool licence: GPL-2.0.txt\n\nmade-up GPL licence\n".to_string());
    parts.push("Bundled tool licence: zlib.txt\n\nmade-up zlib licence\n".to_string());
    assert_eq!(licenses_text(Some(&exe)).unwrap(), parts.join("\n"));
}

#[test]
fn export_models_writes_both_files_with_the_pinned_sha256() {
    let s = Scratch::new("ctl-export");
    let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&s.0);
    let (code, out, err) = ctl(&ctx, &["export-models", "models"]);
    let detection = s.0.join("models").join(DETECTION_NAME);
    let recognition = s.0.join("models").join(RECOGNITION_NAME);
    assert_eq!((code, String::from_utf8(err).unwrap()), (0, String::new()));
    assert_eq!(
        String::from_utf8(out).unwrap(),
        format!("wrote {}\nwrote {}\n", detection.display(), recognition.display())
    );
    let (d, r) = (std::fs::read(&detection).unwrap(), std::fs::read(&recognition).unwrap());
    assert_eq!((d.len(), r.len(), d.len() + r.len()), (DETECTION_LEN, RECOGNITION_LEN, 12_212_656));
    assert_eq!(sha256_hex(&d), DETECTION_SHA256);
    assert_eq!(sha256_hex(&r), RECOGNITION_SHA256);
    assert!(d == DETECTION && r == RECOGNITION, "byte-identical to the embedded models");
}

#[test]
fn export_models_refuses_an_existing_file_and_writes_neither() {
    for existing in [DETECTION_NAME, RECOGNITION_NAME] {
        let s = Scratch::new("ctl-export-refuse");
        s.write(&format!("models/{existing}"), "made-up model");
        let target = s.0.join("models").join(existing);
        let message = format!("{} exists; export-models writes neither file over an existing one", target.display());
        let ctx = Ctx::for_test(&s.0);
        let (code, out, err) = ctl(&ctx, &["export-models", "models"]);
        assert_eq!((code, out), (2, vec![]), "{existing}");
        assert_eq!(String::from_utf8(err).unwrap(), format!("lazymkvctl export-models: error: {message}\n"));
        assert_eq!(export_models(&s.0.join("models")), Err(message));
        assert_eq!(std::fs::read(&target).unwrap(), b"made-up model");
        let names: Vec<std::ffi::OsString> =
            std::fs::read_dir(s.0.join("models")).unwrap().map(|entry| entry.unwrap().file_name()).collect();
        assert_eq!(names, [std::ffi::OsString::from(existing)], "neither model was written");
    }
}

    assert!(!s.0.join("a").exists(), "an argument error writes nothing");
}

        assert!(!lazymkv_dev::COMMANDS.iter().any(|(command, _, _)| *command == name), "{name}");
    }
}

/// E1 and call 26: once the notices are committed, the CI job fails on a difference and still uploads the

#[test]
fn the_ci_notices_job_fails_when_the_committed_notices_differ() {
    let path = concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/../../.github/workflows/ci.yml");
    let ci = std::fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("{path}: {error}"));
    let job = &ci[ci.find("  notices:").expect("the notices job")..];
    let upload = job.find("- name: Upload the generated notices").expect("the upload step");
    let compare = job.find("- name: Compare with the committed notices").expect("the comparison step");
    assert!(upload < compare, "the artifact is uploaded before the comparison can fail");
    assert!(job[compare..].contains("if ! diff -u crates/ctl/crate-notices.txt crate-notices.txt; then"));
    assert!(job[compare..].contains("exit 1"));
    let lower = ci.to_lowercase();
    assert!(!lower.contains("report only") && !lower.contains("is not committed yet"));
}
```

What this task builds: design part 12.1's second test layer. Real mkvmerge, ffprobe and ffmpeg run on short Matroska files that the test makes (from ffmpeg's lavfi sources, libavfilter's virtual input, or from `core::testsupport::mks`), through the drivers the engine uses, which catches wrong command lines and wrong parsing of real output that the stand-ins cannot. CI installs MKVToolNix on all three runners and an FFmpeg at or above 7.0 on each (call 20, K11): ubuntu's apt FFmpeg is 6.1, so ubuntu takes a static 7.x build pinned by uniform resource locator (URL) and Secure Hash Algorithm 256 (SHA-256) digest; windows takes MKVToolNix by its installer, pinned the same way (call 20 over design 12.1's package managers, T5-R49). K11's skip below 7.0 stays as the rule for a machine without a new enough copy; on CI, where every runner installs the three tools, a missing tool or an older FFmpeg fails the test instead of skipping, as Task 13's cross-check already does for a missing ffprobe, so a green run proves that layer 2 ran.

```rust
//! Layer 2 of the tests (design part 12.1, G1; calls 20 and 24; T5-R49): the real mkvmerge, ffprobe and ffmpeg on
//! short Matroska files made during the test, from ffmpeg's lavfi sources (libavfilter's virtual input) or from
//! `core::testsupport::mks`, through the drivers the engine uses. Each tool comes from LAZYMKV_TEST_MKVMERGE,
//! LAZYMKV_TEST_FFPROBE or LAZYMKV_TEST_FFMPEG, else the first match on PATH, and ffmpeg and ffprobe must be FFmpeg
//! 7.0 or later (K11). Without a tool, or with an older FFmpeg, a test prints `skipped: <reason>` and passes; on CI
//! (`CI` set), where every runner installs the three, it fails instead, so a green run proves that layer 2 ran. Every
//! file is made up: block shapes and sine tones, no byte of the evidence clone (RP21).

use std::collections::BTreeSet;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
use std::process::Command;
use std::time::Duration;

use lazymkv_core::audio::levels::parse_levels;
use lazymkv_core::audio::pass::{
    centre, ffmpeg_args, graph, last_peak, parse_layouts, parse_streamhash, pass_streams, peak_clipped, proxy_check,
    series_file, GAIN_FIRST_DB,
};
use lazymkv_core::disc::StreamKind;
use lazymkv_core::ipc::OutputStream;
use lazymkv_core::job::Tool;
use lazymkv_core::recording::files::PacketsFile;
use lazymkv_core::subtitle::bitmap::mkv::read_stream;
use lazymkv_core::subtitle::bitmap::CODEC_PGS;
use lazymkv_core::testsupport::mks::{mks, pgs_display_set, MksBlock, MksEncoding, MksShape, MksTrack};
use lazymkv_core::testsupport::{Scratch, ScratchExt};
use lazymkv_core::tracks::layout::{Layout, OutputTrack};
use lazymkv_core::verify::VerifyReport;
use lazymkv_platform::fakes::FakeHost;
use lazymkv_platform::StdProcessGuard;
use lazymkv_tools::{
    exe_name, extract, extract_args, ident, layouts_args, packets, packets_args, probe, proxy_check_args, remux,
    remux_args, run_ffmpeg, streamhash_args, CancelToken, Limits, ToolCtx,
};
use serde_json::json;

/// Layer 2's three tools, each with the variable that names it (design part 12.1).
const MKVMERGE: (&str, Tool) = ("LAZYMKV_TEST_MKVMERGE", Tool::Mkvmerge);
const FFPROBE: (&str, Tool) = ("LAZYMKV_TEST_FFPROBE", Tool::Ffprobe);
const FFMPEG: (&str, Tool) = ("LAZYMKV_TEST_FFMPEG", Tool::Ffmpeg);

/// The lavfi sources, 3 s each. VIDEO is a black 64 x 36 picture at 25 frames a second. SURROUND is 5.1 in ffmpeg's
/// order FL FR FC LFE BL BR: 440 Hz at 0.1 on the fronts, 1 kHz at 0.2 on the centre (a root mean square level of -17.0 dB), silence on
/// the LFE (low-frequency effects) channel, 300 Hz at 0.05 on the backs. STEREO is two equal channels of 700 Hz at
/// 0.1, so its side (0.5 L - 0.5 R) is silent. MONO is 500 Hz at 0.1.
const VIDEO: &str = "color=c=black:s=64x36:r=25:d=3";
const SURROUND: &str = "aevalsrc=0.1*sin(2*PI*440*t)|0.1*sin(2*PI*440*t)|0.2*sin(2*PI*1000*t)|0|0.05*sin(2*PI*300*t)|0.05*sin(2*PI*300*t):c=5.1:s=48000:d=3";
const STEREO: &str = "aevalsrc=0.1*sin(2*PI*700*t)|0.1*sin(2*PI*700*t):c=stereo:s=48000:d=3";
const MONO: &str = "aevalsrc=0.1*sin(2*PI*500*t):c=mono:s=48000:d=3";
```

```rust
#[test]
fn real_mkvmerge_keeps_zlib_on_a_pgs_track_and_ffprobe_lists_its_inflated_sizes() {
    let Some(tools) = real_tools(&[MKVMERGE, FFPROBE]) else { return };

    assert!(sizes.windows(2).all(|w| w[0] != w[1]), "the four made-up events need four sizes: {sizes:?}");
    // The raw file stores the PGS track plain, so any zlib in the evidence file is mkvmerge's own default (K1).
    let track = MksTrack { number: 1, kind: 17, codec_id: CODEC_PGS.to_string(), codec_private: Vec::new(),
        language: "eng".to_string(), encoding: MksEncoding::None };

    std::fs::create_dir_all(job.join("subs")).unwrap();
    let identified = env.run(|ctx| ident(ctx, mkvmerge, &raw, &job.join("mkvmerge.json"))).unwrap().unwrap();
    let kinds: Vec<(i64, &str, &str)> =
        identified.tracks.iter().map(|t| (t.id, t.r#type.as_str(), t.codec.as_str())).collect();
    assert_eq!(kinds, [(0, "subtitles", "HDMV PGS")]);
    let evidence = scratch.0.join("staging/j/evidence/t00.mks");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(evidence.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
    let args = extract_args(&evidence, &[0], &raw);
    assert_eq!(env.run(|ctx| extract(ctx, mkvmerge, &args, &job.join("evidence-mkvmerge.txt"))).unwrap(), Ok(()));
    let bytes = std::fs::read(&evidence).unwrap();
    let inflated: u64 = sizes.iter().sum();
    assert!((bytes.len() as u64) < inflated,
        "mkvmerge wrote {} bytes for {inflated} bytes of events, so it did not compress the PGS track (K1)", bytes.len());
    let stream = read_stream(&bytes, 0).unwrap();
    let by_reader: Vec<(i64, u64)> = stream.blocks.iter().map(|b| ((b.pts * 1000.0).round() as i64, b.size)).collect();
    let made: Vec<(i64, u64)> = times.iter().copied().zip(sizes.iter().copied()).collect();
    assert_eq!(by_reader, made, "mkvmerge kept each event's time and bytes");
    let listing = job.join("subs/sub-0.packets.json");
    assert_eq!(env.run(|ctx| packets(ctx, ffprobe, &packets_args(0, &evidence), &listing)).unwrap(), Ok(()));
    let listed: PacketsFile = serde_json::from_slice(&std::fs::read(&listing).unwrap()).unwrap();
    let by_ffprobe: Vec<(i64, u64)> = listed
        .packets()
        .iter()
        .map(|p| ((text(&p.pts_time).parse::<f64>().unwrap() * 1000.0).round() as i64, text(&p.size).parse().unwrap()))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(by_ffprobe, by_reader,
        "call 24: this runner's ffprobe lists other (pts ms, size) pairs than the reader over mkvmerge's file; stop and give the owner both lists");
    println!("cross-check over mkvmerge's file: {} packets, sizes {sizes:?}, equal in number, order and size", by_reader.len());
}

#[test]
fn real_ffmpeg_step_10a_pass_writes_phase_0s_level_files_over_a_lavfi_file() {
    let Some(tools) = real_tools(&[FFMPEG, FFPROBE]) else { return };
    let (ffmpeg, ffprobe) = (&tools[0], &tools[1]);
    let scratch = Scratch::new("layer2-pass");
    let env = Env::new();
    let raw = lavfi_mkv(ffmpeg, &scratch.0, &[(SURROUND, "eng"), (STEREO, "spa")]);
    let label = scratch.0.join("job/t00");
    let work = scratch.0.join("work/levels-j-t00");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&label).unwrap();
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&work).unwrap();
    let probed = env.run(|ctx| probe(ctx, ffprobe, &raw, &label.join("ffprobe-streams.json"))).unwrap().unwrap();
    let audio = pass_streams(&probed.streams);
    assert_eq!(audio.iter().map(|s| (s.index, s.channels)).collect::<Vec<_>>(), [(1, 6), (2, 2)]);
    let listed = env.run(|ctx| run_ffmpeg(ctx, ffmpeg, &layouts_args(), &work.join("ffmpeg-layouts.txt"), Some(&work)));
    let layouts = parse_layouts(&String::from_utf8_lossy(&listed.unwrap().unwrap().stdout)).unwrap();
    let main_centre = centre(&audio[0], &layouts);
    assert!(main_centre.has_fc && main_centre.guessed.is_none(), "{main_centre:?}");
    let graph = graph(&audio, 1, &[2], &layouts, true, GAIN_FIRST_DB);
    let series: Vec<(&str, &str)> = graph.series.iter().map(|s| (s.name.as_str(), s.raw.as_str())).collect();
    assert_eq!(series, [("main-mix", "raw-main-mix.txt"), ("main-fc", "raw-main-fc.txt"), ("cand-2", "raw-cand-2.txt")]);
    let proxy: Vec<(i64, &str)> = graph.proxy.iter().map(|t| (t.stream, t.series.as_str())).collect();
    assert_eq!(proxy, [(1, "mix"), (1, "fc"), (2, "mix"), (2, "side")]);
    std::fs::write(work.join("graph.txt"), &graph.text).unwrap();
    let args = ffmpeg_args(&raw.display().to_string(), &graph, true, Some("audio-proxy.mka.partial"));
    assert!(args.iter().any(|a| a == "-/filter_complex"), "K11: the pass hands its graph over as -/filter_complex graph.txt");
    let pass = env.run(|ctx| run_ffmpeg(ctx, ffmpeg, &args, &work.join("pass.txt"), Some(&work))).unwrap();
    pass.unwrap_or_else(|why| panic!("{why}: {}", read(&work.join("pass.txt.stderr"))));
    let hashes = parse_streamhash(&read(&work.join("streamhash.txt")), audio.len()).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(hashes.iter().map(|(k, _)| *k).collect::<Vec<_>>(), [0, 1]);
    for s in &graph.series {
        let file = series_file(&read(&work.join(&s.raw)), &s.name, "raw.mkv").unwrap();
        let header = format!(
            "# lazymkv audio levels v2: frame_ms=20 band_hz=300-3400 unit=dB floor=-100 series={} file=raw.mkv\r\n",
            s.name
        );
        assert!(file.starts_with(&header), "{}: {:?}", s.name, file.lines().next());
        assert!(file.ends_with("\r\n") && !file.replace("\r\n", "").contains('\n'), "{}: every line ends with CRLF", s.name);
        let values = parse_levels(&file).unwrap();
        assert!((149..=151).contains(&values.len()), "{}: {} frames of 20 ms for 3 s", s.name, values.len());
        assert!(values.iter().all(|v| (-100.0..=0.0).contains(v)), "{}: {values:?}", s.name);
        if s.name == "main-fc" {
            let mut sorted = values.clone();
            sorted.sort_by(f64::total_cmp);
            let median = sorted[sorted.len() / 2];
            assert!((median + 17.0).abs() <= 0.5, "main-fc's median is {median} dB; the centre's 1 kHz tone at 0.2 is -17.0 dB");
        }
    }
    assert!(work.join("audio-proxy.mka.partial").is_file());
    let check = env.run(|ctx| {
        run_ffmpeg(ctx, ffprobe, &proxy_check_args("audio-proxy.mka.partial"), &work.join("proxy-check.txt"), Some(&work))
    });
    check.unwrap().unwrap();
    let durations = proxy_check(&read(&work.join("proxy-check.json")), &graph.proxy).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(durations.len(), 4);
    assert!(durations.iter().all(|d| (2.9..=3.1).contains(d)), "{durations:?}");
    for (k, track) in graph.proxy.iter().enumerate() {
        assert_eq!(peak_clipped(&read(&work.join(&track.peak))), Ok(false), "proxy track {k} ({} {})", track.stream, track.series);
    }
    let side = last_peak(&read(&work.join(&graph.proxy[3].peak))).unwrap();
    assert!(side.contains("inf"), "the side of two equal channels is silent: {side}");
}

#[test]
fn real_ffmpeg_streamhash_pass_lists_every_audio_stream() {
    let Some(tools) = real_tools(&[FFMPEG]) else { return };
    let ffmpeg = &tools[0];
    let scratch = Scratch::new("layer2-streamhash");
    let env = Env::new();
    let raw = lavfi_mkv(ffmpeg, &scratch.0, &[(SURROUND, "eng"), (STEREO, "spa"), (MONO, "eng")]);
    let work = scratch.0.join("work/levels-j-t00");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&work).unwrap();
    let args = streamhash_args(&raw, "streamhash.txt");
    let run = env.run(|ctx| run_ffmpeg(ctx, ffmpeg, &args, &work.join("streamhash-ffmpeg.txt"), Some(&work))).unwrap();
    run.unwrap_or_else(|why| panic!("{why}: {}", read(&work.join("streamhash-ffmpeg.txt.stderr"))));
    let text = read(&work.join("streamhash.txt"));
    let hashes = parse_streamhash(&text, 3).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(hashes.iter().map(|(k, _)| *k).collect::<Vec<_>>(), [0, 1, 2]);
    assert!(hashes.iter().all(|(_, h)| h.len() == 32 && h.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit())), "{hashes:?}");
    assert_eq!(hashes.iter().map(|(_, h)| h).collect::<BTreeSet<_>>().len(), 3, "three streams, three digests");
    assert_eq!(parse_streamhash(&text, 4), Err("streamhash.txt holds 3 of 4 stream hashes".to_string()));
    assert!(!text.contains(",v,"), "only the audio streams are hashed: {text}");
}

#[test]
fn real_mkvmerge_identifies_and_remuxes_a_lavfi_file() {
    let Some(tools) = real_tools(&[MKVMERGE, FFMPEG]) else { return };
    let (mkvmerge, ffmpeg) = (&tools[0], &tools[1]);
    let scratch = Scratch::new("layer2-remux");
    let env = Env::new();
    let raw = lavfi_mkv(ffmpeg, &scratch.0, &[(SURROUND, "spa"), (STEREO, "eng")]);
    let job = scratch.0.join("job/t00");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(&job).unwrap();
    let identified = env.run(|ctx| ident(ctx, mkvmerge, &raw, &job.join("mkvmerge.json"))).unwrap().unwrap();
    let tracks: Vec<serde_json::Value> = identified
        .tracks
        .iter()
        .map(|t| json!({"id": t.id, "type": t.r#type, "language": t.properties.get("language"),
            "channels": t.properties.get("audio_channels")}))
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(tracks, [
        json!({"id": 0, "type": "video", "language": "und", "channels": null}),
        json!({"id": 1, "type": "audio", "language": "spa", "channels": 6}),
        json!({"id": 2, "type": "audio", "language": "eng", "channels": 2}),
    ]);
    let seconds = identified.container.properties.duration as f64 / 1e9;
    assert!((2.9..=3.1).contains(&seconds), "{seconds} s");
    // The layout puts the English stereo first and the Spanish 5.1 second, so the remux reorders the tracks.
    let track = |stream: u32, kind: StreamKind, language: Option<&str>, name: Option<&str>, default: bool, original: bool| {
        OutputTrack { stream, kind, language: language.map(String::from), name: name.map(String::from), default,
            forced: false, hearing_impaired: false, original }
    };
    let layout = Layout {
        tracks: vec![
            track(0, StreamKind::Video, None, None, true, false),
            track(2, StreamKind::Audio, Some("eng"), Some("Stereo"), true, false),
            track(1, StreamKind::Audio, Some("spa"), Some("Surround 5.1"), false, true),
        ],
        chapters_kept: true,
    };
    let staged = VerifyReport { duration_ok: true, expected_seconds: seconds, file_seconds: seconds, chapters_ok: true,
        scan_chapters: 0, file_chapters: 0, tracks_ok: true, pairs: vec![(0, Some(0)), (1, Some(1)), (2, Some(2))],
        extra_tracks: Vec::new(), unknown_removed: Vec::new(), mismatches: Vec::new(), unchecked: Vec::new(),
        read_errors: Vec::new(), ok: true };
    let partial = scratch.0.join("lib/.lazymkv-partial/t00.mkv.partial");
    std::fs::create_dir_all(partial.parent().unwrap()).unwrap();
    let args = remux_args(&partial, &layout, &staged, &raw).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(env.run(|ctx| remux(ctx, mkvmerge, &args, &job.join("remux-mkvmerge.txt"))).unwrap(), Ok(()));
    let out = env.run(|ctx| ident(ctx, mkvmerge, &partial, &job.join("final-mkvmerge.json"))).unwrap().unwrap();
    let facts: Vec<serde_json::Value> = out
        .tracks
        .iter()
        .map(|t| {
            let p = |key: &str| t.properties.get(key).cloned();
            json!({"id": t.id, "type": t.r#type, "language": p("language"), "name": p("track_name"),
                "default": p("default_track"), "forced": p("forced_track"),
                "hearing_impaired": p("flag_hearing_impaired"), "original": p("flag_original"),
                "channels": p("audio_channels")})
        })
        .collect();
    assert_eq!(facts, [
        json!({"id": 0, "type": "video", "language": "und", "name": null, "default": true, "forced": false,
            "hearing_impaired": false, "original": false, "channels": null}),
        json!({"id": 1, "type": "audio", "language": "eng", "name": "Stereo", "default": true, "forced": false,
            "hearing_impaired": false, "original": false, "channels": 2}),
        json!({"id": 2, "type": "audio", "language": "spa", "name": "Surround 5.1", "default": false, "forced": false,
            "hearing_impaired": false, "original": true, "channels": 6}),
    ]);
    let final_seconds = out.container.properties.duration as f64 / 1e9;
    assert!((2.9..=3.1).contains(&final_seconds), "{final_seconds} s");
}

#[test]
fn the_layer_2_skip_reads_ffmpegs_version_and_skips_below_7_0() {
    assert_eq!(below_7_0("ffmpeg version 6.1.1-3ubuntu5 Copyright (c) 2000-2023 the FFmpeg developers"),
        Some("ffmpeg version 6.1.1-3ubuntu5 is below FFmpeg 7.0, layer 2's minimum (K11)".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(below_7_0("ffprobe version n6.0 Copyright (c) 2007-2023 the FFmpeg developers"),
        Some("ffprobe version n6.0 is below FFmpeg 7.0, layer 2's minimum (K11)".to_string()));
    for line in [
        "ffmpeg version 7.0 Copyright (c) 2000-2024 the FFmpeg developers",
        "ffmpeg version n7.1.2-12-g0123abcd-20251020 Copyright (c) 2000-2025 the FFmpeg developers",
        "ffprobe version 9.0.2-full_build-www.gyan.dev Copyright (c) 2007-2026 the FFmpeg developers",
        "ffmpeg version 10.0 Copyright (c) 2000-2027 the FFmpeg developers",
    ] {
        assert_eq!(below_7_0(line), None, "{line}");
    }
    assert_eq!(below_7_0("ffmpeg version N-117000-g0123abcd Copyright (c) 2000-2025 the FFmpeg developers"),
        Some("ffmpeg version N-117000-g0123abcd names no release number, so layer 2 cannot tell that it is FFmpeg 7.0 or later (K11)".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(below_7_0("   "),
        Some("-version printed nothing, so layer 2 cannot tell that it is FFmpeg 7.0 or later (K11)".to_string()));
}
```

The made-up PGS events are Task 13's solid rectangles (no glyph, no font); the tones and the black picture are lavfi's. The level expectation of `main-fc` is the one value of a series this test pins: phase 0's centre chain is `pan=mono|c0=FC` (`scripts/phase0/audio-levels.ps1` line 283), so a 1 kHz tone of amplitude 0.2 measures 20 log10(0.2 / sqrt(2)) = -17.0 dB (decibels) through the 300 to 3400 Hz band; the mix and the candidate pass through ffmpeg's own mono downmix, whose gain the test does not pin. The silent side track is the edge of `peak_clipped`'s `inf` rule over real ffmpeg output.

Expected: the build fails with ``error[E0425]: cannot find function `real_tools` in this scope`` and the same for `lavfi_mkv`, `read`, `text` and `below_7_0`, and ``error[E0433]: failed to resolve: use of undeclared type `Env` ``.

  - `struct Env { host: FakeHost, limits: Limits, cancel: CancelToken }` with `fn new() -> Env` and `fn run<R>(&self, f: impl FnOnce(&ToolCtx) -> R) -> R`, as `crates/fake-tools/tests/mkvmerge_ffprobe_driver.rs:28-58` builds its `Env` (the same `FakeHost::new("2026-10-23", 1_800_000_000)` and `Limits { header: 120 s, scan: 60 s, exit_wait: 60 s, after_kill: 10 ms }`), with two differences: the guard is `&StdProcessGuard` itself (a real tool is not a freshly copied stand-in, so `BusyRetry` has nothing to retry) and `on_progress` ignores its fraction (no progress list, no watchdog). The 120 s header bound is a give-up bound, not a wait, so it does not scale by `ci_factor()`.
  - `fn read(path: &Path) -> String`: `std::fs::read_to_string`, panicking `<path>: <error>`.
  - `fn text(value: &Option<serde_json::Value>) -> String`: a JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) string as written, another value as its JSON form, None as `""` (ffprobe writes `pts_time` and `size` as strings), as Task 13's helper of the same name.
  - `fn below_7_0(first_line: &str) -> Option<String>`: None when the line names FFmpeg 7.0 or later, else the reason. The words are the line split on whitespace; none gives `-version printed nothing, so layer 2 cannot tell that it is FFmpeg 7.0 or later (K11)`. `<shown>` is the first three words joined by single spaces. The release word is the third when the second is `version`; its major number is the run of ASCII digits at its start after one leading lowercase `n` is removed (BtbN's `n7.1` builds). No digits gives `<shown> names no release number, so layer 2 cannot tell that it is FFmpeg 7.0 or later (K11)`; a major below 7 gives `<shown> is below FFmpeg 7.0, layer 2's minimum (K11)`.
  - `fn real_tool(var: &str, tool: Tool) -> Result<PathBuf, String>`: when `var` is set and not empty, its path, or Err `<var> names <path>, which is not a file` when that is not a file; otherwise the first `dir.join(exe_name(tool))` over `std::env::split_paths` of `PATH` that is a file, or Err `no <tool.as_str()> (set <var> or put <tool.as_str()> on PATH)`. For `Tool::Ffmpeg` and `Tool::Ffprobe` it then runs `<path> -version` with `std::process::Command` (an error is Err `<path> -version could not run: <error>`) and gives `below_7_0` of the first line of its standard output as the Err when Some.
  - `fn skip_or_fail(reason: &str)`: with `CI` set (`std::env::var_os("CI").is_some()`, as GitHub Actions sets it and `ci_factor` reads it), `panic!("layer 2 must run on CI (call 20, T5-R49): {reason}")`; else `lazymkv_dev::evidence::skip(reason)`.
  - `fn real_tools(wanted: &[(&str, Tool)]) -> Option<Vec<PathBuf>>`: `real_tool` of each in order; at the first Err, `skip_or_fail` of it and None; else the paths in `wanted`'s order. Each test checks its tools in the order it lists them, so the first missing one is the one its line names.
  - `fn lavfi_mkv(ffmpeg: &Path, dir: &Path, audio: &[(&str, &str)]) -> PathBuf`: runs the real ffmpeg with `std::process::Command`, `current_dir(dir)`, and these arguments, then gives `dir.join("raw.mkv")`. For `audio` = `[(s1, l1), ..., (sn, ln)]`: `-v error -nostdin -y -f lavfi -i <VIDEO>`, then `-f lavfi -i <sk>` for each source in order, then `-map 0:v`, then `-map <k>:a` for k = 1 to n, then `-c:v ffv1 -c:a flac`, then `-metadata:s:a:<k-1> language=<lk>` for each, then `-t 3 raw.mkv`. A spawn error panics `<ffmpeg> could not run: <error>`; an exit other than success panics `ffmpeg could not make the test file (lavfi, ffv1, flac, matroska): <its standard error, trimmed>`. FFV1 and FLAC (Free Lossless Audio Codec) are FFmpeg's own encoders, present in every build the runners install, so the file needs no external library. The streams are then 0 (video), 1 to n (audio), as a rip's are.

The mini PC is idle: no rip, no desktop-session job, no trial run. Nothing is installed (P24).

Run: `scripts/box.sh cargo test -p fake-tools --locked --test layer2`
Expected: `test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed`. `the_layer_2_skip_reads_ffmpegs_version_and_skips_below_7_0` runs; each of the other four either runs or prints one `skipped: no <tool> (set LAZYMKV_TEST_<TOOL> or put <tool> on PATH)` line, depending on what the Secure Shell (SSH) session's `PATH` holds (`box.sh` does not set `CI`, so nothing fails for a missing tool). Each `skipped:` line counts as not run (Global Constraints, Tests) and is listed in the evidence line.

Run, with the three paths Task 0 Step 7's `lazymkvctl selftest` reported for `mkvmerge`, `ffprobe` and `ffmpeg` (S80: each tool check carries its path), written with `%LOCALAPPDATA%` or `%ProgramFiles%` in place of the expanded user or program folder, so no Windows user name is typed: `scripts/box.sh "set LAZYMKV_TEST_MKVMERGE=<mkvmerge path>&& set LAZYMKV_TEST_FFPROBE=<ffprobe path>&& set LAZYMKV_TEST_FFMPEG=<ffmpeg path>&& cargo test -p fake-tools --locked --test layer2 -- --nocapture"`
Expected: `test result: ok. 5 passed; 0 failed`, no `skipped:` line, and the line `cross-check over mkvmerge's file: 4 packets, sizes [<four sizes>], equal in number, order and size` (mkvmerge 100.0, ffprobe and ffmpeg 9.0.2; R6-phase0-6). A `skipped:` line means a path is wrong: the controller reads it again by `scripts/phase0/env.ps1`'s rule (`PATH`, then `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\WinGet\Links`, then `C:\Program Files\WinGet\Links`) over plain `ssh` and runs the command again; the run does not count until no `skipped:` line prints.

A failure here is a finding, never a reason to loosen an assertion: a failed `assert_eq!(by_ffprobe, by_reader, ...)` is call 24's stop point (Step 9's message, with "the mini PC's FFmpeg 9.0.2" as the runner); a parser or driver that refuses real output goes to the controller, who reopens the owning task (Task 13 for the drivers and their argument lists, Task 16 for the graph, the series files, the stream hashes, the peaks and the proxy check) as its own fixing commit with a test before this task's commit; a failure inside `core::subtitle::bitmap` is a frozen path (T5-R54) and goes to the owner.

Evidence lines in `.superpowers/pr5/pr5-mini-pc-runs.txt`:
- `<yyyy-MM-dd>, SSH, layer 2 without the test variables on <short sha>: 5 passed, 0 failed, <k> skipped: lines (<the tools they name>)`.
- `<yyyy-MM-dd>, SSH, layer 2 with the installed mkvmerge <v>, ffprobe <v> and ffmpeg <v> on <short sha>: 5 passed, 0 failed, no skipped: line; the cross-check over mkvmerge's file: 4 packets equal in number, order and size`.

On the Mac, `grep -E '^(MKVToolNix (ubuntu|macos|windows)|FFmpeg ubuntu) ' .superpowers/pr5/decisions.txt` prints exactly four lines. Their values, each the words before its line's first comma (Task 0's form), are written into the workflow literally: `<apt version>` is the `MKVToolNix ubuntu` line's version string, `<macos version>` the `MKVToolNix macos` line's version, `<mkvtoolnix url>` and `<mkvtoolnix sha256>` the `MKVToolNix windows` line's two values, `<ffmpeg url>` and `<ffmpeg sha256>` the `FFmpeg ubuntu` line's two values. Any other output stops the task and goes to the controller (Task 0 Step 5 did not finish).

The header comment, lines 3 to 11 at `07ccc48`, becomes:

```yaml
# Every push to main and every pull request builds and tests the workspace on Linux, macOS and Windows with the
# toolchain rust-toolchain.toml pins. The private evidence repository is not cloned here, so the tests that need it
# print their "skipped: ..." reason and the rest run; docs/phase2/engine.md has the count. Among them, the stand-in
# tools of crates/fake-tools run a whole engine job, from a disc's arrival to a filed placeholder file, on every
# system (design part 12.6, item 2), and on Windows the platform's Windows implementations run too: the named pipe,
# the mutex, the Job Object runner, Credential Manager under a test name, and a native whole job through the real
# pipe (design parts 12.4 and 12.6, item 3). Tests that need the drive, the share or the owner's desktop session are
# ignored here and run on the mini PC.
#
# Layer 2 (design part 12.1, G1): every runner installs MKVToolNix and an FFmpeg of 7.0 or later (K11), each pinned
# (P33, call 20). Ubuntu takes MKVToolNix from apt at its pinned version and a static FFmpeg 7.x build whose SHA-256
# (Secure Hash Algorithm 256) digest is checked before anything in it runs, since apt's FFmpeg is 6.1; macOS takes
# both from Homebrew and checks mkvmerge's version against the pin; Windows takes FFmpeg from Chocolatey and
# MKVToolNix by its installer, checked against its SHA-256. Each job hands the three programs to the tests as
# LAZYMKV_TEST_MKVMERGE, LAZYMKV_TEST_FFPROBE and LAZYMKV_TEST_FFMPEG; the layer 2 tests
# (crates/fake-tools/tests/layer2.rs) and the ffprobe size cross-check fail here, instead of skipping, when one is
# missing or too old (T5-R49, call 24).
#
# The OCR (optical character recognition) models: the models job restores them from the cache keyed by their
# SHA-256 pins, and on a miss downloads them once through lazymkv-ocr-models' build script; the three test jobs only
# restore that cache (calls 2 and 3). lazymkv-ocr (rten and ocrs) builds, and its worker runs over a made-up
```

The three install steps of the `test` job (lines 42 to 52 at `07ccc48`, the steps named `Install ffmpeg (Linux)`, `Install ffmpeg (macOS)` and `Install ffmpeg (Windows)`) are replaced, in place, by:

```yaml
      # Layer 2 (design part 12.1, call 20): apt's FFmpeg is 6.1, below K11's 7.0, so ubuntu takes the pinned static
      # 7.x build, checked before anything in it runs, and MKVToolNix from apt at the pinned version (T5-R28).
      - name: Install FFmpeg 7.x and MKVToolNix (Linux)
        if: runner.os == 'Linux'
        shell: bash
        env:
          FFMPEG_URL: <ffmpeg url>
          FFMPEG_SHA256: <ffmpeg sha256>
          MKVTOOLNIX_VERSION: <apt version>
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          curl --fail --location --silent --show-error --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg.tar.xz" "$FFMPEG_URL"
          printf '%s  %s\n' "$FFMPEG_SHA256" "$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg.tar.xz" | sha256sum --check --strict -
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg"
          tar -xJf "$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg.tar.xz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg" --strip-components=1
          test -x "$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg"
          test -x "$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg/bin/ffprobe"
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends "mkvtoolnix=$MKVTOOLNIX_VERSION"
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"
          {
            echo "LAZYMKV_TEST_MKVMERGE=$(command -v mkvmerge)"
            echo "LAZYMKV_TEST_FFPROBE=$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg/bin/ffprobe"
            echo "LAZYMKV_TEST_FFMPEG=$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg" -version | sed -n 1p
          "$RUNNER_TEMP/ffmpeg/bin/ffprobe" -version | sed -n 1p
          mkvmerge --version

      # Homebrew's FFmpeg is above 7.0; its MKVToolNix must be the pinned version, so a formula that moved on fails
      # here and goes to the owner for a new pin (P33, T5-R28).
      - name: Install FFmpeg and MKVToolNix (macOS)
        if: runner.os == 'macOS'
        shell: bash
        env:
          MKVTOOLNIX_VERSION: <macos version>
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          brew install ffmpeg mkvtoolnix
          prefix="$(brew --prefix)"
          first="$("$prefix/bin/mkvmerge" --version | sed -n 1p)"
          echo "$first"
          case "$first" in
            "mkvmerge v$MKVTOOLNIX_VERSION "*) ;;
            *) echo "Homebrew installed $first, not the pinned MKVToolNix $MKVTOOLNIX_VERSION (P33)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          {
            echo "LAZYMKV_TEST_MKVMERGE=$prefix/bin/mkvmerge"
            echo "LAZYMKV_TEST_FFPROBE=$prefix/bin/ffprobe"
            echo "LAZYMKV_TEST_FFMPEG=$prefix/bin/ffmpeg"
          } >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          "$prefix/bin/ffmpeg" -version | sed -n 1p

      # Chocolatey's FFmpeg is above 7.0; MKVToolNix comes by its own installer, pinned by URL and SHA-256 and run
      # silently (call 20 over design part 12.1's package managers, T5-R49).
      - name: Install FFmpeg and MKVToolNix (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: pwsh
        env:
          MKVTOOLNIX_URL: <mkvtoolnix url>
          MKVTOOLNIX_SHA256: <mkvtoolnix sha256>
        run: |
          $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
          $ProgressPreference = 'SilentlyContinue'
          choco install ffmpeg -y --no-progress
          if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "choco install ffmpeg exited $LASTEXITCODE" }
          $setup = Join-Path $env:RUNNER_TEMP 'mkvtoolnix-setup.exe'
          Invoke-WebRequest -Uri $env:MKVTOOLNIX_URL -OutFile $setup
          $hash = (Get-FileHash -LiteralPath $setup -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLowerInvariant()
          if ($hash -ne $env:MKVTOOLNIX_SHA256) { throw "the MKVToolNix installer has SHA-256 $hash, not $env:MKVTOOLNIX_SHA256" }
          $install = Start-Process -FilePath $setup -ArgumentList '/S' -Wait -PassThru
          if ($install.ExitCode -ne 0) { throw "the MKVToolNix installer exited $($install.ExitCode)" }
          $mkvmerge = Join-Path $env:ProgramFiles 'MKVToolNix\mkvmerge.exe'
          if (-not (Test-Path -LiteralPath $mkvmerge)) { throw "$mkvmerge is not there after the install" }
          & $mkvmerge --version
          $ffmpeg = (Get-Command ffmpeg.exe).Source
          $ffprobe = (Get-Command ffprobe.exe).Source
          & $ffmpeg -version | Select-Object -First 1
          "LAZYMKV_TEST_MKVMERGE=$mkvmerge" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Append -Encoding utf8
          "LAZYMKV_TEST_FFPROBE=$ffprobe" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Append -Encoding utf8
          "LAZYMKV_TEST_FFMPEG=$ffmpeg" | Out-File -FilePath $env:GITHUB_ENV -Append -Encoding utf8
```

- [ ] **Step 13: The byte-for-byte check (SSH; call 9, R1-evidence-4, R5-code-25, R6-phase0-63, T5-R18; a stop point).** The controller writes this helper to `$SCRATCH/pr5-compare-series.ps1`, copies it with `scp -q -o BatchMode=yes "$SCRATCH/pr5-compare-series.ps1" "$LAZYMKV_BOX:C:/lazymkv/tmp/pr5-compare-series.ps1"` and deletes the scratch copy. It prints names and numbers only, never a line of a file (each header names the rip file):

```powershell
# Compares phase 0's level series with the engine's, byte for byte, header line included (T5-R18). Prints numbers only.
param([Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Phase0, [Parameter(Mandatory)][string]$Engine)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$pattern = '^(main-mix|main-fc|cand-\d+)\.txt$'
function Get-Series([string]$dir) { @(Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $dir -File | Where-Object { $_.Name -match $pattern } | ForEach-Object { $_.Name } | Sort-Object) }
$p = Get-Series $Phase0
$e = Get-Series $Engine
"series phase0 $($p -join ',') engine $($e -join ',')"
$bad = 0
if (($p -join ',') -ne ($e -join ',')) { $bad++ }
foreach ($name in $p) {
    if ($e -notcontains $name) { continue }
    $a = Join-Path $Phase0 $name
    $b = Join-Path $Engine $name
    fc.exe /b $a $b > $null
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) { "$name same bytes $((Get-Item -LiteralPath $a).Length)"; continue }
    $bad++
    $la = [IO.File]::ReadAllLines($a)
    $lb = [IO.File]::ReadAllLines($b)
    $diff = 0
    $first = 0
    for ($i = 0; $i -lt [math]::Max($la.Count, $lb.Count); $i++) {
        if ($la[$i] -cne $lb[$i]) { $diff++; if ($first -eq 0) { $first = $i + 1 } }
    }
    $header = if ($la[0] -ceq $lb[0]) { 'same' } else { 'differs' }
    "$name DIFFERENT bytes $((Get-Item -LiteralPath $a).Length) $((Get-Item -LiteralPath $b).Length) lines $($la.Count) $($lb.Count) differing $diff first $first header $header"
}
"RESULT $(if ($bad -gt 0) { 'DIFFERENT' } else { 'same' })"
```

## Declined

No blocking or important finding of the skeleton's two critiques (`.superpowers/pr5/plan/skeleton-critique-coverage.md` and `skeleton-critique-interfaces.md`, git-ignored) is declined outright, and every minor is applied. The items below were taken in part, or in a form other than the first one the critique offered, with the reason.

1. **Coverage finding 4** (the CI half of call 24 before the trial): taken in part. The CI cross-check is Task 13, after the trial and before step 10 (Task 14), not before the trial, because the packet driver it uses is one of the step 10 drivers that interfaces finding 5 moves after the trial. The trial measures no ffprobe size (Task 11's goldens check the mini PC's recorded packet lists, made with FFmpeg 9.0.2), so no engine task rests on the check before it runs.
2. **Coverage finding 5** (keep the worker's `.exit.json` and the reason in the job folder): declined in favour of interfaces finding 6's form, which copies none of the capture into the job folder. Design 7.1's table has no row for the worker's capture and a panic's standard error can hold text; the run's exit code and wall time are kept in `summary.json` and its `job.log` line (T5-R57).
3. **Interfaces finding 5** (split Task 9): applied as Tasks 9 and 13, with one addition: `Spawn` derives `Default` in Task 9 so that `crates/tools/src/ocr.rs`, frozen from the trial on (T5-R54), needs no edit when Task 13 adds `cwd`.
4. **Interfaces finding 7** (the engine's cap tests): taken in its second form, a `cap` function filled from the test-only `ocr_cap_override` (T5-R58), rather than paying the 60 s floor, which would add two unscaled 60 s waits per system on every push.
5. **Interfaces finding 11** (proof that the checked copy is used): the proof is the source-scan test `the_unit_moves_files_across_volumes_only_through_the_checked_copy` rather than a fault seam that refuses renames across the two roots, since the engine has no file-system layer to put such a seam in and the harness keeps the data folder and staging on one volume; the helper's own unit tests run across two temporary roots.
6. **Interfaces finding 15** (the notices job as its own task): taken in its second form; Task 7 says why the report-only job rides with the model cache (both are that task's `ci.yml` edits for the new packages, the job cannot fail before Task 23, and its first artifact is needed only there), rather than adding a task and a three-system CI round for no new risk.
7. **Coverage finding 16** (F1's "one rten build"): taken as the ruling T5-R52 (one build per run in the ubuntu job, no build cache), rather than an `actions/cache` of the target folder keyed by `Cargo.lock`, which the notes do not ask for and which would store a whole target folder per lock hash.
8. **Coverage finding 7** (`subs_run`'s refusal): the ruling T5-R51 gives an unread stream its own line in place of phase 0's "read it with ocr-subs.ps1" hint, which stays for phase 0's shape under its golden; the suggested test is therefore named `a_title_with_an_unread_stream_has_the_unread_line_as_its_subtitles_section`.
9. **Coverage finding 11** (R4-commands-57): T23 is added to the map rather than the id dropped from Task 23's Covers, since Task 23 commits the notices the template makes.
10. **Coverage finding 3 and interfaces finding 12** name different freeze lists; T5-R54 takes their union, with `Cargo.toml` and `Cargo.lock` standing for the ocrs and rten pins.

The plan's own review (`.superpowers/pr5/plan/plan-critique-coverage.md`, `plan-critique-consistency.md` and `plan-critique-rules.md`, git-ignored) is applied whole except for the parts below, each with its reason.

11. **Coverage finding 1, its engine scenario and its Task 19 check** (a stand-in disc with three audio streams, main, candidate and unmeasured, and the rendering after the copy): taken in part. The reader's new branch, a level folder without `audio-proxy.json` giving its own `streamhash.txt`'s pairs, is pinned in dev over a made-up label with three audio streams (Task 17 Step 5, `a_level_folder_without_audio_proxy_json_gives_every_streams_md5_from_its_streamhash_txt`), and the engine calls that reader unchanged on the job folder's label folder. A three-stream stand-in disc would need new scan, identify, probe, graph, peak and proxy-check answers whose values only a run could confirm, and over `movie-direct`'s one audio stream the Task 19 check could not tell the two readings apart.
12. **Rules finding 5 (proportion), parts (a) and (c)**: declined. The Interface sheet stays: subagent-driven execution hands each task its own text, and the sheet is the one place every cross-task name and signature is fixed; it was checked again line by line against the tasks after this review. Task 15 Step 11's and Task 17 Step 13's bodies stay, since they fix the write orders C3 rests on (T5-R12, T5-R13) and the sentences the tests pin, and Task 17 Step 13 now gives the loop's whole body (consistency finding 4). Part (b) is applied (the notes' section 4 is a pointer), and the sentences no test reached either got a test (`a_pass_that_leaves_no_hash_file_is_decision_failed` in Task 17, `a_worker_that_exits_0_without_records_leaves_each_stream_unread` in Task 15) or a note that no scenario reaches them.
13. **Coverage finding 2's engine test** (a held job whose staged tuning folder is removed, then approved): taken in another setup. A job held under this build already holds `tuning_copy: done` from its first DecisionDone, so the approval's DecisionDone owes no new copy, and only a rewritten `state.json` could stage pull request 4's record. `a_pending_copy_with_no_staged_tuning_folder_owes_nothing_and_the_cleanup_deletes_the_staging_data` (Task 19) takes a pending copy whose staged folder is gone through the same `start_copy`, `CopyEnd::Nothing`, `copy_ended` and cleanup path.

## Planner notes

The drafters' concerns, as the plan settles them. "Resolved" lines changed the task texts above when the plan was assembled; "carried" lines are decisions the drafter made inside its task, or checks only execution can make, and the executing task meets each one where it is named. The controller records any further ruling in its execution ledger, and Task 26 carries the ledger's rulings into engine.md.

### Resolved across tasks

1. **T5-R64 added.** Tasks 13 and 24 fail on CI where a tool is missing or FFmpeg is below 7.0, instead of printing `skipped:`, so a green run proves the cross-check and layer 2 ran. That narrows design 12.1 for CI, so it is a ruling the owner can overturn: Task 0 Step 1 names it with the other rulings that amend design text, and Tasks 0, 1 and 26 now say T5-R1 to T5-R65.
2. **The crate count and a second `miniz_oxide`.** Task 0 Step 4 now expects more than the notes' 15 to 25 transitive crates (phase 0's lock suggests 40 to 45), and says so to the owner rather than stopping. It also reads out a second `miniz_oxide` on the 0.9 line by name. Task 1's tripwire asserts one 0.8 copy, so a 0.9 copy is the owner's to accept with A1's second yes.
3. **FFmpeg on macos and windows.** Call 20 pins only ubuntu's static FFmpeg 7.x. Task 0 Step 6's sentence now tells the owner that macos and windows keep their package managers' FFmpeg, which the layer 2 tests check is at or above 7.0.
4. **`decisions.txt` lines are read in Task 0's and Task 1's forms.** Task 7 reads `A3 pins, <date>, <model> sha256 <hex>` with an exact `grep`. Tasks 7 and 24 take each value from the words before the line's first comma. Task 7 copies the licence text Task 0 already fetched (`.superpowers/pr5/CC-BY-SA-4.0.txt`) instead of downloading it again.
5. **`LAZYMKV_OCRS_MODELS` on CI.** Task 7 sets it once, at the `test` job's level, as the absolute `${{ github.workspace }}/.ocrs-models`. A relative path would not resolve, because cargo runs a build script in its package's folder. Task 1's interface line, Task 10's two `ocr-trial` steps and ruling T5-R41 now say so, and no step repeats the variable.

### Carried, by task

- **Task 0.** The `ocrs` feature expected is `onnx` alone, inferred from phase 0's `["onnx", "rten"]`; the index read decides. The CI tools' sources are the planner's choice: BtbN's dated autobuilds with `checksums.sha256`, the MKVToolNix Windows release folder and its checksum file, packages.ubuntu.com, formulae.brew.sh and creativecommons.org. A Windows release without a published checksum goes to the owner, and the installer is never downloaded to hash it. BtbN prunes old autobuilds, so a pinned URL may vanish later (owner item 27). The junction baseline's 13 ignored and 40 `skipped:` lines come from pull request 4's end; a different count is recorded, not a stop.
- **Task 1.** The `cargo tree -i rten` output when rten is outside a package's graph is either an error or a "nothing to print" warning, and both are accepted; a profile-spec warning on macos and windows is taken as harmless (unverified). The new workspace entries follow the `ureq` entry. `png` and `sha2`'s major and minor and the `ocrs` features are placeholders until Task 0 runs. The rten tripwire checks the two pins and that no `rten-*` name has two versions, not each `rten-*` version. A3 runs first (Step 1), over plain SSH only.
- **Task 2.** The three dev tests sit in `crates/dev/src/cmd/decide.rs`' `mod tests` (`--lib unread_stream`, 3 passed), beside the fixtures they use. A stream named unread that `subs/index.json` does not list is tagged `und`. `FactsSummary.text_streams` is empty while a title has an unread stream. A `summary.json` that does not parse skips the subtitles section and the decision. The expected compile errors are rustc's usual wording.
- **Task 3.** `MksBlock.cluster_ms` and `MksShape.timestamp_scale` exist so Review Focus 4's negative relative time and a non-default scale can be written. Several encodings undone highest order first and scope bit 2 are stated but not exercised. The hand-assembled file's byte count should be checked first if that test fails. The inflater needs `miniz_oxide`'s default `with-alloc` feature, which Task 1's `miniz_oxide = "0.8"` keeps.
- **Task 4.** The run-length rules are stricter than ffmpeg's (a short line or an overflowing run is an error). A real-disc quirk ffmpeg tolerates would show at Task 11 as a decode error and go to the owner. Clear display sets are never decoded, so a palette-only update under `sub_clear_max_bytes` is missed, as spec 8.7's event rule implies.
- **Task 5.** A line box's rows are the line's rows; the 16-pixel padding applies to the columns only, so a neighbouring line's ink stays out. Trigger 4's middle row is `video_height / 2`, and ink on it counts on neither side. The invented rules (the darker grey kept where objects overlap, a missing palette index transparent, pixels outside the frame clipped, the median of an even count the mean of the middle two) each have a test. The crop key's fixed answer was computed with Python on the Mac and not yet run in Rust; a Rust run that gives another key goes to the controller.
- **Task 6.** The record keys follow R6-phase0-17's order (`frame`, `file`, `t`, `pts`, `text`, `lines`, then the rest), not the skeleton's comment. `check_events` never compares a record's `pts` with ffprobe's `pts_time`; a tolerance for that would be the owner's. `chars` counts UTF-16 units, as phase 0's `String.Length` did.
- **Task 7.** `cargo-about`'s `about.toml` keys and template model, ureq 3.5.0's body-limit call, the `actions/cache` log wording and cargo's build-script failure line are written from documentation and checked at the first push. The notices job runs `cargo about generate` without `--locked`, which the plan cannot confirm the pinned version takes, and runs `git diff --exit-code Cargo.lock` in the same step after it, so a run that resolved the lock again fails. The `fail-on-cache-miss: true` restore makes a cache miss in a test job fail at once. A cache saved on the pull request's ref is not visible to `main`, so the merge misses once and downloads again; call 3's "once per cache miss" still holds. The CodeQL check can only find what its log shows (owner item 22).
- **Task 8.** `read_stream` takes the opened `SubStream` and the start `Instant`, so a codec, lacing or encoding refusal comes before the 12 MB (megabytes) of models load. `rten::Model::load_static_slice` over the embedded bytes is the one unverified interface: a refusal there is a stop that goes to the controller and the owner. ocrs gets RGB bytes, each grey value three times, as phase 0 gave it.
- **Task 9.** A kill outranks the exit code, exit 3 without a reason line is `Exited(Some(3))`, and exit 2 without a line gives `lazymkv-ocr refused its arguments`. The worker's lines reach no output callback. The run's wall time is `<capture>.exit.json`'s `elapsed_ms`, which Tasks 10 and 15 read. If the cap-kill test is ever flaky, the fix is more events, never a scaled bound.
- **Task 10.** The script reads each row's slug, label and stream from `trial-tracks.txt`; given values are checks only. `parity`'s "same side of every threshold" is pinned per measure to R6-phase0-35's bands. Two expectations are not certain: that changing one event to dialogue changes SO (an `assert_ne` guards it), and that the real ocrs over block shapes gives no text.
- **Task 11.** The goldens take a fourth variable, `LAZYMKV_OCR_STAGING`, for rows without a dataset copy of `evidence.mks` (R6-phase0-18, 20), and the script test is named for four variables. K1's byte figures and design 10.9's counts are checked by the controller against the printed log rather than hard-coded in `crates/` (RP21). The release build of rten on the mini PC carries call 4's retry, and `wait.sh` is run again while it exits 3.
- **Task 12.** `-Show 0` keeps `ocrs-trial.ps1` from printing subtitle text into a log that reaches the Mac. The restart uses `Start-ScheduledTask -TaskName lazymkv-engine` on pull request 4's build; Task 25 redeploys. Arm R runs the remaining rows after a kill, so the owner gets every number, and the six-track mean is total wall time over the 4,931 events.
- **Task 13.** `packets` runs with no time limit, since design 5.3's 120 s covers only the header calls. The mini PC's ffprobe path is `env.ps1`'s fallback, and a `skipped:` line there means the path is read again over plain SSH. The extraction uses `--gui-mode` and no `-q`, so progress reaches `ctx.on_progress`.
- **Task 14.** `step10::extract` takes a `log` for its `job.log` lines. The stand-in hands a matching group's later runs the next answer, so each test runs one extraction per job. `probe-summary.json` is written on a failed extraction too, as phase 0 does. That a restart with the staging root unreachable asks the staging reach for an `Inspecting` job is assumed, not verified.
- **Task 15.** The cap override comes from a scenario file `ocr-cap-s.txt` (whole seconds, times `ci_factor()`) that `Harness::new` reads; no setting holds it (T5-R58). With `sub_clear_max_bytes` 40, the text rule's events are asserted, not its reviews, since dev drops a text rule that differs from the default (RP15). The stand-in answers the two worker runs by run order. The cancel test asserts the state `Failed` with class Unknown, the message `cancelled by the owner` and the work folder's removal (R3-worker-16); the implementer keeps all three.
- **Task 16.** `net_fixed1`'s expected strings are predictions until Step 1 reads them on the mini PC. A printed `-0.0` switches Step 8 to the second sign rule, and any other mismatch goes to the owner (owner item 26). `manifest.txt` is written with CRLF and no BOM (byte order mark), where phase 0's `Set-Content` wrote a BOM; the readers accept both. `gains_tried` is always written, `[-18]` for a proxy kept at the first gain.
- **Task 17.** Copies into the job folder go through `staged::copy_into_job` (the source's bytes, their count checked, then `write_atomic`), so every engine-written job-folder file goes through `write_atomic` (R5-code-30); copies into staging and `tuning_root` stay `copy_checked`, whose `.partial` is now flushed before its size check (Task 14). T5-R38's `job.log` line for dataset-only lines is tested through `pass_lines` only, and R5-code-33 (the job's own settings) is pinned in code without a test. `step_10_reads_before_step_10a_decodes` assumes Task 15's two-subs title key `t00-00800` and the stand-in's stem `lazymkv-ocr`.
- **Task 18.** An absent staged folder also calls `clear_incomplete`, with no line, so a re-run never mixes old and new files. The torn move is built by hand between restarts. The retry trigger rests on pull request 4's `AwaitingLookup` round fetching a `Pending { Stale }` record again. If `decide.json` holds per-run values beyond the scratch root, the comparison is narrowed.
- **Task 19.** "Before another step" means before any job's step, so a filed job's pending copy is retried before the next restart; on an idle engine each cleanup pass retries it too (call 10's "when `tuning_root` answers"). A job none of whose titles has a staged tuning folder owes nothing (`CopyEnd::Nothing`, C2), so its copy never stays pending for good. The dataset gets the whole staged folder, `summary.json` included. The number of `retried` lines depends on timing, so the tests pin the first and last lines and one `copied` line. engine.md's lines 1170 and 1330 are left to Task 26.
- **Task 20.** A running refresh is joined at shutdown, so a stalled share can hold up shutdown for one job folder's copy. A `job.log` or `state.json` the owner rewrites during a refresh can fail that refresh's size check; it costs a `job.log` line and the next trigger copies again (accepted, not tested).
- **Task 21.** R4-commands-39's new usage text changes `retune_subtitles.rs`' `USAGE_LINE` and its command-table row test. That is the standard error usage line, not the report, so "single-folder output unchanged" still holds for the report. `worst(&[])` is 3 (D2's all-unlabelled run). T5-R40 applies to every run, not only several-folder ones.
- **Task 22.** `decide --job`'s `--text` uses the job's own settings' `tuning_root` (`CommandJob.tuning_root`), where Task 19 copied its dataset (ENG-19); `retune --jobs` uses the engine's current `tuning_root`. A relayed retune's refresh and Task 20's own refresh of the same folder could race on one `.partial`; this is not tested. `lazymkvctl` now places its absolute `--spec` at the first `--`, and Task 23 edits `USAGE` after this task.
- **Task 23.** `export_models` keeps the skeleton's `Result<(), String>`, so every error exits 2, a full disk included. In a release layout, design 11.4's `licenses\` folder may hold parts 1, 2 and 4 again; pull request 6 decides whether to filter it. `crates/ctl/crate-notices.txt` holds third-party licence texts and is exempt from the dash rule; Task 26's dash check reads only engine.md, the design and `README.md`.
- **Task 24.** The static archive is assumed to hold `bin/ffmpeg` and `bin/ffprobe` under its top folder. The real-tool expectations (mkvmerge keeping each PGS event's size through extraction, the `main-fc` level within 0.5 dB of -17.0, the series lengths, `-J`'s flags) are checked first on the mini PC in Step 4, and a failure goes to the controller or the owner, never to a loosened assertion.
- **Task 25.** R4-commands-8 and R5-code-91's "the notes" are read as engine.md. The rten build's peak memory goes into Step 5's evidence line, which Task 26 carries into "Pull request 5 on the mini PC". The replay's stand-in lives in `C:\lazymkv\dev\tools\pr5-replay\`. Its rip answer needs a `\rip\` needle. It relies on `copy_from` taking an absolute UNC (universal naming convention) path and on Task 15's `creates_first`. If pull request 4's job is not past its 7 days, C2's check records only the due date.
- **Task 26.** The mini PC evidence lines carry no task tag, so the controller maps each to its task by its stated form. Design part 7.5's sentence on where step 10a and the OCR write is amended for B1 (the worker's folder), which T5-R50 now lists.
